prompt

You have exactly three tools, each taking a single string:

  bash(command)   one shell command. A fresh shell every call, at /app.
                  Combined stdout+stderr comes back, truncated in the middle if very long.
  view_image(path) look at a PNG or JPEG in the box; you see the image itself.
  submit(notes)   you are done. Ends the task.

There is no network. Work iteratively and check your work as you go. The task ends when you call submit: there is
no one to report back to until then. Each of your replies is a step, and each turn ends with
how many steps and minutes are left: when either runs out, the task ends as it stands.

How your answer is graded: only /app/data/pktbuf.v and /app/data/pktbuf_egress.v, as you leave them, are read. Your submit notes are not.
Write /app/data/pktbuf.v as soon as you have an answer, and update it as you go; a run
that ends before it exists scores 0.

The line card's packet buffer, `pktbuf`, has to move to board rev C. Rev C replaces the buffer SRAM, NW61F1024, with the NW61P1024 on the same footprint and pins. ECR-0412 is approved: make the RTL change so that `pktbuf` works on rev C boards as they are built.

Everything is in `/app/data`:

- `pktbuf.v`, `pktbuf_egress.v`: the design as it runs on rev B today.
- `docs/pktbuf_spec.md`: the block specification.
- `docs/ECR-0412_pktbuf_rev_c.md`: the change request.
- `docs/NW61F1024_excerpt.md`, `docs/NW61P1024_excerpt.md`: the old and the new SRAM.
- `docs/board_rev_c_notes.md`: rev C board notes.
- `docs/ila_sram_sn0007.csv`: a capture of the SRAM ports from rev C bring-up, described in the board notes.
- `tb/tb_smoke.v` and `Makefile`: a smoke test with a model of the rev B SRAM. `make -s -C /app/data` runs it on Icarus Verilog, `make -s -C /app/data verilator` on Verilator. It passes on the design as handed over. It is not graded and you may change it.

What is graded is `/app/data/pktbuf.v` and `/app/data/pktbuf_egress.v` as you leave them. Only these two files are compiled, so every module the design uses must be in them. Keep the top module `pktbuf` with its name, ports and parameters unchanged; the modules under it are yours to change.

The grader runs withheld testbenches against a model of the rev C SRAM, with random traffic and backpressure, at several `DW`/`AW` settings. It checks the behaviour and performance in the specification as amended by the ECR. Each testbench runs once on Icarus Verilog 13 (`iverilog -g2012`) and 16 times on Verilator 5.048 (`--binary --timing --x-initial unique --x-assign unique`, `+verilator+rand+reset+2`), each time with a new stimulus seed and new random power-up values for every flop and memory. A check passes only if it passes in every run.

Before any testbench runs, the two files must pass these rules, or the score is 0:

- synthesizable RTL that elaborates on its own at every graded `DW`/`AW`;
- no `initial` blocks, delays, `force`/`release`, `defparam`, `bind`, `import`/`export`, `wait`, `fork`, `forever`, `while`, `event` or `->`, escaped identifiers, hierarchical names or user-defined primitives;
- no system tasks or functions except `$clog2`, `$signed` and `$unsigned`, and no compiler directives except `` `timescale `` and `` `default_nettype ``;
- every event control is `@*` or a list of `posedge`/`negedge` edges, and opens an `always` block;
- no register given a value where it is declared;
- parameter overrides on instances by name only, as in `#(.DW(DW))`.

cat /app/data/docs/pktbuf_spec.md

# pktbuf: packet buffer, block specification

Revision 1.4. Applies to `pktbuf.v` and `pktbuf_egress.v`.

## 1. Purpose

`pktbuf` sits between the line-side receive stream and the switch interface. It stores whole packets, or forwards them as they arrive, using an external synchronous SRAM as the buffer memory. One SRAM holds the words of all packets in a ring, in arrival order.

## 2. Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Supported |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DW` | Data width of both streams and of the SRAM word | 8 to 32 |
| `AW` | SRAM address width; the buffer holds 2**`AW` words | 6 to 12 |

The line card uses `DW = 32`, `AW = 10`. Other boards use other values; the block must work for every supported combination.

## 3. Ports

| Port | Dir | Width | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clk` | in | 1 | Clock. The SRAM is clocked from the same clock. |
| `rst_n` | in | 1 | Reset, active low, asserted asynchronously, released synchronously to `clk`. |
| `cfg_cut_through` | in | 1 | 0: store-and-forward. 1: cut-through. Static, see 5.4. |
| `in_valid` | in | 1 | Ingress beat valid. |
| `in_ready` | out | 1 | Ingress beat accepted at this edge if `in_valid` is also high. |
| `in_data` | in | `DW` | Ingress data. |
| `in_last` | in | 1 | Last beat of a packet. |
| `in_err` | in | 1 | Packet error. Only meaningful with `in_last`; ignored on other beats. |
| `out_valid` | out | 1 | Egress beat valid. |
| `out_ready` | in | 1 | Egress beat taken at this edge if `out_valid` is also high. |
| `out_data` | out | `DW` | Egress data. |
| `out_last` | out | 1 | Last beat of a packet. |
| `out_err` | out | 1 | Packet error, on the last beat only (cut-through mode). |
| `out_retry` | in | 1 | Retry request from the switch. Sampled only at the edge that moves the last beat of a packet; ignored at every other edge. See 5.5. |
| `drop_count` | out | 16 | Packets dropped since reset, wraps at 2**16. |
| `sram_ce_n` | out | 1 | SRAM chip enable, active low. A command is issued in each cycle with `sram_ce_n` low. |
| `sram_we_n` | out | 1 | SRAM write enable, active low: low for a write command, high for a read command. |
| `sram_addr` | out | `AW` | SRAM word address. |
| `sram_wdata` | out | `DW` | SRAM write data (to the SRAM's D inputs). |
| `sram_rdata` | in | `DW` | SRAM read data (from the SRAM's Q outputs). |

All `sram_*` outputs are driven from flops. The ports connect straight to the SRAM pins: the board and the FPGA I/O add no register stages. When the SRAM samples the pins and when it returns read data depend on the SRAM part; see the board's SRAM datasheet.

## 4. Streams

Both streams use valid/ready. A beat moves at a rising edge of `clk` at which valid and ready are both high. Once valid is high, the sender holds the beat (data, last, err) unchanged until it moves. `in_ready` may change at any time; a sender does not wait for `in_ready` before raising `in_valid`.

A packet is 1 or more beats, the last with `in_last` high. In store-and-forward mode a packet is at most 2**`AW` beats. In cut-through mode there is no limit.

## 5. Behaviour

### 5.1 Reset

While `rst_n` is low and after it is released: `out_valid` is low, `drop_count` is 0, and no SRAM command is issued (`sram_ce_n` high) until there is a beat to write. `in_ready` is high no later than 4 cycles after release.

### 5.2 Store-and-forward (`cfg_cut_through` = 0)

A packet is sent on the egress stream only after its last beat has been received. A packet whose last beat has `in_err` high is dropped: none of its beats is sent, and `drop_count` increments by one. Packets leave in the order they arrived. `out_err` is always 0.

### 5.3 Cut-through (`cfg_cut_through` = 1)

A packet may start on the egress stream as soon as its first beat has been stored. No packet is dropped and `drop_count` does not change. `out_err` is high on the last beat of a packet whose last ingress beat had `in_err` high, and low on every other beat.

### 5.4 Changing mode

`cfg_cut_through` may change only while the block is empty (every accepted beat has been sent or dropped) and no ingress beat has been accepted for at least 8 cycles. After a change, no ingress beat is offered for at least 8 cycles.

### 5.5 Retry (store-and-forward)

In store-and-forward mode the switch can refuse a packet at its end. If `out_retry` is high at the edge that moves the last beat of a packet, the block sends the same packet again, complete and unchanged, before any other packet. The resent packet can be refused again in the same way, any number of times. If `out_retry` is low at that edge, the packet is released. In cut-through mode `out_retry` is ignored.

### 5.6 Capacity and flow control

The buffer holds up to 2**`AW` words and up to 8 packets whose last beat has been received but which have not yet been released (store-and-forward) or completely read from the SRAM (cut-through). `in_ready` is low while either limit is reached. In store-and-forward mode a packet's words are kept until the packet is released. A word's location is free again once the block no longer needs it.

### 5.7 SRAM use

The SRAM takes one command per cycle. How the ingress and egress sides share it is up to the design, within the requirements of section 6. (The rev B design lets them take turns.) Once the block is empty (every accepted beat has been sent or dropped) and no beat is being received, it issues no SRAM command.

## 6. Performance

### 6.1 Ingress

While the buffer has room and the egress side is not reading, one beat is accepted per cycle.

### 6.2 Egress

While `out_ready` is high and the SRAM is not needed by the ingress side, one beat per cycle is sent, with no gaps, until the stored words run out.

### 6.3 Line rate

In store-and-forward mode, with the block empty, a packet of up to 32 beats whose beats are all offered back to back is accepted at one beat per cycle. If `out_ready` is held high and nothing else arrives, the first egress beat moves no later than 4 cycles after the edge that took the last ingress beat, and the remaining beats follow at one per cycle with no gaps.

### 6.4 Cut-through first beat

In cut-through mode, when the block is empty (every accepted beat has been sent) and `out_ready` is high, the first beat of a packet moves on the egress stream no later than 5 cycles after the edge that took it at the ingress. This is the switch's arbitration budget for cut-through packets.

## 7. Implementation notes

- The design must be synthesizable RTL. Everything below the top level is in `pktbuf.v` and `pktbuf_egress.v`.
- No initial blocks, delays, system tasks other than `$clog2`, `$signed` and `$unsigned`, and no compiler directives other than `` `timescale `` and `` `default_nettype ``. Parameter overrides on instances are by name.
- Every flop that affects behaviour is reset; the block must behave the same whatever the power-up state of its flops and memories.

cat /app/data/docs/ECR-0412_pktbuf_rev_c.md

# ECR-0412: pktbuf on board rev C

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Status | Approved |
| Affects | `pktbuf.v`, `pktbuf_egress.v` (line card FPGA) |
| Board | Line card rev C |

## Reason

The buffer SRAM on rev B, NW61F1024, is end of life. Rev C fits the NW61P1024 in its place. The footprint and the signals between FPGA and SRAM are the same: CE#, WE#, A[9:0], D[31:0] (write data) and Q[31:0] (read data). The NW61P1024 is a pipelined part with late write, so its timing differs. See `NW61F1024_excerpt.md`, `NW61P1024_excerpt.md` and `board_rev_c_notes.md`.

## Change

1. `pktbuf` works with the NW61P1024 as fitted and strapped on rev C boards. Rev B support is not needed. The other boards that use `pktbuf` with other `DW`/`AW` move to NW61P-family parts of the matching organisation, wired and strapped as on rev C, so the same SRAM timing applies at every `DW`/`AW`.
2. The top-level module name, ports and parameters stay as they are. The FPGA top level is not changed.
3. Behaviour stays as in `pktbuf_spec.md` for every supported `DW` and `AW`, in both modes, under any backpressure, with one exception: the line-rate limit in section 6.3 becomes **10 cycles** from the edge that took the last ingress beat to the edge that takes the first egress beat (was 4). Everything else in section 6 is unchanged: the ingress rate in 6.1, the gap-free requirements in 6.2 and 6.3, and the cut-through first-beat latency in 6.4, which is fixed by the switch.
4. All logic stays in `pktbuf.v` and `pktbuf_egress.v`.

## Verification

The block regression is being moved to a rev C SRAM model and will be run on the changed RTL at several `DW`/`AW` settings, on Icarus Verilog and on Verilator with random power-up state. The smoke test in `tb/` models the rev B part and is not part of the sign-off.

# NW61F1024: 1K x 32 synchronous SRAM, flow-through, separate I/O

Datasheet excerpt (functional description and timing summary). Rev 2.1.

## Description

The NW61F1024 is a 32 768-bit synchronous static RAM organised as 1024 words of 32 bits, with separate data inputs (D) and data outputs (Q). All inputs are registered at the rising edge of CLK. Reads are flow-through: the addressed word appears on Q in the same cycle, after the clock edge that sampled the read command.

## Pins

| Pin | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLK | in | Clock. All inputs are sampled at its rising edge. |
| CE# | in | Chip enable, active low. High: no operation (deselect). |
| WE# | in | Write enable, active low. Low with CE# low: write. High with CE# low: read. |
| A[9:0] | in | Word address. |
| D[31:0] | in | Write data. |
| Q[31:0] | out | Read data. Driven at all times; undefined except in the read data cycle. |

## Operation

Edge *n* is the rising edge of CLK at which CE# is sampled low.

| Command at edge *n* | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Deselect (CE# high) | No operation. |
| Read (WE# high) | A is sampled at edge *n*. The word is on Q after edge *n* and is captured by the controller at edge *n*+1. |
| Write (WE# low) | A and D are sampled at edge *n*. The word is written at edge *n*. |

A read at edge *n*+1 of the address written at edge *n* returns the new data. Any sequence of reads and writes may be issued, one per cycle.

## Timing summary

| Parameter | Min | Max | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clock frequency | | 133 | MHz |
| Read latency (command edge to capture edge) | 1 | 1 | cycle |

# NW61P1024: 1K x 32 synchronous SRAM, pipelined, late write, separate I/O

Datasheet excerpt (functional description and timing summary). Rev 1.4.

## Description

The NW61P1024 is a 32 768-bit synchronous static RAM organised as 1024 words of 32 bits, with separate data inputs (D) and data outputs (Q). It is pin-compatible with the NW61F1024. All inputs are registered at the rising edge of CLK. Reads go through an output pipeline whose depth is set by the LAT pin. Writes use late write: the write data follows the write command by one cycle, so reads and writes can be mixed at one command per cycle without dead cycles.

## Pins

| Pin | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLK | in | Clock. All inputs are sampled at its rising edge. |
| CE# | in | Chip enable, active low. High: no operation (deselect). |
| WE# | in | Write enable, active low. Low with CE# low: write. High with CE# low: read. |
| A[9:0] | in | Word address. |
| D[31:0] | in | Write data, sampled one cycle after the write command (late write). |
| Q[31:0] | out | Read data. Driven at all times; undefined except in the read data cycle. |
| LAT | in | Read latency select, static (strap). See below. Must not change while CLK runs. |

## Read latency

| LAT | Read latency RL (command edge to capture edge) | Clock frequency, max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L | 2 cycles | 100 MHz |
| H | 3 cycles | 166 MHz |

## Operation

Edge *n* is the rising edge of CLK at which a command is sampled.

| Command at edge *n* | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Deselect (CE# high) | No operation. |
| Read (WE# high) | A is sampled at edge *n* and the word is read from the array at edge *n*. It is on Q in the cycle before edge *n*+RL and is captured by the controller at edge *n*+RL. Q holds it for that one cycle only. |
| Write (WE# low) | A is sampled at edge *n*. D is sampled at edge *n*+1, whatever command is issued at edge *n*+1. |

Any sequence of reads, writes and deselects may be issued, one command per cycle. No dead cycle is needed between a read and a write in either order.

## Timing summary

| Parameter | Symbol | Min | Max | Unit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clock cycle time, LAT = L | tCYC | 10.0 | | ns | |
| Clock cycle time, LAT = H | tCYC | 6.0 | | ns | |
| Write data after write command | tWD | 1 | 1 | cycle | |
| Read latency | RL | 2 / 3 | 2 / 3 | cycle | set by LAT |

# Line card rev C: hardware notes for FPGA designers

Extract of the rev C design notes. Items that do not concern the packet buffer are left out.

## Clocks

| Net | Frequency | Source | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLK_CORE | 125.00 MHz | PLL1 out 0 | FPGA core, `pktbuf` `clk` |
| SRAM_CLK | 125.00 MHz | PLL1 out 1, phase aligned to CLK_CORE | U12 CLK |

## Buffer SRAM (U12)

U12 is the NW61P1024 (rev B: NW61F1024). Pins as on rev B:

| FPGA signal | U12 pin |
| --- | --- |
| `sram_ce_n` | CE# |
| `sram_we_n` | WE# |
| `sram_addr[9:0]` | A[9:0] |
| `sram_wdata[31:0]` | D[31:0] |
| `sram_rdata[31:0]` | Q[31:0] |

The `pktbuf` SRAM ports connect straight to the FPGA pins; the FPGA I/O has no input or output registers on these signals. Board delays are within one cycle at 125 MHz, so the edges in the U12 datasheet are `pktbuf` clock edges.

### Straps (schematic rev C, sheet 7, as released 2026-06-10)

| Pin | Network | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U12 LAT | R40 10k to GND fitted, R41 10k to VDDQ not fitted | L |

## Bring-up log (excerpt)

| Date | Board | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-08-19 | SN 0003 | FPGA configures, PLL1 locks. SRAM read/write with the rev B `pktbuf` fails as expected (rev B timing). |
| 2026-08-21 | SN 0007 | SRAM march test from the debug core at 125 MHz: 0.3 % read errors, random bits, all addresses. Same test at 100 MHz passes. |
| 2026-08-28 | SN 0007 | Errors traced to the LAT strap: 125 MHz is above the LAT = L limit in the U12 datasheet. |
| 2026-09-02 | all | ECO-117 released: on every rev C board, R40 removed and R41 fitted. March test at 125 MHz passes on SN 0003, 0007, 0011. Schematic to be updated at rev D. |
| 2026-09-03 | SN 0007 | SRAM exerciser v0.3 from the debug core at 125 MHz, driving the `pktbuf` SRAM ports. ILA capture of those ports in `ila_sram_sn0007.csv`, one row per clock edge (the values at that edge). Steps: 1 write 0x000–0x00F with pattern A; 2 read 0x000–0x00F back; 3 write 0x000–0x00F with pattern B; 4 for k = 0 to 4 idle cycles, write three addresses with pattern C, each followed by k idle cycles and a read of the same address. Steps 1–3 compare OK. Step 4 has no compare yet; capture kept for review. |

So the key finding: read of an address written earlier returns NEW data only if there are ≥2 idle cycles between the write command and the read command (i.e., read command at edge ≥ n+3 where write command at edge n). With read at n+1 or n+2, the read returns OLD data.

Why? Late write: D sampled at edge n+1. The write data is then written to the array... apparently at edge n+2 (one cycle after D is sampled — internal write pipeline). A read at edge n+2 reads the array at edge n+2 — does it see the write happening at the same edge? Apparently not: read at n+2 returns old data, so the write commits after the read at the same edge, or the write commits between edge n+2 and n+3. So effective: a read at edge m returns new data for a write commanded at edge n iff m ≥ n+3.

Hmm wait, but also consider a read at n+1 where the data is being sampled at that same edge — old. Read at n+2 — old. Read at n+3 — new. So the write-to-array commit point is such that reads at edges ≤ n+2 see old, reads at ≥ n+3 see new.

This matters a lot for the RTL: the controller must not read a location sooner than 3 cycles after the write command, OR must bypass (forward) data. Actually with RL=3 and a read latency of 3 cycles, if we write at edge n and want to read, the earliest read command that returns correct data is at edge n+3, data captured at n+6.

But wait — there's a subtlety: the packet buffer reads packets after they're written. In cut-through, the first beat may be read shortly after write. The rev B design (flow-through, RL=1, write at edge n visible to read at n+1) presumably handled this.

Also important: the graded testbench uses "a model of the rev C SRAM". The model presumably implements: RL=3 (LAT=H per ECO-117), late write with D sampled one cycle after command, and read-during-write behavior matching the ILA: reads within 2 cycles of the write command to the same address return old data; reads at ≥3 cycles return new data. Possibly the model is simpler: write commits at edge n+2 (data sampled at n+1, written to array at n+2? but then read at n+2 would be ambiguous). Hmm.

Let me think about how the model likely works:
- At each edge: if CE#=0 and WE#=0: schedule write: addr captured; data captured at next edge; array written... at edge n+2? If array written at edge n+2 at the same sampling moment as a read at n+2, order matters. The observed behavior: read at n+2 → old. So in the model, the array write at edge n+2 happens after the read sample at n+2, or the read at n+2 uses the value before the write. Simplest model consistent: at each edge, first process reads (sample array), then process pending writes. I.e., writes commanded at n take effect in the array at edge n+2, after reads at edge n+2 are sampled. Equivalently: read at edge m sees writes commanded at edges ≤ m-3.

Actually another possible model: writes sampled D at n+1, array written at n+2 nonblocking, reads sample at the edge with current (pre-write) value — same result: read at n+2 sees old. Or array written at n+3 before read: read at n+3 sees new. All consistent: read at edge m sees writes from commands at edges ≤ m−3.

To be safe, the RTL should ensure it never reads an address within 3 cycles of writing it (command edges), or use bypass forwarding. But there's another subtlety: what about two writes to the same address? In a ring buffer, addresses are written once per packet-slot usage, so no issue.

Now, the design: we need to rewrite pktbuf to work with RL=3, late write. Let me look at the current design.

cat /app/data/pktbuf.v

// pktbuf.v
//
// Packet buffer between the line-side receive stream and the switch
// interface. Packets arrive on a valid/ready stream, are stored in an
// external synchronous SRAM, and leave on a second valid/ready stream.
// The block behaviour is specified in docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// Written for board rev B, where the SRAM is the NW61F1024 flow-through
// part (docs/NW61F1024_excerpt.md).
//
// This file holds the top level: ingress, the packet descriptor queue,
// buffer space and retry bookkeeping, the SRAM command arbiter and the
// SRAM pins. The read pipeline and the output queue are in
// pktbuf_egress.v.

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,          // data width, also the SRAM word width
    parameter AW = 10           // SRAM address width, 2**AW words
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,           // asynchronous assert, active low

    input  wire          cfg_cut_through, // 0 store-and-forward, 1 cut-through

    // ingress stream
    input  wire          in_valid,
    output wire          in_ready,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] in_data,
    input  wire          in_last,
    input  wire          in_err,          // sampled with in_last only

    // egress stream
    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry,       // sampled with the last beat only

    // status
    output wire [15:0]   drop_count,

    // external SRAM, all outputs driven from flops
    output reg           sram_ce_n,
    output reg           sram_we_n,
    output reg  [AW-1:0] sram_addr,
    output reg  [DW-1:0] sram_wdata,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata
);

    localparam ND  = 8;                         // packet descriptor slots
    localparam NDW = 3;                         // log2(ND)
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}}; // 2**AW words

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Ingress
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg  [AW:0]    wr_ptr;      // address of the next word to write
    reg  [AW:0]    pkt_start;   // first address of the packet being received
    reg  [15:0]    drop_cnt;

    // Packet descriptor queue: the address of each packet's last word and
    // its error flag. In store-and-forward mode an entry means "this packet
    // is complete". In cut-through mode it only marks where a packet ends.
    // Three free-running pointers (one bit wider than the index):
    //   desc_wp    next entry to write
    //   desc_rp    next packet to read from the SRAM
    //   desc_keep  oldest packet not yet released (store-and-forward: the
    //              packet on the egress stream, which may still be retried)
    reg  [AW-1:0]  desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg            desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_rp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_cnt  = desc_wp - desc_rp;     // complete, not yet read
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;   // complete, not yet released

    // Buffer space. Cut-through: a word is free once it has been read.
    // Store-and-forward: a packet's words stay until the packet is released,
    // so that it can be sent again; free_ptr is the first word still held.
    reg  [AW:0]    free_ptr;

    wire [AW:0]    rd_ptr;      // address of the next word to read (egress)
    wire           rd_want;     // egress asks for a read command this cycle
    wire           rd_go;       // ... and gets it
    wire           wr_go;       // an ingress beat is written this cycle
    reg            rr_rd;       // the read wins the next conflict
    wire           pkt_release; // egress: a packet's last beat moved, no retry
    wire           pkt_retry;   // egress: a packet's last beat moved with retry

    wire [AW:0]    used       = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire           can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    // One SRAM command per cycle. When ingress and egress both want the
    // SRAM, they take turns.
    assign in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd);
    assign wr_go    = in_valid && in_ready;
    assign rd_go    = rd_want && !wr_go;

    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
    wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;
    wire pkt_pop;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_ptr    <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            pkt_start <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            drop_cnt  <= 16'd0;
            rr_rd     <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (pkt_drop) begin
                wr_ptr   <= pkt_start;          // forget the whole packet
                drop_cnt <= drop_cnt + 16'd1;
            end else if (wr_go) begin
                wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
                if (in_last)
                    pkt_start <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
            end

            if (wr_go && rd_want)
                rr_rd <= 1'b1;
            else if (rd_go && in_valid && can_accept)
                rr_rd <= 1'b0;
        end
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Descriptor queue, release and retry
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (pkt_push) begin
            desc_end[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            desc_err[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= in_err;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            desc_wp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_rp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_keep <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            free_ptr  <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (pkt_push)
                desc_wp <= desc_wp + 1'b1;

            if (pkt_retry)
                desc_rp <= desc_keep;           // read the packet again
            else if (pkt_pop)
                desc_rp <= desc_rp + 1'b1;

            if (cfg_cut_through) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_rp;
                free_ptr  <= rd_ptr;
            end else if (pkt_release) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_keep + 1'b1;
                free_ptr  <= free_ptr + {1'b0, desc_end[desc_keep[NDW-1:0]] - free_ptr[AW-1:0]} + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    // What the egress may read next.
    wire head_valid = (desc_cnt != 0);
    wire rd_last    = head_valid && (rd_ptr[AW-1:0] == desc_end[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]]);
    wire rd_err     = desc_err[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]];

    // Store-and-forward: only words of complete packets.
    // Cut-through: any word already written.
    wire rd_avail   = cfg_cut_through ? (rd_ptr != wr_ptr) : head_valid;

    assign pkt_pop  = rd_go && rd_last;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // SRAM pins
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            sram_ce_n <= 1'b1;
            sram_we_n <= 1'b1;
        end else begin
            sram_ce_n <= !(wr_go || rd_go);
            sram_we_n <= !wr_go;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go) begin
            sram_addr  <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            sram_wdata <= in_data;
        end else if (rd_go) begin
            sram_addr  <= rd_ptr[AW-1:0];
        end
    end

    assign drop_count = drop_cnt;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Egress
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    pktbuf_egress #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) u_egress (
        .clk         (clk),
        .rst_n       (rst_n),
        .retry_en    (!cfg_cut_through),
        .rd_avail    (rd_avail),
        .rd_last     (rd_last),
        .rd_err      (rd_err),
        .rd_go       (rd_go),
        .rd_want     (rd_want),
        .rd_ptr      (rd_ptr),
        .rd_restart  (free_ptr),
        .pkt_release (pkt_release),
        .pkt_retry   (pkt_retry),
        .sram_rdata  (sram_rdata),
        .out_valid   (out_valid),
        .out_ready   (out_ready),
        .out_data    (out_data),
        .out_last    (out_last),
        .out_err     (out_err),
        .out_retry   (out_retry)
    );

endmodule

cat /app/data/pktbuf_egress.v

// pktbuf_egress.v
//
// Egress half of pktbuf: issues SRAM reads in address order, follows each
// read through the SRAM, queues the returned words for the egress stream,
// and handles a retry request at the end of a packet. See
// docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// Written for board rev B (NW61F1024, flow-through).

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf_egress #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,

    input  wire          retry_en,    // store-and-forward: out_retry is honoured
    input  wire          rd_avail,    // the word at rd_ptr may be read
    input  wire          rd_last,     // ... and is the last of its packet
    input  wire          rd_err,      // ... and that packet had in_err
    input  wire          rd_go,       // the arbiter issues the read this cycle
    output wire          rd_want,
    output reg  [AW:0]   rd_ptr,
    input  wire [AW:0]   rd_restart,  // first word of the packet on the egress stream
    output wire          pkt_release, // a last beat moved, packet done
    output wire          pkt_retry,   // a last beat moved with out_retry: send it again

    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,

    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry
);

    localparam QD = 4;      // output queue entries
    localparam QW = 2;      // log2(QD)

    // Read pipeline, NW61F flow-through:
    //   rd_p0  the read command is on the SRAM pins
    //   rd_p1  the SRAM sampled it at this edge; its data is on sram_rdata
    //          and is captured at the next edge
    reg rd_p0, rd_p1;
    reg tag_last0, tag_last1;
    reg tag_err0,  tag_err1;

    reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_last [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_err  [0:QD-1];
    reg [QW-1:0] q_wp;
    reg [QW-1:0] q_rp;
    reg [QW:0]   q_cnt;

    wire [QW:0] in_flight = {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p0} + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p1};
    wire        q_push    = rd_p1;
    wire        q_pop     = out_valid && out_ready;

    // End of a packet on the egress stream. A retry throws away everything
    // read ahead (queued words and reads in flight) and starts reading the
    // same packet again from its first word.
    wire        last_out  = q_pop && out_last;
    assign pkt_retry   = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
    assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

    // Ask for a read only when its data is sure to find a free entry.
    assign rd_want = rd_avail && ((q_cnt + in_flight) < QD);

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            rd_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            rd_ptr <= rd_restart;
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (rd_go)
                rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1'b1;
            rd_p0 <= rd_go;
            rd_p1 <= rd_p0;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        tag_last0 <= rd_last;
        tag_err0  <= rd_err;
        tag_last1 <= tag_last0;
        tag_err1  <= tag_err0;
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (q_push) begin
            q_data[q_wp] <= sram_rdata;
            q_last[q_wp] <= tag_last1;
            q_err[q_wp]  <= tag_err1 && tag_last1;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            q_wp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_rp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            q_rp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_wp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (q_push)
                q_wp <= q_wp + 1'b1;
            if (q_pop)
                q_rp <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            case ({q_push, q_pop})
                2'b10:   q_cnt <= q_cnt + 1'b1;
                2'b01:   q_cnt <= q_cnt - 1'b1;
                default: q_cnt <= q_cnt;
            endcase
        end
    end

    assign out_valid = (q_cnt != 0);
    assign out_data  = q_data[q_rp];
    assign out_last  = q_last[q_rp];
    assign out_err   = q_err[q_rp];

endmodule

`timescale 1ns/1ps
// Smoke test for pktbuf on board rev B (NW61F1024 flow-through SRAM).
//
// Sends a few packets in store-and-forward mode, then a few in cut-through
// mode, and checks that they come out unchanged. It is a quick sanity check,
// not a regression: no backpressure, no dropped packets, nothing else.
//
// The SRAM model follows docs/NW61F1024_excerpt.md: command, address and
// write data are sampled at the same rising edge; read data is captured by
// the FPGA at the next rising edge.
module tb_smoke;
    localparam DW = 32;
    localparam AW = 10;

    reg clk = 1'b0;
    always #5 clk = ~clk;

    reg           rst_n     = 1'b0;
    reg           cfg_ct    = 1'b0;
    reg           in_valid  = 1'b0;
    reg  [DW-1:0] in_data   = {DW{1'b0}};
    reg           in_last   = 1'b0;
    reg           in_err    = 1'b0;
    reg           out_ready = 1'b1;
    reg           out_retry = 1'b0;
    wire          in_ready, out_valid, out_last, out_err;
    wire [DW-1:0] out_data;
    wire [15:0]   drop_count;
    wire          sram_ce_n, sram_we_n;
    wire [AW-1:0] sram_addr;
    wire [DW-1:0] sram_wdata;
    reg  [DW-1:0] sram_rdata;

    pktbuf #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) dut (
        .clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .cfg_cut_through(cfg_ct),
        .in_valid(in_valid), .in_ready(in_ready), .in_data(in_data),
        .in_last(in_last), .in_err(in_err),
        .out_valid(out_valid), .out_ready(out_ready), .out_data(out_data),
        .out_last(out_last), .out_err(out_err), .out_retry(out_retry),
        .drop_count(drop_count),
        .sram_ce_n(sram_ce_n), .sram_we_n(sram_we_n), .sram_addr(sram_addr),
        .sram_wdata(sram_wdata), .sram_rdata(sram_rdata)
    );

    // NW61F1024 model
    reg [DW-1:0] mem [0:(1<<AW)-1];
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b0)
            mem[sram_addr] <= sram_wdata;
        if (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b1)
            sram_rdata <= mem[sram_addr];
        else
            sram_rdata <= 32'hDEADBEEF;
    end

    // expected beats, in order
    reg [DW-1:0] exp_d [0:1023];
    reg          exp_l [0:1023];
    integer      n_in, n_out, errors, i, p, len;

    // count what comes out
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst_n && out_valid && out_ready) begin
            if (out_data !== exp_d[n_out] || out_last !== exp_l[n_out] || out_err !== 1'b0) begin
                if (errors < 5)
                    $display("smoke: beat %0d: got %h last %b err %b, expected %h last %b",
                             n_out, out_data, out_last, out_err, exp_d[n_out], exp_l[n_out]);
                errors = errors + 1;
            end
            n_out = n_out + 1;
        end
    end

    task send_packet(input integer n);
        integer b;
        begin
            for (b = 0; b < n; b = b + 1) begin
                @(negedge clk);
                in_valid = 1'b1;
                in_data  = {p[7:0], b[7:0], 16'hA5C3} ^ (b * 32'h01000193);
                in_last  = (b == n - 1);
                exp_d[n_in] = in_data;
                exp_l[n_in] = in_last;
                n_in = n_in + 1;
                #1;
                while (in_ready !== 1'b1) begin
                    @(negedge clk);
                    #1;
                end
                @(posedge clk);              // the beat is taken at this edge
            end
            @(negedge clk);
            in_valid = 1'b0;
            in_last  = 1'b0;
        end
    endtask

    task wait_drain;
        integer t;
        begin
            t = 0;
            while (n_out < n_in && t < 2000) begin
                @(posedge clk);
                t = t + 1;
            end
        end
    endtask

    initial begin
        n_in = 0; n_out = 0; errors = 0;
        repeat (4) @(negedge clk);
        rst_n = 1'b1;
        repeat (4) @(negedge clk);

        cfg_ct = 1'b0;                       // store-and-forward
        for (p = 0; p < 6; p = p + 1) begin
            len = 5 + (p * 3) % 8;
            send_packet(len);
        end
        wait_drain;
        repeat (10) @(negedge clk);

        cfg_ct = 1'b1;                       // cut-through
        repeat (10) @(negedge clk);
        for (p = 6; p < 12; p = p + 1) begin
            len = 4 + (p * 5) % 9;
            send_packet(len);
        end
        wait_drain;
        repeat (10) @(negedge clk);

        if (n_out != n_in)
            $display("smoke: %0d beats sent, %0d received", n_in, n_out);
        if (errors == 0 && n_out == n_in && drop_count == 16'd0)
            $display("SMOKE PASS: %0d packets, %0d beats", p, n_in);
        else
            $display("SMOKE FAIL: %0d mismatches", errors);
        $finish;
    end

endmodule

reasoning

Let me understand the task in detail.

**Rev B SRAM (NW61F1024):** flow-through
- Read command at edge n: address sampled at edge n, data on Q after edge n, captured by controller at edge n+1. So read latency = 1 cycle.
- Write command at edge n: address and data sampled at edge n; written at edge n.

**Rev C SRAM (NW61P1024):** pipelined with late write
- Read command at edge n: address sampled at edge n, word read at edge n, on Q in the cycle before edge n+RL, captured at edge n+RL. RL = 2 (LAT=L) or 3 (LAT=H).
- Write command at edge n: address sampled at edge n; data (D) sampled at edge n+1. So the write data must be driven on D during the cycle *after* the write command.

The board notes say: rev C boards as originally released had LAT strapped L (R40 fitted to GND), but ECO-117 changed it: R40 removed, R41 fitted → LAT = H. So **LAT = H → RL = 3 cycles**.

Let me double check: "Straps (schematic rev C, sheet 7, as released 2026-06-10): U12 LAT: R40 10k to GND fitted, R41 not fitted → L". Then ECO-117: "on every rev C board, R40 removed and R41 fitted" → LAT = H. The ECR says "make the RTL change so that pktbuf works on rev C boards **as they are built**". As they are built = with ECO-117 applied → LAT=H → RL=3.

The ILA capture confirms the timing. Let me analyze it to make sure RL=3 and late-write confirmed:

Step 1: write 0x000-0x00F with pattern A (c0de0000..c0de000f). Cycles 4-19: ce_n=0, we_n=0, addr 000..00f, but note the wdata: at cycle 4 (write command for addr 000), wdata=00000000. At cycle 5 (write command for addr 001), wdata=c0de0000. So indeed the write data appears one cycle after the write command — late write confirmed. The exerciser drives D one cycle after each write command.

"Late write" — the datasheet doesn't say exactly when the write lands in the array, just that D is sampled at edge n+1. The read at edge 69 reads the array at edge 69. This is a read-during-write hazard: with late write, the write lands in the array at edge n+1 (or later), so a read at edge n+1 sees old data.

  - 84: W 002; 85: R 002 (D=f00d0002); data @88 = 5eed0022 (old)

**Existing design understanding:**

Ingress:
- `wr_ptr` (AW+1 bits): next word address to write. The low AW bits go to the SRAM.
- `pkt_start`: first address of the packet currently being received.
- On a beat with `in_last && in_err` (S&F): drop — wr_ptr rewinds to pkt_start, drop_cnt++.
- On `in_last && !err`: push descriptor (end address = wr_ptr, err flag) at desc_wp.

Descriptor queue: ND=8 entries. desc_wp (write), desc_rp (next packet to read), desc_keep (oldest not yet released; S&F: packet on the egress stream which may be retried).
- desc_cnt = wp - rp: complete packets not yet read.
- desc_held = wp - keep: complete packets not yet released (used for the 8-packet limit).

Buffer space:
- free_ptr: first word still held (S&F) — words before free_ptr are free.
- In cut-through, free_ptr tracks rd_ptr (a word is free once read).
- used = wr_ptr - (ct ? rd_ptr : free_ptr); can_accept = used != CAP && desc_held != ND.

Wait, there's a subtlety: in cut-through, `desc_held != ND` — desc_keep <= desc_rp continuously, so desc_held = desc_wp - desc_rp = desc_cnt. Hmm, in CT mode the "8 packets" limit in spec 5.6 is on packets "whose last beat has been received but which have not yet been ... completely read from the SRAM (cut-through)". desc_rp advances when the last word's read *command* is issued (pkt_pop = rd_go && rd_last). At that point the packet has been "completely read from the SRAM"? The read command is issued, data returns 3 cycles later. Close enough — the descriptor slot frees when the last read is issued.

Arbitration: in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd); wr_go = in_valid && in_ready; rd_go = rd_want && !wr_go. Round-robin: if both want, the one with priority goes; rr_rd toggles: set to 1 (read wins next) when both wr and rd happen same cycle (write won because... hmm). SRAM pins: registered ce_n/we_n/addr/wdata. Command on pins one cycle after the decision.

Egress (`pktbuf_egress`):

**pktbuf.v** (top):
```systemverilog
`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    ... same ports ...
);

    localparam ND  = 8;
    localparam NDW = 3;
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}};

    // ingress
    reg  [AW:0]  wr_ptr;
    reg  [AW:0]  pkt_start;
    reg  [15:0]  drop_cnt;

    // descriptors
    reg  [AW-1:0] desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg            desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp, desc_rp, desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_cnt  = desc_wp - desc_rp;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;

    reg  [AW:0]    free_ptr;

    wire [AW:0]   rd_ptr;
    wire           rd_want, rd_go, wr_go;
    reg            rr_rd;
    wire           pkt_release, pkt_retry;

    wire [AW:0]    used       = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire            can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    assign in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd);
    assign wr_go    = in_valid && in_ready;
    assign rd_go    = rd_want && !wr_go;

    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
    wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;
    wire pkt_pop;

    // write-age delay line: value of wr_ptr 1 and 2 cycles ago
    reg [AW:0] w_d1, w_d2;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_ptr    <= 0;
            pkt_start <= 0;
            drop_cnt  <= 0;
            rr_rd     <= 0;
            w_d1      <= 0;
            w_d2      <= 0;
        end else begin
            w_d1 <= wr_ptr;
            w_d2 <= w_d1;
            if (pkt_drop) begin
                wr_ptr   <= pkt_start;
                drop_cnt <= drop_cnt + 1;
            end else if (wr_go) begin
                wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1;
                if (in_last) pkt_start <= wr_ptr + 1;
            end
            if (wr_go && rd_want)      rr_rd <= 1;
            else if (rd_go && in_valid && can_accept) rr_rd <= 0;
        end
    end
```

Now the egress module:

```systemverilog
`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf_egress #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,
    input  wire          retry_en,
    input  wire          rd_avail,
    input  wire          rd_last,
    input  wire          rd_err,
    input  wire          rd_young,   // word at rd_ptr too new for a safe SRAM read
    input  wire [DW-1:0] yb_data,    // young-word bypass data for rd_ptr
    input  wire          rd_go,
    output wire          rd_want,
    output reg  [AW:0]   rd_ptr,
    input  wire [AW:0]   rd_restart,
    output wire          pkt_release,
    output wire          pkt_retry,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,
    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry
);

    localparam QD = 4;
    localparam QW = 2;

    // read pipeline, NW61P pipelined (RL=3):
    //   cycle c:    rd_go (command decided)
    //   cycle c+1:  rd_p1, command on the SRAM pins
    //   cycle c+2:  rd_p2, SRAM samples the command at the end of this cycle
    //   cycle c+3:  rd_p3
    //   cycle c+4:  rd_p4, read data on sram_rdata, captured at the next edge
    reg rd_p1, rd_p2, rd_p3, rd_p4;
    reg tag_last1, tag_last2, tag_last3, tag_last4;
    reg tag_err1,  tag_err2,  tag_err3,  tag_err4;

    // young-word skid buffer (one entry)
    reg          skid_valid;
    reg [DW-1:0] skid_data;
    reg          skid_last;
    reg          skid_err;

    reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_last [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_err  [0:QD-1];
    reg [QW-1:0] q_wp, q_rp;
    reg [QW:0]   q_cnt;

    wire [QW+1:0] in_flight = {2'b0, rd_p1} + {2'b0, rd_p2} + {2'b0, rd_p3} + {2'b0, rd_p4};
    wire          pipe_empty = !(rd_p1 || rd_p2 || rd_p3 || rd_p4);
    wire [QW+1:0] reserved  = {1'b0, q_cnt} + in_flight + {{QW+1{1'b0}}, skid_valid};
    wire          room      = reserved < QD;

    wire q_pop  = out_valid && out_ready;
    wire last_out = q_pop && out_last;
    assign pkt_retry   = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
    assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

    // fetch decisions
    wire skip_dir  = rd_avail && rd_young && !skid_valid && pipe_empty && room && !pkt_retry;
    wire skip_skid = rd_avail && rd_young && !skid_valid && !pipe_empty && room && !pkt_retry;
    wire skid_push = skid_valid && pipe_empty && !pkt_retry;
    assign rd_want = rd_avail && !rd_young && !skid_valid && room && !pkt_retry;

    wire fetch    = skip_dir || skip_skid || rd_go;
    wire q_push   = rd_p4 || skip_dir || skid_push;

    ...
```

Hmm wait — pkt_retry gating of fetch decisions: rd_go comes from the top (arbiter) — during cycle r (pkt_retry), rd_go might be 1 — the rd_ptr block gives retry priority ✓; but rd_want during cycle r: feeds in_ready (arbiter) — gating with !pkt_retry avoids a wasted read... but rd_go = rd_want && !wr_go computed in top — if I gate rd_want with !pkt_retry, rd_go = 0 during retry ✓ cleaner. But pkt_retry is computed INSIDE egress from q_pop... rd_want = f(pkt_retry) and pkt_retry = f(q_pop) — no combinational loop (q_pop = out_valid && out_ready; out_valid = q_cnt != 0 ✓ no loop through rd_want) ✓.

Also skip_dir during pkt_retry: gated ✓. skid_push during pkt_retry: gated ✓ (the retry clears everything anyway, but gating avoids phantom pushes... at edge r: retry branch clears; q_push during r — if not gated, q_data[q_wp] written (discarded by q_wp reset ✓ harmless)... but q_cnt update: retry branch wins ✓. Gating is belt-and-braces ✓ keep it.)

rd_ptr update:
```systemverilog

        if (!rst_n) begin

        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
```

Let me now think about the design change needed.

Key facts:
- Rev C SRAM is NW61P1024, pipelined, late write.
- The LAT strap: schematic said LAT=L (RL=2), but ECO-117 changed it: R40 removed, R41 fitted → LAT = H → RL = 3 cycles. "ECO-117 released: on every rev C board, R40 removed and R41 fitted." So as boards are built now, LAT=H, RL=3. The ECR says "make the RTL change so that pktbuf works on rev C boards as they are built" — so RL=3.
- Late write: write data D sampled one cycle after the write command. So sram_wdata must be presented the cycle AFTER the write command. In the current rev B design, sram_wdata is registered simultaneously with the command. For rev C, wdata needs a one-cycle delay relative to the command. Looking at the ILA capture: write command at cycle 4 (ce_n=0, we_n=0, addr=000), and wdata c0de0000 appears at cycle 5. Yes — wdata follows the command by one cycle.

Let me verify with the ILA: cycle 4: ce=0,we=0,addr=000,wdata=00000000. Cycle 5: ce=0,we=0,addr=001,wdata=c0de0000. So the write to addr 0 has data c0de0000 (sampled at cycle 5's edge? Actually "one row per clock edge (the values at that edge)" — so at edge 4 the command is sampled, at edge 5 the data c0de0000 is sampled along with the next command). Good.

Reads: read commands at cycles 24-39 (ce=0, we=1, addr 000...00f). Read data c0de0000 appears at cycle 27. Command at edge 24 → data at row 27. RL = 3: "captured by the controller at edge n+RL". So read at edge n, data captured at edge n+3. That matches LAT=H, RL=3.

Also the write-then-read in step 4: cycle 68: write addr 000, data at cycle 69 = f00d0000. Read of addr 000 at cycle 69 (ce=0,we=1,addr=000). Data f00d0000 appears at cycle 72. 69+3 = 72. ✓. Interesting: the read at edge 69 of the address whose write data is sampled at edge 69 returns the new data — write data is sampled at edge 69 and the array read at edge 69... the datasheet says read "is read from the array at edge n". The write data sampled at edge 69 — does the read at edge 69 get the new or old data? Capture shows new data (f00d0000). That's a detail of the SRAM; for our design, we control scheduling so we don't need same-edge read-after-write-data.

Also note the k=1 case at cycle 92-97: write cmd at 92 (data at 93), read cmd at 94, data at 97 = 5eed0022 (new data). Fine.

So the change:
1. Read latency is now 3 cycles (RL=3) instead of 1. The egress read pipeline must capture sram_rdata 3 cycles after the read command edge.
2. Write data must be delayed by one cycle relative to the write command.

Also consistent! Both models give the same observable behavior at the pins:

A read with cmd at edge m returns the value at address A as of... the newest write with cmd edge ≤ m-3 (wdata edge ≤ m-2). I.e., writes become visible to reads 3 edges after the write cmd edge.

For my design, the safe rule: **a read of address A must have its command edge at least 3 edges after the write command edge of the last write to A** (equivalently ≥2 edges after the wdata edge). To be conservative, I could require read cmd edge ≥ write cmd edge + 3. But that's the minimal to satisfy both candidate models.

Now the impact on cut-through first-beat latency (6.4, 5 cycles): beat taken E1; write cmd edge E2; wdata edge E3; earliest safe read cmd edge E5; data captured E8 (RL=3); fall-through beat moves E8. E1→E8 = 7 > 5. IMPOSSIBLE without a bypass.

Therefore: the design MUST forward ingress data to the egress path for words not yet visible in the SRAM, at least for the first beat. Or more generally: implement a write-to-read bypass for recently-written words.

Approach: keep a small CAM-like structure of recent writes (address + data), and when read data returns from the SRAM, check whether the read address matches a write that was "too recent" at read-cmd time; if so, use the bypass data. That's complex.

Alternative cleaner approach: delay-line bypass. Since the write visibility delay is exactly 3 edges from cmd, and reads also have latency 3 from cmd: if read cmd at edge m reads address A, and a write to A had cmd at edge m-3 (the minimum safe), it sees new data. Anything closer needs bypass. Rather than a general CAM, note the design's access pattern: it's a FIFO ring — reads and writes are sequential. The only read-after-write hazard is for the most recently written few words (the tail of the ring).

Simplest robust solution: a small "tail buffer" in flops. Keep the last K words written in a register FIFO (K ≥ hazard window). When the egress needs to read a word that is still within the tail window, don't read the SRAM at all — or read but override with tail data. Actually simpler: the egress read path can be served from the tail buffer whenever rd_ptr is within the last K written words; otherwise from SRAM.

The core problem: SRAM read latency 3 (cmd to data) + write visibility 3 (cmd to readable). Total cmd-to-cmd hazard: a word written with cmd at edge n can be read with cmd at edge n+3 earliest, data at n+6.

### pktbuf_egress.v (new)

```verilog
`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf_egress #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,

    input  wire          retry_en,
    input  wire          rd_avail,
    input  wire          rd_last,
    input  wire          rd_err,
    input  wire          rd_go,

    input  wire [AW:0]   rd_restart,

    output wire          pkt_retry,

    // bypass: data for the word at rd_ptr when it is too new to read from the SRAM
    input  wire          rd_bypass,   // the word at rd_ptr is not yet visible in the SRAM
    input  wire [DW-1:0] rd_bdata,    // ... its data, from the tail copy

    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,

    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry
);

    localparam QD = 8;      // output queue entries
    localparam QW = 3;      // log2(QD)

    // Read pipeline, NW61P pipelined (LAT = H, RL = 3):
    //   rd_go    read command leaves the arbiter (this cycle)
    //   rd_p0    the command is on the SRAM pins
    //   rd_p1    the SRAM samples the command at the end of this cycle
    //   rd_p2    read pipeline
    //   rd_p3    read data is on sram_rdata this cycle; captured at the end
    reg rd_p0, rd_p1, rd_p2, rd_p3;
    reg          tag_last0, tag_last1, tag_last2, tag_last3;
    reg          tag_err0,  tag_err1,  tag_err2,  tag_err3;
    reg          tag_bpass0, tag_bpass1, tag_bpass2, tag_bpass3;
    reg [DW-1:0] tag_bdata0, tag_bdata1, tag_bdata2, tag_bdata3;
    ...
```

```verilog
// pktbuf.v
// ... header comment updated for rev C ...

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,
    input  wire          cfg_cut_through,
    input  wire          in_valid,
    output wire          in_ready,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] in_data,
    input  wire          in_last,
    input  wire          in_err,
    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry,
    output wire [15:0]   drop_count,
    output reg           sram_ce_n,
    output reg           sram_we_n,
    output reg  [AW-1:0] sram_addr,
    output reg  [DW-1:0] sram_wdata,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata
);

    localparam ND  = 8;
    localparam NDW = 3;
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}};
    localparam TW  = 2;                       // tail copy depth = 2**TW words

    // ingress
    reg  [AW:0]    wr_ptr;
    reg  [AW:0]    pkt_start;
    reg  [15:0]    drop_cnt;

    reg  [AW-1:0]  desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg            desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_rp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_cnt  = desc_wp - desc_rp;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;

    reg  [AW:0]    free_ptr;

    wire [AW:0]    rd_ptr;
    wire           rd_want;
    wire           rd_go;
    wire           wr_go;
    wire           pkt_release;
    wire           pkt_retry;

    wire [AW:0]    used       = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire           can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    // Rev C: reads have priority for the SRAM command slot. ...
    assign in_ready = can_accept && !rd_want;
    assign wr_go    = in_valid && in_ready;
    assign rd_go    = rd_want;
    ...
```

```verilog
    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
```

```verilog
    // Rev C: a word cannot be read back from the SRAM until three clock
    // edges after its write command (late write, pipelined array; see
    // docs/ila_sram_sn0007.csv). Words that new are served from a small
    // flop copy of the most recently written words instead. ...
    reg [DW-1:0] tail_data [0:(1<<TW)-1];
    reg          wr_d1, wr_d2;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go)
            tail_data[wr_ptr[TW-1:0]] <= in_data;
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_d1 <= 1'b0;
            wr_d2 <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            wr_d1 <= wr_go;
            wr_d2 <= wr_d1;
        end
    end

    wire [1:0]   recent_wr = {1'b0, wr_d1} + {1'b0, wr_d2};
    wire [AW:0]  unread   = wr_ptr - rd_ptr;
    wire         rd_bypass = (unread <= {{(AW-1){1'b0}}, recent_wr});
    wire [DW-1:0] rd_bdata = tail_data[rd_ptr[TW-1:0]];
```

Now write the TB model for rev C SRAM (for my own testing):

```verilog
    // NW61P1024 model, LAT = H (RL = 3), late write.
    reg [DW-1:0] mem [0:(1<<AW)-1];
    reg          w_v0, w_v1;
    reg [AW-1:0] w_a0, w_a1;
    reg [DW-1:0] w_d1;
    reg          r_v0, r_v1, r_v2;
    reg [DW-1:0] r_d0, r_d1, r_d2;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        // write: command edge, then data edge, then array update
        if (w_v1) mem[w_a1] <= w_d1;         // array write 2 edges after cmd
```

Let me write the egress file:

```verilog
// pktbuf_egress.v
//
// Egress half of pktbuf: issues SRAM reads in address order, follows each
// read through the SRAM, queues the returned words for the egress stream,
// and handles a retry request at the end of a packet. See
// docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// Board rev C (NW61P1024, pipelined, late write, LAT strapped high):
//   - read data is captured three cycles after the read command edge
//     (RL = 3), so the read pipeline is four stages deep;
//   - a word is not readable in the SRAM until three edges after its
//     write command edge (see docs/ila_sram_sn0007.csv); words that new
//     are bypassed from the flop copy presented on rd_bypass/rd_bdata;
//   - the first queue entry falls through to the output stream, so a
//     returning word can leave on the same edge it is captured.

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf_egress #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,

    input  wire          retry_en,
    input  wire          rd_avail,
    input  wire          rd_last,
    input  wire          rd_err,
    input  wire          rd_go,
    output wire          rd_want,
    output reg  [AW:0]   rd_ptr,
    input  wire [AW:0]   rd_restart,
    output wire          pkt_release,
    output wire          pkt_retry,

    input  wire          rd_bypass,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] rd_bdata,

    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,

    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry
);

    localparam QD = 8;
    localparam QW = 3;

    reg rd_p0, rd_p1, rd_p2, rd_p3;
    reg          tag_last0, tag_last1, tag_last2, tag_last3;
    reg          tag_err0,  tag_err1,  tag_err2,  tag_err3;
    reg          tag_byp0,  tag_byp1,  tag_byp2,  tag_byp3;
    reg [DW-1:0] tag_dat0,  tag_dat1,  tag_dat2,  tag_dat3;

    reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_last [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_err  [0:QD-1];
    reg [QW-1:0] q_wp;
    reg [QW-1:0] q_rp;
    reg [QW:0]   q_cnt;

    wire [QW:0]  in_flight = {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p0} + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p1}
                           + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p2} + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p3};
    wire         q_push    = rd_p3;
    wire [DW-1:0] push_data = tag_byp3 ? tag_dat3 : sram_rdata;
    wire         push_last = tag_last3;
    wire         push_err  = tag_err3 && tag_last3;

    wire         q_empty = (q_cnt == {(QW+1){1'b0}});

    assign out_valid = !q_empty || q_push;
    assign out_data  = q_empty ? push_data : q_data[q_rp];
    assign out_last  = q_empty ? push_last : q_last[q_rp];
    assign out_err   = q_empty ? push_err  : q_err[q_rp];
    wire         q_pop = out_valid && out_ready;

    wire         last_out = q_pop && out_last;
    assign pkt_retry   = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
    assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

    assign rd_want = rd_avail && ((q_cnt + in_flight) < QD);

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            rd_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p2  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p3  <= 1'b0;
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            rd_ptr <= rd_restart;
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p2  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p3  <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (rd_go)
                rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1'b1;
            rd_p0 <= rd_go;
            rd_p1 <= rd_p0;
            rd_p2 <= rd_p1;
            rd_p3 <= rd_p2;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        tag_last0 <= rd_last;
        tag_err0  <= rd_err;
        tag_byp0  <= rd_bypass;
        tag_dat0  <= rd_bdata;
        tag_last1 <= tag_last0;
        tag_err1  <= tag_err0;
        tag_byp1  <= tag_byp0;
        tag_dat1  <= tag_dat0;
        tag_last2 <= tag_last1;
        tag_err2  <= tag_err1;
        tag_byp2  <= tag_byp1;
        tag_dat2  <= tag_dat1;
        tag_last3 <= tag_last2;
        tag_err3  <= tag_err2;
        tag_byp3  <= tag_byp2;
        tag_dat3  <= tag_dat2;
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (q_push) begin
            q_data[q_wp] <= push_data;
            q_last[q_wp] <= push_last;
            q_err[q_wp]  <= push_err;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            q_wp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_rp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            q_rp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_wp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (q_push)
                q_wp <= q_wp + 1'b1;
            if (q_pop)
                q_rp <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            case ({q_push, q_pop})
                2'b10:   q_cnt <= q_cnt + 1'b1;
                2'b01:   q_cnt <= q_cnt - 1'b1;
                default: q_cnt <= q_cnt;
            endcase
        end
    end

endmodule
```

But WAIT — there's a subtle issue with the fall-through and q_rp when q_empty && q_push && q_pop: the entry was written at q_wp == q_rp (empty ⇒ wp == rp). q_rp advances past it ✓. Next word: out_data = q_data[q_rp] when non-empty ✓.

Now pktbuf.v full:

```verilog
// pktbuf.v  (header updated)

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    ... same ports ...
);

    localparam ND  = 8;
    localparam NDW = 3;
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}};
    localparam TW  = 2;

    reg  [AW:0]    wr_ptr;
    reg  [AW:0]    pkt_start;
    reg  [15:0]    drop_cnt;

    reg  [AW-1:0]  desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg            desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_rp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_cnt  = desc_wp - desc_rp;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;

    reg  [AW:0]    free_ptr;

    wire [AW:0]    rd_ptr;
    wire           rd_want;
    wire           rd_go;
    wire           wr_go;
    wire           pkt_release;
    wire           pkt_retry;

    wire [AW:0]    used       = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire           can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    // One SRAM command per cycle. On rev C the read side has priority:
    // with RL = 3 the cut-through first-beat budget (spec 6.4) leaves no
    // room for a read to wait behind a write.
    assign in_ready = can_accept && !rd_want;
    assign wr_go    = in_valid && in_ready;
    assign rd_go    = rd_want;

    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
    wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;
    wire pkt_pop;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_ptr    <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            pkt_start <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            drop_cnt  <= 16'd0;
        end else begin
            if (pkt_drop) begin
                wr_ptr   <= pkt_start;
                drop_cnt <= drop_cnt + 16'd1;
            end else if (wr_go) begin
                wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
                if (in_last)
                    pkt_start <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (pkt_push) begin
            desc_end[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            desc_err[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= in_err;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            desc_wp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_rp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_keep <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            free_ptr  <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (pkt_push)
                desc_wp <= desc_wp + 1'b1;

            if (pkt_retry)
                desc_rp <= desc_keep;
            else if (pkt_pop)
                desc_rp <= desc_rp + 1'b1;

            if (cfg_cut_through) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_rp;
                free_ptr  <= rd_ptr;
            end else if (pkt_release) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_keep + 1'b1;
                free_ptr  <= free_ptr + {1'b0, desc_end[desc_keep[NDW-1:0]] - free_ptr[AW-1:0]} + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    wire head_valid = (desc_cnt != 0);
    wire rd_last    = head_valid && (rd_ptr[AW-1:0] == desc_end[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]]);
    wire rd_err     = desc_err[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]];

    wire rd_avail   = cfg_cut_through ? (rd_ptr != wr_ptr) : head_valid;

    assign pkt_pop  = rd_go && rd_last;

    // Rev C: the NW61P1024 is pipelined with late write. A word is not
    // readable in the array until three clock edges after its write
    // command edge (docs/ila_sram_sn0007.csv); a read issued sooner
    // returns stale data. The last 2**TW written words are kept in flops;
    // a read of a word still inside that window takes the flop copy.
    reg [DW-1:0] tail_data [0:(1<<TW)-1];
    reg          wr_d1, wr_d2;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go)
            tail_data[wr_ptr[TW-1:0]] <= in_data;
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_d1 <= 1'b0;
            wr_d2 <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            wr_d1 <= wr_go;
            wr_d2 <= wr_d1;
        end
    end

    wire [1:0]   recent_wr = {1'b0, wr_d1} + {1'b0, wr_d2};
    wire [AW:0]  unread    = wr_ptr - rd_ptr;
    wire         rd_bypass = (unread <= {{(AW-1){1'b0}}, recent_wr});
    wire [DW-1:0] rd_bdata  = tail_data[rd_ptr[TW-1:0]];

    // SRAM pins. Late write: the write data follows the write command by
    // one cycle.
    reg [DW-1:0] wdata_d1;
    reg          wdata_d1_v;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            sram_ce_n  <= 1'b1;
            sram_we_n  <= 1'b1;
            wdata_d1_v <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            sram_ce_n  <= !(wr_go || rd_go);
            sram_we_n  <= !wr_go;
            wdata_d1_v <= wr_go;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go) begin
            sram_addr <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            wdata_d1  <= in_data;
        end else if (rd_go) begin
            sram_addr <= rd_ptr[AW-1:0];
        end
        if (wdata_d1_v)
            sram_wdata <= wdata_d1;
    end

    assign drop_count = drop_cnt;

    pktbuf_egress #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) u_egress (
        .clk         (clk),
        .rst_n       (rst_n),
        .retry_en    (!cfg_cut_through),
        .rd_avail    (rd_avail),
        .rd_last     (rd_last),
        .rd_err      (rd_err),
        .rd_go       (rd_go),
```

Now I understand the situation. Let me analyze the key facts:

1. **Rev C SRAM (NW61P1024)**: pipelined, late-write. Board notes say ECO-117 re-strapped LAT to **H** on every rev C board → **RL=3** (confirmed by the ILA capture: read cmd at edge 24, data at edge 27).
2. **Late write**: wdata is sampled one cycle after the write command (ILA: cmd row 4, wdata row 5).
3. **Write visibility hazard**: the ILA step-4 capture shows a read returns NEW data only if its command edge is ≥3 edges after the write command edge (k=0,1 → old data; k=2 → new). So freshly-written words must be bypassed from flops.
4. **Performance consequences**: cut-through first-beat budget stays 5 cycles (6.4) — with RL=3 the read must win the very next command slot (read priority) and the output queue needs fall-through. S&F budget relaxes to 10 cycles.

// pktbuf_egress.v
//
// Egress half of pktbuf: issues SRAM reads in address order, follows each
// read through the SRAM, queues the returned words for the egress stream,
// and handles a retry request at the end of a packet. See
// docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// Board rev C (NW61P1024, pipelined, late write, LAT strapped high):
//   - read data is captured three cycles after the read command edge
//     (RL = 3), so the read pipeline is four stages deep;
//   - a word cannot be read from the array until three edges after its
//     write command edge (see docs/ila_sram_sn0007.csv); words that new
//     are bypassed from the flop copy on rd_bypass/rd_bdata;
//   - the head of the output queue falls through to the output stream, so
//     a returning word can leave on the same edge it is captured.

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf_egress #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,

    input  wire          retry_en,    // store-and-forward: out_retry is honoured
    input  wire          rd_avail,    // the word at rd_ptr may be read
    input  wire          rd_last,     // ... and is the last of its packet
    input  wire          rd_err,      // ... and that packet had in_err
    input  wire          rd_go,       // the arbiter issues the read this cycle
    output wire          rd_want,
    output reg  [AW:0]   rd_ptr,
    input  wire [AW:0]   rd_restart,  // first word of the packet on the egress stream
    output wire          pkt_release, // a last beat moved, packet done
    output wire          pkt_retry,   // a last beat moved with out_retry: send it again

    input  wire          rd_bypass,   // the word at rd_ptr is too new for the SRAM
    input  wire [DW-1:0] rd_bdata,    // ... its data, from the tail copy

    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,

    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry
);

    localparam QD = 8;      // output queue entries
    localparam QW = 3;      // log2(QD)

    // Read pipeline, NW61P pipelined, LAT = H (RL = 3):
    //   rd_go  the read command leaves the arbiter this cycle
    //   rd_p0  the command is on the SRAM pins
    //   rd_p1  the SRAM samples the command at the end of this cycle
    //   rd_p2  the word is read from the array and flows down the pipe
    //   rd_p3  the data is on sram_rdata this cycle and is captured at
    //          the next edge
    reg          rd_p0, rd_p1, rd_p2, rd_p3;
    reg          tag_last0, tag_last1, tag_last2, tag_last3;
    reg          tag_err0,  tag_err1,  tag_err2,  tag_err3;
    reg          tag_byp0,  tag_byp1,  tag_byp2,  tag_byp3;
    reg [DW-1:0] tag_dat0,  tag_dat1,  tag_dat2,  tag_dat3;

    reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_last [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_err  [0:QD-1];
    reg [QW-1:0] q_wp;
    reg [QW-1:0] q_rp;
    reg [QW:0]   q_cnt;

    wire [QW:0]   in_flight = {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p0} + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p1}
                            + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p2} + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p3};
    wire          q_push    = rd_p3;
    wire [DW-1:0] push_data = tag_byp3 ? tag_dat3 : sram_rdata;
    wire          push_last = tag_last3;
    wire          push_err  = tag_err3 && tag_last3;

    // Fall-through: with the queue empty, the word returning this cycle is
    // offered on the output stream in the same cycle.
    wire          q_empty = (q_cnt == {(QW+1){1'b0}});

    assign out_valid = !q_empty || q_push;
    assign out_data  = q_empty ? push_data : q_data[q_rp];
    assign out_last  = q_empty ? push_last : q_last[q_rp];
    assign out_err   = q_empty ? push_err  : q_err[q_rp];
    wire          q_pop = out_valid && out_ready;

    // End of a packet on the egress stream. A retry throws away everything
    // read ahead (queued words and reads in flight) and starts reading the
    // same packet again from its first word.
    wire          last_out  = q_pop && out_last;
    assign pkt_retry   = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
    assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

    // Ask for a read only when its data is sure to find a free entry.
    assign rd_want = rd_avail && ((q_cnt + in_flight) < QD);

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            rd_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p2  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p3  <= 1'b0;
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            rd_ptr <= rd_restart;
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p2  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p3  <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (rd_go)
                rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1'b1;
            rd_p0 <= rd_go;
            rd_p1 <= rd_p0;
            rd_p2 <= rd_p1;
            rd_p3 <= rd_p2;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        tag_last0 <= rd_last;
        tag_err0  <= rd_err;
        tag_byp0  <= rd_bypass;
        tag_dat0  <= rd_bdata;
        tag_last1 <= tag_last0;
        tag_err1  <= tag_err0;
        tag_byp1  <= tag_byp0;
        tag_dat1  <= tag_dat0;
        tag_last2 <= tag_last1;
        tag_err2  <= tag_err1;
        tag_byp2  <= tag_byp1;
        tag_dat2  <= tag_dat1;
        tag_last3 <= tag_last2;
        tag_err3  <= tag_err2;
        tag_byp3  <= tag_byp2;
        tag_dat3  <= tag_dat2;
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (q_push) begin
            q_data[q_wp] <= push_data;
            q_last[q_wp] <= push_last;
            q_err[q_wp]  <= push_err;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            q_wp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_rp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            q_rp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_wp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (q_push)
                q_wp <= q_wp + 1'b1;
            if (q_pop)
                q_rp <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            case ({q_push, q_pop})
                2'b10:   q_cnt <= q_cnt + 1'b1;
                2'b01:   q_cnt <= q_cnt - 1'b1;
                default: q_cnt <= q_cnt;
            endcase
        end
    end

endmodule
EOF
