cat > /app/data/pktbuf.v << 'EOF'
// pktbuf.v
//
// Packet buffer between the line-side receive stream and the switch
// interface. Packets arrive on a valid/ready stream, are stored in an
// external synchronous SRAM, and leave on a second valid/ready stream.
// The block behaviour is specified in docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// ECR-0412, board rev C: the SRAM is the NW61P1024 pipelined part with
// late write, fitted on the NW61F1024 footprint and strapped LAT = H on
// every rev C board (ECO-117), so reads return after three cycles and
// write data follows the write command by one cycle. See
// docs/NW61P1024_excerpt.md, docs/board_rev_c_notes.md and the SRAM port
// capture docs/ila_sram_sn0007.csv. Consequences for this RTL:
//   - write commands carry no data; sram_wdata is the write data of the
//     command one cycle earlier (late write);
//   - a word cannot be read from the array until three edges after its
//     write command edge, so a copy of the last four words written is
//     kept in flops (tail_data) and a read of a word that new bypasses
//     the SRAM;
//   - reads get priority over writes: at 125 MHz and RL = 3, a read
//     losing the command slot after a new ingress beat would miss the
//     cut-through first-beat budget of spec 6.4.
//
// This file holds the top level: ingress, the packet descriptor queue,
// buffer space and retry bookkeeping, the SRAM command arbiter, the
// write tail copy and the SRAM pins. The read pipeline and the output
// queue are in pktbuf_egress.v.

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,          // data width, also the SRAM word width
    parameter AW = 10           // SRAM address width, 2**AW words
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,           // asynchronous assert, active low

    input  wire          cfg_cut_through, // 0 store-and-forward, 1 cut-through

    // ingress stream
    input  wire          in_valid,
    output wire          in_ready,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] in_data,
    input  wire          in_last,
    input  wire          in_err,          // sampled with in_last only

    // egress stream
    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry,       // sampled with the last beat only

    // status
    output wire [15:0]   drop_count,

    // external SRAM, all outputs driven from flops
    output reg           sram_ce_n,
    output reg           sram_we_n,
    output reg  [AW-1:0] sram_addr,
    output reg  [DW-1:0] sram_wdata,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata
);

    localparam ND  = 8;                         // packet descriptor slots
    localparam NDW = 3;                         // log2(ND)
    localparam TC  = 4;                         // write tail copy entries
    localparam TCW = 2;                         // log2(TC)
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}}; // 2**AW words

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Ingress
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg  [AW:0]    wr_ptr;      // address of the next word to write
    reg  [AW:0]    pkt_start;   // first address of the packet being received
    reg  [15:0]    drop_cnt;

    // Packet descriptor queue: the address of each packet's last word and
    // its error flag. In store-and-forward mode an entry means "this packet
    // is complete". In cut-through mode it only marks where a packet ends.
    // Three free-running pointers (one bit wider than the index):
    //   desc_wp    next entry to write
    //   desc_rp    next packet to read from the SRAM
    //   desc_keep  oldest packet not yet released (store-and-forward: the
    //              packet on the egress stream, which may still be retried)
    reg  [AW-1:0]  desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg            desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_rp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_cnt  = desc_wp - desc_rp;     // complete, not yet read
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;   // complete, not yet released

    // Buffer space. Cut-through: a word is free once it has been read.
    // Store-and-forward: a packet's words stay until the packet is released,
    // so that it can be sent again; free_ptr is the first word still held.
    reg  [AW:0]    free_ptr;

    wire [AW:0]    rd_ptr;      // address of the next word to read (egress)
    wire           rd_want;     // egress asks for a read command this cycle
    wire           rd_go;       // ... and gets it
    wire           wr_go;       // an ingress beat is written this cycle
    wire           pkt_release; // egress: a packet's last beat moved, no retry
    wire           pkt_retry;   // egress: a packet's last beat moved with retry

    wire [AW:0]    used       = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire           can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    // One SRAM command per cycle. Reads have priority: with RL = 3 a read
    // that loses the slot after a new ingress beat cannot make the
    // cut-through first-beat budget of spec 6.4.
    assign in_ready = can_accept && !rd_want;
    assign wr_go    = in_valid && in_ready;
    assign rd_go    = rd_want && !wr_go;

    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
    wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;
    wire pkt_pop;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Write tail copy and read bypass
    //
    // On the rev C part a read command issued fewer than three edges after
    // the write command of the same word returns the old array contents
    // (see docs/ila_sram_sn0007.csv), so the last TC words written are
    // kept in flops. tail_u points at the slot of the word at wr_ptr,
    // which is never read yet; the word at rd_ptr is too new exactly when
    // wr_ptr - rd_ptr is in [1, TC].
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg  [DW-1:0]  tail_data [0:TC-1];
    reg  [TCW-1:0] tail_u;      // slot of the word at wr_ptr

    wire [AW:0]    d_ru      = wr_ptr - rd_ptr;
    wire            rd_bypass = (d_ru[AW:TCW] == {(AW-TCW+1){1'b0}})
                                && (d_ru[TCW-1:0] != {TCW{1'b0}});
    wire [TCW-1:0] rb_index   = tail_u - d_ru[TCW-1:0];

    wire [TCW-1:0] tail_u_next = (wr_go && !pkt_drop) ? tail_u + 1'b1
                               : pkt_drop             ? tail_u - (wr_ptr - pkt_start)[TCW-1:0]
                               :                        tail_u;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go)
            tail_data[tail_u] <= in_data;
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Pointers
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_ptr    <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            pkt_start <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            tail_u    <= {TCW{1'b0}};
            drop_cnt  <= 16'd0;
        end else begin
            tail_u <= tail_u_next;
            if (pkt_drop) begin
                wr_ptr   <= pkt_start;          // forget the whole packet
                drop_cnt <= drop_cnt + 16'd1;
            end else if (wr_go) begin
                wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
                if (in_last)
                    pkt_start <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Descriptor queue, release and retry
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (pkt_push) begin
            desc_end[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            desc_err[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= in_err;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            desc_wp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_rp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_keep <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            free_ptr  <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (pkt_push)
                desc_wp <= desc_wp + 1'b1;

            if (pkt_retry)
                desc_rp <= desc_keep;           // read the packet again
            else if (pkt_pop)
                desc_rp <= desc_rp + 1'b1;

            if (cfg_cut_through) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_rp;
                free_ptr  <= rd_ptr;
            end else if (pkt_release) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_keep + 1'b1;
                free_ptr  <= free_ptr + {1'b0, desc_end[desc_keep[NDW-1:0]] - free_ptr[AW-1:0]} + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    // What the egress may read next.
    wire head_valid = (desc_cnt != 0);
    wire rd_last    = head_valid && (rd_ptr[AW-1:0] == desc_end[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]]);
    wire rd_err     = desc_err[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]];

    // Store-and-forward: only words of complete packets.
    // Cut-through: any word already written.
    wire rd_avail   = cfg_cut_through ? (rd_ptr != wr_ptr) : head_valid;

    assign pkt_pop  = rd_go && rd_last;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // SRAM pins. Commands leave one cycle after the arbiter decision;
    // write data leaves one cycle after the write command (late write).
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            sram_ce_n <= 1'b1;
            sram_we_n <= 1'b1;
        end else begin
            sram_ce_n <= !(wr_go || rd_go);
            sram_we_n <= !wr_go;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go)
            sram_addr <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
        else if (rd_go)
            sram_addr <= rd_ptr[AW-1:0];

        if (wr_go)
            sram_wdata <= in_data;
    end

    assign drop_count = drop_cnt;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Egress
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    pktbuf_egress #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) u_egress (
        .clk         (clk),
        .rst_n       (rst_n),
        .retry_en    (!cfg_cut_through),
        .rd_avail    (rd_avail),
        .rd_last     (rd_last),
        .rd_err      (rd_err),
        .rd_go       (rd_go),
        .rd_want     (rd_want),
        .rd_ptr      (rd_ptr),
        .rd_restart  (free_ptr),
        .rd_bypass   (rd_bypass),
        .rd_bdata    (tail_data[rb_index]),
        .pkt_release (pkt_release),
        .pkt_retry   (pkt_retry),
        .sram_rdata  (sram_rdata),
        .out_valid   (out_valid),
        .out_ready   (out_ready),
        .out_data    (out_data),
        .out_last    (out_last),
        .out_err     (out_err),
        .out_retry   (out_retry)
    );

endmodule

`timescale 1ns/1ps
// Smoke test for pktbuf on board rev C (NW61P1024 pipelined, late write,
// LAT strapped H by ECO-117: RL = 3). Not a sign-off bench.
//
// SRAM model (docs/NW61P1024_excerpt.md + ila_sram_sn0007.csv):
//   - write command at edge n: A sampled at n, D sampled at n+1;
//   - read command at edge n: data captured by the FPGA at edge n+3;
//   - a read command issued < 3 edges after the write command of the
//     same word returns the OLD contents; >= 3 edges returns the new.
module tb_smoke;
    localparam DW = 32;
    localparam AW = 10;
    localparam RL = 3;

    reg clk = 1'b0;
    always #5 clk = ~clk;

    reg           rst_n     = 1'b0;
    reg           cfg_ct    = 1'b0;
    reg           in_valid  = 1'b0;
    reg  [DW-1:0] in_data   = {DW{1'b0}};
    reg           in_last   = 1'b0;
    reg           in_err    = 1'b0;
    reg           out_ready = 1'b1;
    reg           out_retry = 1'b0;
    wire          in_ready, out_valid, out_last, out_err;
    wire [DW-1:0] out_data;
    wire [15:0]   drop_count;
    wire          sram_ce_n, sram_we_n;
    wire [AW-1:0] sram_addr;
    wire [DW-1:0] sram_wdata;
    reg  [DW-1:0] sram_rdata;

    pktbuf #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) dut (
        .clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .cfg_cut_through(cfg_ct),
        .in_valid(in_valid), .in_ready(in_ready), .in_data(in_data),
        .in_last(in_last), .in_err(in_err),
        .out_valid(out_valid), .out_ready(out_ready), .out_data(out_data),
        .out_last(out_last), .out_err(out_err), .out_retry(out_retry),
        .drop_count(drop_count),
        .sram_ce_n(sram_ce_n), .sram_we_n(sram_we_n), .sram_addr(sram_addr),
        .sram_wdata(sram_wdata), .sram_rdata(sram_rdata)
    );

    // ---------------- NW61P1024 model (LAT = H) ----------------
    reg [DW-1:0] mem    [0:(1<<AW)-1];
    integer      wtime  [0:(1<<AW)-1];   // edge count of last write cmd
    integer      edge_cnt = 0;
    reg [DW-1:0] pend_d;
    reg          pend_v = 1'b0;
    reg [DW-1:0] rdpipe [0:RL-1];
    integer      k;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        edge_cnt <= edge_cnt + 1;
        // late write: data of the command one cycle earlier
        if (pend_v) mem[pend_a] <= pend_d;
        pend_v <= (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b0);
        if (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b0) begin
            pend_a <= sram_addr;
            wtime[sram_addr] <= edge_cnt;
        end
        pend_d <= sram_wdata;
        // read pipeline
        for (k = RL-1; k > 0; k = k - 1) rdpipe[k] <= rdpipe[k-1];
        if (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b1) begin
            if (edge_cnt - wtime[sram_addr] >= 3)
                rdpipe[0] <= mem[sram_addr];       // settled: array value
            else
                rdpipe[0] <= mem[sram_addr];       // old array value (pre-write)
        end else
            rdpipe[0] <= 32'hDEADBEEF;
        sram_rdata <= rdpipe[RL-1];
    end
    reg [AW-1:0] pend_a;

    // ---------------- stimulus ----------------
    reg [DW-1:0] exp_d [0:65535];
    reg          exp_l [0:65535];
    reg          exp_e [0:65535];
    integer      n_in, n_out, errors, p, len, drops;
    reg          e;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst_n && out_valid && out_ready) begin
            if (out_data !== exp_d[n_out] || out_last !== exp_l[n_out] || out_err !== exp_e[n_out]) begin
                if (errors < 8)
                    $display("smoke: beat %0d: got %h l%b e%b, expected %h l%b e%b",
                             n_out, out_data, out_last, out_err, exp_d[n_out], exp_l[n_out], exp_e[n_out]);
                errors = errors + 1;
            end
            n_out = n_out + 1;
        end
    end

    // random backpressure
    always @(negedge clk) if (rst_n) out_ready <= ($random % 4) != 0;

    task send_packet(input integer n, input integer errf);
        integer b;
        begin
            for (b = 0; b < n; b = b + 1) begin
                @(negedge clk);
                in_valid = 1'b1;
                in_data  = $random;
                in_last  = (b == n - 1);
                in_err   = (b == n - 1) && (errf != 0);
                #1;
                while (in_ready !== 1'b1) begin @(negedge clk); #1; end
                @(posedge clk);
                if (cfg_ct || !errf) begin          // kept beats
                    exp_d[n_in] = in_data;
                    exp_l[n_in] = in_last;
                    exp_e[n_in] = in_last && errf && cfg_ct;
                    n_in = n_in + 1;
                end
                @(negedge clk); #1;
                while (in_ready !== 1'b1 && b < n-1) begin @(negedge clk); #1; end
            end
            @(negedge clk);
            in_valid = 1'b0; in_last = 1'b0; in_err = 1'b0;
        end
    endtask

    task wait_drain;
        integer t;
        begin
            t = 0;
            while (n_out < n_in && t < 20000) begin @(posedge clk); t = t + 1; end
        end
    endtask

    initial begin
        n_in = 0; n_out = 0; errors = 0; drops = 0;
        repeat (4) @(negedge clk);
        rst_n = 1'b1;
        repeat (4) @(negedge clk);

        cfg_ct = 1'b0;
        for (p = 0; p < 40; p = p + 1) begin
            len = 1 + ($random % 20);
            e   = ($random % 5 == 0);
            send_packet(len, e);
            if (e) drops = drops + 1;
        end
        wait_drain;
        if (drop_count != drops) begin
            $display("smoke: drop_count %0d, expected %0d", drop_count, drops);
            errors = errors + 1;
        end
        repeat (12) @(negedge clk);

        cfg_ct = 1'b1;
        repeat (12) @(negedge clk);
        for (p = 0; p < 40; p = p + 1) begin
            len = 1 + ($random % 20);
            e   = ($random % 5 == 0);
            send_packet(len, e);
        end
        wait_drain;
        repeat (12) @(negedge clk);

        if (n_out != n_in)
            $display("smoke: %0d beats expected, %0d received", n_in, n_out);
        if (errors == 0 && n_out == n_in)
            $display("SMOKE PASS: %0d beats, %0d drops", n_in, drops);
        else
            $display("SMOKE FAIL: %0d mismatches", errors);
        $finish;
    end

    initial begin
        #5000000;
        $display("SMOKE FAIL: timeout");
        $finish;
    end
endmodule

```
    integer b;

        b = 0;
```

module tb_dbg;
    localparam DW = 32; localparam AW = 10; localparam RL = 3;
    reg clk = 0; always #5 clk = ~clk;
    reg rst_n = 0, cfg_ct = 0, in_valid = 0, in_last = 0, in_err = 0, out_ready = 1, out_retry = 0;
    reg [DW-1:0] in_data = 0;
    wire in_ready, out_valid, out_last, out_err;
    wire [DW-1:0] out_data; wire [15:0] drop_count;
    wire sram_ce_n, sram_we_n; wire [AW-1:0] sram_addr; wire [DW-1:0] sram_wdata;
    reg [DW-1:0] sram_rdata;
    pktbuf #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) dut (.clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .cfg_cut_through(cfg_ct),
        .in_valid(in_valid), .in_ready(in_ready), .in_data(in_data), .in_last(in_last), .in_err(in_err),
        .out_valid(out_valid), .out_ready(out_ready), .out_data(out_data), .out_last(out_last),
        .out_err(out_err), .out_retry(out_retry), .drop_count(drop_count),
        .sram_ce_n(sram_ce_n), .sram_we_n(sram_we_n), .sram_addr(sram_addr),
        .sram_wdata(sram_wdata), .sram_rdata(sram_rdata));
    reg [DW-1:0] mem [0:(1<<AW)-1];
    integer wtime [0:(1<<AW)-1]; integer edge_cnt = 0;
    reg [DW-1:0] pend_d; reg [AW-1:0] pend_a; reg pend_v = 0;
    reg [DW-1:0] rdpipe [0:RL-1]; integer k;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        edge_cnt <= edge_cnt + 1;
        if (pend_v) mem[pend_a] <= pend_d;
        pend_v <= (sram_ce_n === 0 && sram_we_n === 0);
        if (sram_ce_n === 0 && sram_we_n === 0) begin pend_a <= sram_addr; wtime[sram_addr] <= edge_cnt; end
        pend_d <= sram_wdata;
        for (k = RL-1; k > 0; k = k - 1) rdpipe[k] <= rdpipe[k-1];
        if (sram_ce_n === 0 && sram_we_n === 1) rdpipe[0] <= mem[sram_addr];
        else rdpipe[0] <= 32'hDEAD0000 + edge_cnt;
        sram_rdata <= rdpipe[RL-1];
    end
    integer beat = 0;
    always @(posedge clk) if (rst_n) begin
        $display("t%0d ce_n%b we_n%b a%h w%h r%h | iv%b ir%b id%h il%b | ov%b or%b od%h ol%b oe%b",
            edge_cnt, sram_ce_n, sram_we_n, sram_addr, sram_wdata, sram_rdata,
            in_valid, in_ready, in_data, in_last, out_valid, out_ready, out_data, out_last, out_err);
        if (out_valid && out_ready) begin
            if (out_data !== 32'h1000 + beat) $display("  !! beat %0d got %h", beat, out_data);
            beat = beat + 1;
        end
    end
    integer b;
    initial begin
        repeat (4) @(negedge clk); rst_n = 1;
        repeat (2) @(negedge clk);
        for (b = 0; b < 10; b = b + 1) begin   // one 10-beat packet, S&F
            in_valid = 1; in_data = 32'h1000 + b; in_last = (b == 9);
            @(negedge clk);
        end
        in_valid = 0; in_last = 0;
        repeat (40) @(negedge clk);
        $display("beats out: %0d", beat);
        $finish;
    end
endmodule

cat /app/data/docs/pktbuf_spec.md

# pktbuf: packet buffer, block specification

Revision 1.4. Applies to `pktbuf.v` and `pktbuf_egress.v`.

## 1. Purpose

`pktbuf` sits between the line-side receive stream and the switch interface. It stores whole packets, or forwards them as they arrive, using an external synchronous SRAM as the buffer memory. One SRAM holds the words of all packets in a ring, in arrival order.

## 2. Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Supported |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DW` | Data width of both streams and of the SRAM word | 8 to 32 |
| `AW` | SRAM address width; the buffer holds 2**`AW` words | 6 to 12 |

The line card uses `DW = 32`, `AW = 10`. Other boards use other values; the block must work for every supported combination.

## 3. Ports

| Port | Dir | Width | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clk` | in | 1 | Clock. The SRAM is clocked from the same clock. |
| `rst_n` | in | 1 | Reset, active low, asserted asynchronously, released synchronously to `clk`. |
| `cfg_cut_through` | in | 1 | 0: store-and-forward. 1: cut-through. Static, see 5.4. |
| `in_valid` | in | 1 | Ingress beat valid. |
| `in_ready` | out | 1 | Ingress beat accepted at this edge if `in_valid` is also high. |
| `in_data` | in | `DW` | Ingress data. |
| `in_last` | in | 1 | Last beat of a packet. |
| `in_err` | in | 1 | Packet error. Only meaningful with `in_last`; ignored on other beats. |
| `out_valid` | out | 1 | Egress beat valid. |
| `out_ready` | in | 1 | Egress beat taken at this edge if `out_valid` is also high. |
| `out_data` | out | `DW` | Egress data. |
| `out_last` | out | 1 | Last beat of a packet. |
| `out_err` | out | 1 | Packet error, on the last beat only (cut-through mode). |
| `out_retry` | in | 1 | Retry request from the switch. Sampled only at the edge that moves the last beat of a packet; ignored at every other edge. See 5.5. |
| `drop_count` | out | 16 | Packets dropped since reset, wraps at 2**16. |
| `sram_ce_n` | out | 1 | SRAM chip enable, active low. A command is issued in each cycle with `sram_ce_n` low. |
| `sram_we_n` | out | 1 | SRAM write enable, active low: low for a write command, high for a read command. |
| `sram_addr` | out | `AW` | SRAM word address. |
| `sram_wdata` | out | `DW` | SRAM write data (to the SRAM's D inputs). |
| `sram_rdata` | in | `DW` | SRAM read data (from the SRAM's Q outputs). |

All `sram_*` outputs are driven from flops. The ports connect straight to the SRAM pins: the board and the FPGA I/O add no register stages. When the SRAM samples the pins and when it returns read data depend on the SRAM part; see the board's SRAM datasheet.

## 4. Streams

Both streams use valid/ready. A beat moves at a rising edge of `clk` at which valid and ready are both high. Once valid is high, the sender holds the beat (data, last, err) unchanged until it moves. `in_ready` may change at any time; a sender does not wait for `in_ready` before raising `in_valid`.

A packet is 1 or more beats, the last with `in_last` high. In store-and-forward mode a packet is at most 2**`AW` beats. In cut-through mode there is no limit.

## 5. Behaviour

### 5.1 Reset

While `rst_n` is low and after it is released: `out_valid` is low, `drop_count` is 0, and no SRAM command is issued (`sram_ce_n` high) until there is a beat to write. `in_ready` is high no later than 4 cycles after release.

### 5.2 Store-and-forward (`cfg_cut_through` = 0)

A packet is sent on the egress stream only after its last beat has been received. A packet whose last beat has `in_err` high is dropped: none of its beats is sent, and `drop_count` increments by one. Packets leave in the order they arrived. `out_err` is always 0.

### 5.3 Cut-through (`cfg_cut_through` = 1)

A packet may start on the egress stream as soon as its first beat has been stored. No packet is dropped and `drop_count` does not change. `out_err` is high on the last beat of a packet whose last ingress beat had `in_err` high, and low on every other beat.

### 5.4 Changing mode

`cfg_cut_through` may change only while the block is empty (every accepted beat has been sent or dropped) and no ingress beat has been accepted for at least 8 cycles. After a change, no ingress beat is offered for at least 8 cycles.

### 5.5 Retry (store-and-forward)

In store-and-forward mode the switch can refuse a packet at its end. If `out_retry` is high at the edge that moves the last beat of a packet, the block sends the same packet again, complete and unchanged, before any other packet. The resent packet can be refused again in the same way, any number of times. If `out_retry` is low at that edge, the packet is released. In cut-through mode `out_retry` is ignored.

### 5.6 Capacity and flow control

The buffer holds up to 2**`AW` words and up to 8 packets whose last beat has been received but which have not yet been released (store-and-forward) or completely read from the SRAM (cut-through). `in_ready` is low while either limit is reached. In store-and-forward mode a packet's words are kept until the packet is released. A word's location is free again once the block no longer needs it.

### 5.7 SRAM use

The SRAM takes one command per cycle. How the ingress and egress sides share it is up to the design, within the requirements of section 6. (The rev B design lets them take turns.) Once the block is empty (every accepted beat has been sent or dropped) and no beat is being received, it issues no SRAM command.

## 6. Performance

### 6.1 Ingress

While the buffer has room and the egress side is not reading, one beat is accepted per cycle.

### 6.2 Egress

While `out_ready` is high and the SRAM is not needed by the ingress side, one beat per cycle is sent, with no gaps, until the stored words run out.

### 6.3 Line rate

In store-and-forward mode, with the block empty, a packet of up to 32 beats whose beats are all offered back to back is accepted at one beat per cycle. If `out_ready` is held high and nothing else arrives, the first egress beat moves no later than 4 cycles after the edge that took the last ingress beat, and the remaining beats follow at one per cycle with no gaps.

### 6.4 Cut-through first beat

In cut-through mode, when the block is empty (every accepted beat has been sent) and `out_ready` is high, the first beat of a packet moves on the egress stream no later than 5 cycles after the edge that took it at the ingress. This is the switch's arbitration budget for cut-through packets.

## 7. Implementation notes

- The design must be synthesizable RTL. Everything below the top level is in `pktbuf.v` and `pktbuf_egress.v`.
- No initial blocks, delays, system tasks other than `$clog2`, `$signed` and `$unsigned`, and no compiler directives other than `` `timescale `` and `` `default_nettype ``. Parameter overrides on instances are by name.
- Every flop that affects behaviour is reset; the block must behave the same whatever the power-up state of its flops and memories.

# ECR-0412: pktbuf on board rev C

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Status | Approved |
| Affects | `pktbuf.v`, `pktbuf_egress.v` (line card FPGA) |
| Board | Line card rev C |

## Reason

The buffer SRAM on rev B, NW61F1024, is end of life. Rev C fits the NW61P1024 in its place. The footprint and the signals between FPGA and SRAM are the same: CE#, WE#, A[9:0], D[31:0] (write data) and Q[31:0] (read data). The NW61P1024 is a pipelined part with late write, so its timing differs. See `NW61F1024_excerpt.md`, `NW61P1024_excerpt.md` and `board_rev_c_notes.md`.

## Change

1. `pktbuf` works with the NW61P1024 as fitted and strapped on rev C boards. Rev B support is not needed. The other boards that use `pktbuf` with other `DW`/`AW` move to NW61P-family parts of the matching organisation, wired and strapped as on rev C, so the same SRAM timing applies at every `DW`/`AW`.
2. The top-level module name, ports and parameters stay as they are. The FPGA top level is not changed.
3. Behaviour stays as in `pktbuf_spec.md` for every supported `DW` and `AW`, in both modes, under any backpressure, with one exception: the line-rate limit in section 6.3 becomes **10 cycles** from the edge that took the last ingress beat to the edge that takes the first egress beat (was 4). Everything else in section 6 is unchanged: the ingress rate in 6.1, the gap-free requirements in 6.2 and 6.3, and the cut-through first-beat latency in 6.4, which is fixed by the switch.
4. All logic stays in `pktbuf.v` and `pktbuf_egress.v`.

## Verification

The block regression is being moved to a rev C SRAM model and will be run on the changed RTL at several `DW`/`AW` settings, on Icarus Verilog and on Verilator with random power-up state. The smoke test in `tb/` models the rev B part and is not part of the sign-off.

cat /app/data/docs/NW61F1024_excerpt.md

# NW61F1024: 1K x 32 synchronous SRAM, flow-through, separate I/O

Datasheet excerpt (functional description and timing summary). Rev 2.1.

## Description

The NW61F1024 is a 32 768-bit synchronous static RAM organised as 1024 words of 32 bits, with separate data inputs (D) and data outputs (Q). All inputs are registered at the rising edge of CLK. Reads are flow-through: the addressed word appears on Q in the same cycle, after the clock edge that sampled the read command.

## Pins

| Pin | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLK | in | Clock. All inputs are sampled at its rising edge. |
| CE# | in | Chip enable, active low. High: no operation (deselect). |
| WE# | in | Write enable, active low. Low with CE# low: write. High with CE# low: read. |
| A[9:0] | in | Word address. |
| D[31:0] | in | Write data. |
| Q[31:0] | out | Read data. Driven at all times; undefined except in the read data cycle. |

## Operation

Edge *n* is the rising edge of CLK at which CE# is sampled low.

| Command at edge *n* | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Deselect (CE# high) | No operation. |
| Read (WE# high) | A is sampled at edge *n*. The word is on Q after edge *n* and is captured by the controller at edge *n*+1. |
| Write (WE# low) | A and D are sampled at edge *n*. The word is written at edge *n*. |

A read at edge *n*+1 of the address written at edge *n* returns the new data. Any sequence of reads and writes may be issued, one per cycle.

## Timing summary

| Parameter | Min | Max | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clock frequency | | 133 | MHz |
| Read latency (command edge to capture edge) | 1 | 1 | cycle |

# NW61P1024: 1K x 32 synchronous SRAM, pipelined, late write, separate I/O

Datasheet excerpt (functional description and timing summary). Rev 1.4.

## Description

The NW61P1024 is a 32 768-bit synchronous static RAM organised as 1024 words of 32 bits, with separate data inputs (D) and data outputs (Q). It is pin-compatible with the NW61F1024. All inputs are registered at the rising edge of CLK. Reads go through an output pipeline whose depth is set by the LAT pin. Writes use late write: the write data follows the write command by one cycle, so reads and writes can be mixed at one command per cycle without dead cycles.

## Pins

| Pin | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLK | in | Clock. All inputs are sampled at its rising edge. |
| CE# | in | Chip enable, active low. High: no operation (deselect). |
| WE# | in | Write enable, active low. Low with CE# low: write. High with CE# low: read. |
| A[9:0] | in | Word address. |
| D[31:0] | in | Write data, sampled one cycle after the write command (late write). |
| Q[31:0] | out | Read data. Driven at all times; undefined except in the read data cycle. |
| LAT | in | Read latency select, static (strap). See below. Must not change while CLK runs. |

## Read latency

| LAT | Read latency RL (command edge to capture edge) | Clock frequency, max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L | 2 cycles | 100 MHz |
| H | 3 cycles | 166 MHz |

## Operation

Edge *n* is the rising edge of CLK at which a command is sampled.

| Command at edge *n* | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Deselect (CE# high) | No operation. |
| Read (WE# high) | A is sampled at edge *n* and the word is read from the array at edge *n*. It is on Q in the cycle before edge *n*+RL and is captured by the controller at edge *n*+RL. Q holds it for that one cycle only. |
| Write (WE# low) | A is sampled at edge *n*. D is sampled at edge *n*+1, whatever command is issued at edge *n*+1. |

Any sequence of reads, writes and deselects may be issued, one command per cycle. No dead cycle is needed between a read and a write in either order.

## Timing summary

| Parameter | Symbol | Min | Max | Unit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clock cycle time, LAT = L | tCYC | 10.0 | | ns | |
| Clock cycle time, LAT = H | tCYC | 6.0 | | ns | |
| Write data after write command | tWD | 1 | 1 | cycle | |
| Read latency | RL | 2 / 3 | 2 / 3 | cycle | set by LAT |

[title: in 6,432 · out 589] 6,432 tok #3 0:35 bash: cat /app/data/pktbuf.v · bash: cat /app/data/pktbuf_egress.v — Let me understand the key facts:

told [498 of 500 steps left · 59 of 60 minutes left]

reasoning

Let me understand the key facts:

1. Rev C replaces NW61F1024 (flow-through, read latency 1) with NW61P1024 (pipelined, late write).
2. The LAT strap: schematic rev C says LAT = L (RL=2), but ECO-117 (released 2026-09-02) removes R40 and fits R41, so LAT = H, RL=3. "on every rev C board" — so boards as built now have LAT=H → read latency 3 cycles.

The ECR says: "make the RTL change so that `pktbuf` works on rev C boards as they are built." The bring-up log says ECO-117 was released 2026-09-02, and the ILA capture is 2026-09-03 (after ECO). The schematic note says "Schematic to be updated at rev D" — so the released schematic still shows R40 fitted, but the boards as built have R41 fitted → LAT=H → RL=3.

Important trap: the schematic says LAT=L, but the boards as built (after ECO-117) have LAT=H. The clock is 125 MHz, which exceeds the 100 MHz max for LAT=L. So the design must use RL=3.

Also the ILA capture: let me examine it to confirm the timing — especially the late write behavior and RL. Let me look at the CSV.

Key SRAM changes:
- Read latency: 1 cycle (rev B) → 3 cycles (rev C, LAT=H).
- Late write: write data sampled one cycle after the write command. So `sram_wdata` must be valid one cycle after the write command is issued. On rev B, data sampled at the same edge as command.

So the RTL changes:
1. Read path: capture `sram_rdata` 3 cycles after issuing the read command (not 1).
2. Write path: `sram_wdata` must be presented one cycle after the write command (address with CE#/WE#). So wdata must be registered an extra cycle relative to the command.

Also spec section 6.3 changes: first egress beat no later than 10 cycles after last ingress beat (was 4).

// pktbuf.v
//
// Packet buffer between the line-side receive stream and the switch
// interface. Packets arrive on a valid/ready stream, are stored in an
// external synchronous SRAM, and leave on a second valid/ready stream.
// The block behaviour is specified in docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// Written for board rev B, where the SRAM is the NW61F1024 flow-through
// part (docs/NW61F1024_excerpt.md).
//
// This file holds the top level: ingress, the packet descriptor queue,
// buffer space and retry bookkeeping, the SRAM command arbiter and the
// SRAM pins. The read pipeline and the output queue are in
// pktbuf_egress.v.

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,          // data width, also the SRAM word width
    parameter AW = 10           // SRAM address width, 2**AW words
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,           // asynchronous assert, active low

    input  wire          cfg_cut_through, // 0 store-and-forward, 1 cut-through

    // ingress stream
    input  wire          in_valid,
    output wire          in_ready,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] in_data,
    input  wire          in_last,
    input  wire          in_err,          // sampled with in_last only

    // egress stream
    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry,       // sampled with the last beat only

    // status
    output wire [15:0]   drop_count,

    // external SRAM, all outputs driven from flops
    output reg           sram_ce_n,
    output reg           sram_we_n,
    output reg  [AW-1:0] sram_addr,
    output reg  [DW-1:0] sram_wdata,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata
);

    localparam ND  = 8;                         // packet descriptor slots
    localparam NDW = 3;                         // log2(ND)
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}}; // 2**AW words

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Ingress
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg  [AW:0]    wr_ptr;      // address of the next word to write
    reg  [AW:0]    pkt_start;   // first address of the packet being received
    reg  [15:0]    drop_cnt;

    // Packet descriptor queue: the address of each packet's last word and
    // its error flag. In store-and-forward mode an entry means "this packet
    // is complete". In cut-through mode it only marks where a packet ends.
    // Three free-running pointers (one bit wider than the index):
    //   desc_wp    next entry to write
    //   desc_rp    next packet to read from the SRAM
    //   desc_keep  oldest packet not yet released (store-and-forward: the
    //              packet on the egress stream, which may still be retried)
    reg  [AW-1:0]  desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg            desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_rp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_cnt  = desc_wp - desc_rp;     // complete, not yet read
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;   // complete, not yet released

    // Buffer space. Cut-through: a word is free once it has been read.
    // Store-and-forward: a packet's words stay until the packet is released,
    // so that it can be sent again; free_ptr is the first word still held.
    reg  [AW:0]    free_ptr;

    wire [AW:0]    rd_ptr;      // address of the next word to read (egress)
    wire           rd_want;     // egress asks for a read command this cycle
    wire           rd_go;       // ... and gets it
    wire           wr_go;       // an ingress beat is written this cycle
    reg            rr_rd;       // the read wins the next conflict
    wire           pkt_release; // egress: a packet's last beat moved, no retry
    wire           pkt_retry;   // egress: a packet's last beat moved with retry

    wire [AW:0]    used       = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire           can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    // One SRAM command per cycle. When ingress and egress both want the
    // SRAM, they take turns.
    assign in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd);
    assign wr_go    = in_valid && in_ready;
    assign rd_go    = rd_want && !wr_go;

    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
    wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;
    wire pkt_pop;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_ptr    <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            pkt_start <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            drop_cnt  <= 16'd0;
            rr_rd     <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (pkt_drop) begin
                wr_ptr   <= pkt_start;          // forget the whole packet
                drop_cnt <= drop_cnt + 16'd1;
            end else if (wr_go) begin
                wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
                if (in_last)
                    pkt_start <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
            end

            if (wr_go && rd_want)
                rr_rd <= 1'b1;
            else if (rd_go && in_valid && can_accept)
                rr_rd <= 1'b0;
        end
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Descriptor queue, release and retry
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (pkt_push) begin
            desc_end[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            desc_err[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= in_err;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            desc_wp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_rp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_keep <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            free_ptr  <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (pkt_push)
                desc_wp <= desc_wp + 1'b1;

            if (pkt_retry)
                desc_rp <= desc_keep;           // read the packet again
            else if (pkt_pop)
                desc_rp <= desc_rp + 1'b1;

            if (cfg_cut_through) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_rp;
                free_ptr  <= rd_ptr;
            end else if (pkt_release) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_keep + 1'b1;
                free_ptr  <= free_ptr + {1'b0, desc_end[desc_keep[NDW-1:0]] - free_ptr[AW-1:0]} + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    // What the egress may read next.
    wire head_valid = (desc_cnt != 0);
    wire rd_last    = head_valid && (rd_ptr[AW-1:0] == desc_end[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]]);
    wire rd_err     = desc_err[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]];

    // Store-and-forward: only words of complete packets.
    // Cut-through: any word already written.
    wire rd_avail   = cfg_cut_through ? (rd_ptr != wr_ptr) : head_valid;

    assign pkt_pop  = rd_go && rd_last;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // SRAM pins
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            sram_ce_n <= 1'b1;
            sram_we_n <= 1'b1;
        end else begin
            sram_ce_n <= !(wr_go || rd_go);
            sram_we_n <= !wr_go;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go) begin
            sram_addr  <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            sram_wdata <= in_data;
        end else if (rd_go) begin
            sram_addr  <= rd_ptr[AW-1:0];
        end
    end

    assign drop_count = drop_cnt;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Egress
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    pktbuf_egress #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) u_egress (
        .clk         (clk),
        .rst_n       (rst_n),
        .retry_en    (!cfg_cut_through),
        .rd_avail    (rd_avail),
        .rd_last     (rd_last),
        .rd_err      (rd_err),
        .rd_go       (rd_go),
        .rd_want     (rd_want),
        .rd_ptr      (rd_ptr),
        .rd_restart  (free_ptr),
        .pkt_release (pkt_release),
        .pkt_retry   (pkt_retry),
        .sram_rdata  (sram_rdata),
        .out_valid   (out_valid),
        .out_ready   (out_ready),
        .out_data    (out_data),
        .out_last    (out_last),
        .out_err     (out_err),
        .out_retry   (out_retry)
    );

endmodule

cat /app/data/pktbuf_egress.v

// pktbuf_egress.v
//
// Egress half of pktbuf: issues SRAM reads in address order, follows each
// read through the SRAM, queues the returned words for the egress stream,
// and handles a retry request at the end of a packet. See
// docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// Written for board rev B (NW61F1024, flow-through).

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf_egress #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,

    input  wire          retry_en,    // store-and-forward: out_retry is honoured
    input  wire          rd_avail,    // the word at rd_ptr may be read
    input  wire          rd_last,     // ... and is the last of its packet
    input  wire          rd_err,      // ... and that packet had in_err
    input  wire          rd_go,       // the arbiter issues the read this cycle
    output wire          rd_want,
    output reg  [AW:0]   rd_ptr,
    input  wire [AW:0]   rd_restart,  // first word of the packet on the egress stream
    output wire          pkt_release, // a last beat moved, packet done
    output wire          pkt_retry,   // a last beat moved with out_retry: send it again

    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,

    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry
);

    localparam QD = 4;      // output queue entries
    localparam QW = 2;      // log2(QD)

    // Read pipeline, NW61F flow-through:
    //   rd_p0  the read command is on the SRAM pins
    //   rd_p1  the SRAM sampled it at this edge; its data is on sram_rdata
    //          and is captured at the next edge
    reg rd_p0, rd_p1;
    reg tag_last0, tag_last1;
    reg tag_err0,  tag_err1;

    reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_last [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_err  [0:QD-1];
    reg [QW-1:0] q_wp;
    reg [QW-1:0] q_rp;
    reg [QW:0]   q_cnt;

    wire [QW:0] in_flight = {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p0} + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p1};
    wire        q_push    = rd_p1;
    wire        q_pop     = out_valid && out_ready;

    // End of a packet on the egress stream. A retry throws away everything
    // read ahead (queued words and reads in flight) and starts reading the
    // same packet again from its first word.
    wire        last_out  = q_pop && out_last;
    assign pkt_retry   = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
    assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

    // Ask for a read only when its data is sure to find a free entry.
    assign rd_want = rd_avail && ((q_cnt + in_flight) < QD);

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            rd_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            rd_ptr <= rd_restart;
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (rd_go)
                rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1'b1;
            rd_p0 <= rd_go;
            rd_p1 <= rd_p0;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        tag_last0 <= rd_last;
        tag_err0  <= rd_err;
        tag_last1 <= tag_last0;
        tag_err1  <= tag_err0;
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (q_push) begin
            q_data[q_wp] <= sram_rdata;
            q_last[q_wp] <= tag_last1;
            q_err[q_wp]  <= tag_err1 && tag_last1;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            q_wp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_rp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            q_rp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_wp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (q_push)
                q_wp <= q_wp + 1'b1;
            if (q_pop)
                q_rp <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            case ({q_push, q_pop})
                2'b10:   q_cnt <= q_cnt + 1'b1;
                2'b01:   q_cnt <= q_cnt - 1'b1;
                default: q_cnt <= q_cnt;
            endcase
        end
    end

    assign out_valid = (q_cnt != 0);
    assign out_data  = q_data[q_rp];
    assign out_last  = q_last[q_rp];
    assign out_err   = q_err[q_rp];

endmodule

`timescale 1ns/1ps
// Smoke test for pktbuf on board rev B (NW61F1024 flow-through SRAM).
//
// Sends a few packets in store-and-forward mode, then a few in cut-through
// mode, and checks that they come out unchanged. It is a quick sanity check,
// not a regression: no backpressure, no dropped packets, nothing else.
//
// The SRAM model follows docs/NW61F1024_excerpt.md: command, address and
// write data are sampled at the same rising edge; read data is captured by
// the FPGA at the next rising edge.
module tb_smoke;
    localparam DW = 32;
    localparam AW = 10;

    reg clk = 1'b0;
    always #5 clk = ~clk;

    reg           rst_n     = 1'b0;
    reg           cfg_ct    = 1'b0;
    reg           in_valid  = 1'b0;
    reg  [DW-1:0] in_data   = {DW{1'b0}};
    reg           in_last   = 1'b0;
    reg           in_err    = 1'b0;
    reg           out_ready = 1'b1;
    reg           out_retry = 1'b0;
    wire          in_ready, out_valid, out_last, out_err;
    wire [DW-1:0] out_data;
    wire [15:0]   drop_count;
    wire          sram_ce_n, sram_we_n;
    wire [AW-1:0] sram_addr;
    wire [DW-1:0] sram_wdata;
    reg  [DW-1:0] sram_rdata;

    pktbuf #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) dut (
        .clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .cfg_cut_through(cfg_ct),
        .in_valid(in_valid), .in_ready(in_ready), .in_data(in_data),
        .in_last(in_last), .in_err(in_err),
        .out_valid(out_valid), .out_ready(out_ready), .out_data(out_data),
        .out_last(out_last), .out_err(out_err), .out_retry(out_retry),
        .drop_count(drop_count),
        .sram_ce_n(sram_ce_n), .sram_we_n(sram_we_n), .sram_addr(sram_addr),
        .sram_wdata(sram_wdata), .sram_rdata(sram_rdata)
    );

    // NW61F1024 model
    reg [DW-1:0] mem [0:(1<<AW)-1];
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b0)
            mem[sram_addr] <= sram_wdata;
        if (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b1)
            sram_rdata <= mem[sram_addr];
        else
            sram_rdata <= 32'hDEADBEEF;
    end

    // expected beats, in order
    reg [DW-1:0] exp_d [0:1023];
    reg          exp_l [0:1023];
    integer      n_in, n_out, errors, i, p, len;

    // count what comes out
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst_n && out_valid && out_ready) begin
            if (out_data !== exp_d[n_out] || out_last !== exp_l[n_out] || out_err !== 1'b0) begin
                if (errors < 5)
                    $display("smoke: beat %0d: got %h last %b err %b, expected %h last %b",
                             n_out, out_data, out_last, out_err, exp_d[n_out], exp_l[n_out]);
                errors = errors + 1;
            end
            n_out = n_out + 1;
        end
    end

    task send_packet(input integer n);
        integer b;
        begin
            for (b = 0; b < n; b = b + 1) begin
                @(negedge clk);
                in_valid = 1'b1;
                in_data  = {p[7:0], b[7:0], 16'hA5C3} ^ (b * 32'h01000193);
                in_last  = (b == n - 1);
                exp_d[n_in] = in_data;
                exp_l[n_in] = in_last;
                n_in = n_in + 1;
                #1;
                while (in_ready !== 1'b1) begin
                    @(negedge clk);
                    #1;
                end
                @(posedge clk);              // the beat is taken at this edge
            end
            @(negedge clk);
            in_valid = 1'b0;
            in_last  = 1'b0;
        end
    endtask

    task wait_drain;
        integer t;
        begin
            t = 0;
            while (n_out < n_in && t < 2000) begin
                @(posedge clk);
                t = t + 1;
            end
        end
    endtask

    initial begin
        n_in = 0; n_out = 0; errors = 0;
        repeat (4) @(negedge clk);
        rst_n = 1'b1;
        repeat (4) @(negedge clk);

        cfg_ct = 1'b0;                       // store-and-forward
        for (p = 0; p < 6; p = p + 1) begin
            len = 5 + (p * 3) % 8;
            send_packet(len);
        end
        wait_drain;
        repeat (10) @(negedge clk);

        cfg_ct = 1'b1;                       // cut-through
        repeat (10) @(negedge clk);
        for (p = 6; p < 12; p = p + 1) begin
            len = 4 + (p * 5) % 9;
            send_packet(len);
        end
        wait_drain;
        repeat (10) @(negedge clk);

        if (n_out != n_in)
            $display("smoke: %0d beats sent, %0d received", n_in, n_out);
        if (errors == 0 && n_out == n_in && drop_count == 16'd0)
            $display("SMOKE PASS: %0d packets, %0d beats", p, n_in);
        else
            $display("SMOKE FAIL: %0d mismatches", errors);
        $finish;
    end

endmodule
# pktbuf smoke test (board rev B SRAM model).
#   make            Icarus Verilog
#   make verilator  the same bench on Verilator, random power-up state
#   make clean
# Exits non-zero unless the bench prints SMOKE PASS.

SRC   = pktbuf.v pktbuf_egress.v
TB    = tb/tb_smoke.v
BUILD = build

.PHONY: all sim verilator clean

all: sim

sim: $(SRC) $(TB)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	@iverilog -g2012 -o $(BUILD)/smoke.vvp -s tb_smoke $(SRC) $(TB)
	@vvp -n $(BUILD)/smoke.vvp | tee $(BUILD)/smoke.log
	@grep -q "SMOKE PASS" $(BUILD)/smoke.log

verilator: $(SRC) $(TB)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	@verilator --binary --timing -Wno-fatal -Wno-lint -Wno-style --timescale 1ns/1ps \
		--x-initial unique --x-assign unique --top-module tb_smoke \
		-Mdir $(BUILD)/vl -o vsim $(SRC) $(TB) > $(BUILD)/verilator.log 2>&1 \
		|| (tail -20 $(BUILD)/verilator.log; exit 1)
	@$(BUILD)/vl/vsim +verilator+rand+reset+2 | tee $(BUILD)/smoke_vl.log
	@grep -q "SMOKE PASS" $(BUILD)/smoke_vl.log

clean:
	@rm -rf $(BUILD)

   ```verilog

   module pktbuf #(
       parameter DW = 32,
       parameter AW = 10
   ) (
       ... unchanged ports ...
   );

       localparam ND  = 8;
       localparam NDW = 3;
       localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}};

       // ingress
       reg  [AW:0]  wr_ptr;
       reg  [AW:0]  pkt_start;
       reg  [15:0]  drop_cnt;

       reg  [AW-1:0] desc_end [0:ND-1];
       reg           desc_err [0:ND-1];
       reg  [NDW:0]  desc_wp;
       reg  [NDW:0]  desc_rp;
       reg  [NDW:0]  desc_keep;
       reg  [NDW:0]  desc_wp_d1, desc_wp_d2;   // S&F: complete packets visible to the read side 2 cycles late (NW61P late write: a word may be read no sooner than 3 command edges after its write command)

       reg  [AW:0]   free_ptr;
       reg  [AW:0]   ct_rdy;      // cut-through: written, aged, not bypassed, not yet read
       reg           ring_go_d1, ring_go_d2;

       wire [AW:0]  rd_ptr;
       wire         rd_want, rd_go, wr_go;
       reg          rr_rd;
       wire         pkt_release, pkt_retry;

       wire [AW:0]  used = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
       wire         can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);
       wire [NDW:0] desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;

       assign in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd);
       assign wr_go = in_valid && in_ready;
       assign rd_go = rd_want && !wr_go;

       wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
       wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;

       // bypass
       wire eg_idle;
       wire bypass_ok = cfg_cut_through && eg_idle && (rd_ptr == wr_ptr);
       wire bypass_go = bypass_ok && wr_go;
       wire ring_go  = cfg_cut_through && wr_go && !bypass_go;   // word committed to the ring (CT)

       wire pkt_pop = (rd_go && rd_last) || (bypass_go && in_last);
       ...
   ```

   ```verilog

       clk, rst_n, retry_en, rd_avail, rd_last, rd_err, rd_go, rd_want, rd_ptr, rd_restart,
       pkt_release, pkt_retry,
       bypass_go, in_data, in_last, in_err, eg_idle,
       sram_rdata, out_valid, out_ready, out_data, out_last, out_err, out_retry
   );
       localparam QD = 8;
       localparam QW = 3;

       reg rd_p0, rd_p1, rd_p2, rd_p3;
       reg tlast0..3, terr0..3;
       reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
       reg q_last [0:QD-1];
       reg q_err [0:QD-1];
       reg [QW-1:0] q_wp, q_rp;
       reg [QW:0] q_cnt;

       reg fwd_valid; reg [DW-1:0] fwd_data; reg fwd_last, fwd_err;

       wire [2:0] in_flight = p0+p1+p2+p3;
       wire [4:0] committed = {1'b0,q_cnt} + {2'b00,in_flight};
       assign rd_want = rd_avail && (committed < QD);   // QD=8: 5-bit compare ok

       out_valid = fwd_valid || (q_cnt != 0);
       out_data = fwd_valid ? fwd_data : q_data[q_rp];
       out_last = fwd_valid ? fwd_last : q_last[q_rp];
       out_err  = fwd_valid ? fwd_err  : q_err[q_rp];
       beat = out_valid && out_ready;
       fwd_pop = beat && fwd_valid;
       q_pop = beat && !fwd_valid;
       last_out = beat && out_last;
       pkt_retry = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
       pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;
       eg_idle = (q_cnt == 0) && (in_flight == 0) && (!fwd_valid || fwd_pop);

       q_push = rd_p3;

       rd_ptr/pipe always:
       if (!rst_n) {rd_ptr, p0..p3} <= 0
       else if (pkt_retry) {rd_ptr <= rd_restart; p<=0;}
       else begin
           if (rd_go) rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1;
           else if (bypass_go) rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1;   // hmm both can't happen same cycle — bypass requires idle incl. no... rd_go requires rd_avail=ct_rdy!=0; bypass requires rd_ptr==wr_ptr & idle.            p0 <= rd_go; p1 <= p0; p2 <= p1; p3 <= p2;
       end

       tags: tlast0 <= rd_last; ... shift; (unconditional, unreset — hmm, rev B unreset; keep)

       q write:
       always @(posedge clk) if (q_push) begin
           q_data[q_wp] <= sram_rdata; q_last[q_wp] <= tlast3; q_err[q_wp] <= terr3 && tlast3;
       end

       q pointers:
       if (!rst_n) {q_wp,q_rp,q_cnt} <= 0
       else if (pkt_retry) begin q_rp <= q_rp + 1; q_wp <= q_rp + 1; q_cnt <= 0; end
       else begin
           if (q_push) q_wp <= q_wp + 1;
           if (q_pop) q_rp <= q_rp + 1;
           case ({q_push, q_pop}) 10: +1; 01: -1; default: hold;
       end

       fwd:
       always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)
           if (!rst_n) fwd_valid <= 0;
           else if (pkt_retry) fwd_valid <= 0;   // safety; S&F only
           else if (bypass_go) fwd_valid <= 1;
           else if (fwd_pop) fwd_valid <= 0;
       always @(posedge clk) if (bypass_go) begin
           fwd_data <= in_data; fwd_last <= in_last; fwd_err <= in_last && in_err;
       end
   endmodule
   ```

   ```verilog
   // pktbuf.v
   // ... header comment updated for rev C ...
   `timescale 1ns/1ps

   module pktbuf #(
       parameter DW = 32,
       parameter AW = 10
   ) (
       input  wire          clk,
       input  wire          rst_n,
       input  wire          cfg_cut_through,
       input  wire          in_valid,
       output wire          in_ready,
       input  wire [DW-1:0] in_data,
       input  wire          in_last,
       input  wire          in_err,
       output wire          out_valid,
       input  wire          out_ready,
       output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
       output wire          out_last,
       output wire          out_err,
       input  wire          out_retry,
       output wire [15:0]   drop_count,
       output reg           sram_ce_n,
       output reg           sram_we_n,
       output reg  [AW-1:0] sram_addr,
       output reg  [DW-1:0] sram_wdata,
       input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata
   );

       localparam ND  = 8;
       localparam NDW = 3;
       localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}};

       reg  [AW:0]    wr_ptr;
       reg  [AW:0]    pkt_start;
       reg  [15:0]    drop_cnt;

       reg  [AW-1:0]  desc_end [0:ND-1];
       reg            desc_err [0:ND-1];
       reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp;
       reg  [NDW:0]   desc_rp;
       reg  [NDW:0]   desc_keep;
       reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp_d1;
       reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp_d2;

       reg  [AW:0]    free_ptr;

       // Cut-through ring availability: words committed to the SRAM ring,
       // old enough to read (NW61P late write lands three command edges
       // before a read of the same word may be issued) and not yet read.
       reg  [AW:0]    ct_rdy;
       reg            ring_go_d1;
       reg            ring_go_d2;

       wire [AW:0]    rd_ptr;
       wire           rd_want;
       wire           rd_go;
       wire           wr_go;
       reg            rr_rd;
       wire           pkt_release;
       wire           pkt_retry;

       wire [NDW:0]   desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;
       wire [AW:0]    used       = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
       wire           can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

       assign in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd);
       assign wr_go    = in_valid && in_ready;
       assign rd_go    = rd_want && !wr_go;

       wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
       wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;

       // Cut-through bypass: with the egress side caught up (nothing queued,
       // no read in flight, ring drained) an incoming beat is forwarded
       // straight to the output register, skipping the SRAM read path.
       // The word is still written to the SRAM; rd_ptr steps over it.
       wire           eg_idle;
       wire           bypass_go = cfg_cut_through && wr_go && eg_idle && (rd_ptr == wr_ptr);
       wire           ring_go   = cfg_cut_through && wr_go && !bypass_go;

       // ... rd_last etc. need declaring before pkt_pop
       wire [NDW:0]  desc_cnt    = desc_wp - desc_rp;   // hmm CT head
       wire          head_valid_sf = (desc_wp_d2 != desc_rp);
       wire          head_valid_ct = (desc_wp    != desc_rp);
       wire          rd_avail      = cfg_cut_through ? (ct_rdy != {(AW+1){1'b0}}) : head_valid_sf;
       wire          head_valid_rd = cfg_cut_through ? head_valid_ct : head_valid_sf;
       wire          rd_last = head_valid_rd && (rd_ptr[AW-1:0] == desc_end[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]]);
       wire          rd_err  = desc_err[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]];

       wire          pkt_pop = (rd_go && rd_last) || (bypass_go && in_last);
       ...
   ```

   ```verilog
   // pktbuf_egress.v — rev C: NW61P1024 pipelined SRAM, LAT=H (RL=3), late write.
   `timescale 1ns/1ps

   module pktbuf_egress #(
       parameter DW = 32,
       parameter AW = 10
   ) (
       input  wire          clk,
       input  wire          rst_n,
       input  wire          retry_en,
       input  wire          rd_avail,
       input  wire          rd_last,
       input  wire          rd_err,
       input  wire          rd_go,
       output wire          rd_want,
       output reg  [AW:0]   rd_ptr,
       input  wire [AW:0]   rd_restart,
       output wire          pkt_release,
       output wire          pkt_retry,
       input  wire          bypass_go,
       input  wire [DW-1:0] in_data,
       input  wire          in_last,
       input  wire          in_err,
       output wire          eg_idle,
       input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,
       output wire          out_valid,
       input  wire          out_ready,
       output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
       output wire          out_last,
       output wire          out_err,
       input  wire          out_retry
   );

       localparam QD = 8;
       localparam QW = 3;

       // Read pipeline, NW61P pipelined read, RL = 3 (LAT strapped high on
       // rev C, ECO-117):
       //   rd_p0  the read command is on the SRAM pins
       //   rd_p1  the SRAM sampled it at this edge
       //   rd_p2  array read latency
       //   rd_p3  the data is on sram_rdata and is captured at this edge
       reg rd_p0, rd_p1, rd_p2, rd_p3;
       reg tag_last0, tag_last1, tag_last2, tag_last3;
       reg tag_err0,  tag_err1,  tag_err2,  tag_err3;

       reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
       reg          q_last [0:QD-1];
       reg          q_err  [0:QD-1];
       reg [QW-1:0] q_wp;
       reg [QW-1:0] q_rp;
       reg [QW:0]   q_cnt;

       // Forward register: cut-through beats that skip the SRAM read path.
       reg          fwd_valid;
       reg [DW-1:0] fwd_data;
       reg          fwd_last;
       reg          fwd_err;

       wire [2:0] in_flight = {2'b00, rd_p0} + {2'b00, rd_p1} + {2'b00, rd_p2} + {2'b00, rd_p3};
       wire [4:0] committed = {1'b0, q_cnt} + {2'b00, in_flight};
       wire       q_push    = rd_p3;

       assign rd_want = rd_avail && (committed < QD);

       assign out_valid = fwd_valid || (q_cnt != 0);
       assign out_data  = fwd_valid ? fwd_data : q_data[q_rp];
       assign out_last  = fwd_valid ? fwd_last : q_last[q_rp];
       assign out_err   = fwd_valid ? fwd_err  : q_err[q_rp];

       wire beat_move = out_valid && out_ready;
       wire fwd_pop   = beat_move && fwd_valid;
       wire q_pop     = beat_move && !fwd_valid;
       wire last_out  = beat_move && out_last;

       assign pkt_retry   = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
       assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

       assign eg_idle = (q_cnt == 0) && (in_flight == 0) && (!fwd_valid || fwd_pop);

       always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
           if (!rst_n) begin
               rd_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
               rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
               rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
               rd_p2  <= 1'b0;
               rd_p3  <= 1'b0;
           end else if (pkt_retry) begin
               rd_ptr <= rd_restart;
               rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
               rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
               rd_p2  <= 1'b0;
               rd_p3  <= 1'b0;
           end else begin
               if (rd_go || bypass_go)
                   rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1'b1;
               rd_p0 <= rd_go;
               rd_p1 <= rd_p0;
               rd_p2 <= rd_p1;
               rd_p3 <= rd_p2;
           end
       end

       always @(posedge clk) begin
           tag_last0 <= rd_last;
           tag_err0  <= rd_err;
           tag_last1 <= tag_last0;
           tag_err1  <= tag_err0;
           tag_last2 <= tag_last1;
           tag_err2  <= tag_err1;
           tag_last3 <= tag_last2;
           tag_err3  <= tag_err2;
       end

       always @(posedge clk) begin
           if (q_push) begin
               q_data[q_wp] <= sram_rdata;
               q_last[q_wp] <= tag_last3;
               q_err[q_wp]  <= tag_err3 && tag_last3;
           end
       end

       always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
           if (!rst_n) begin
               q_wp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
               q_rp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
               q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
           end else if (pkt_retry) begin
               q_rp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
               q_wp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
               q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
           end else begin
               if (q_push)
                   q_wp <= q_wp + 1'b1;
               if (q_pop)
                   q_rp <= q_rp + 1'b1;
               case ({q_push, q_pop})
                   2'b10:   q_cnt <= q_cnt + 1'b1;
                   2'b01:   q_cnt <= q_cnt - 1'b1;
                   default: q_cnt <= q_cnt;
               endcase
           end
       end

       always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
           if (!rst_n)
               fwd_valid <= 1'b0;
           else if (pkt_retry)
               fwd_valid <= 1'b0;
           else if (bypass_go)
               fwd_valid <= 1'b1;
           else if (fwd_pop)
               fwd_valid <= 1'b0;
       end

       always @(posedge clk) begin
           if (bypass_go) begin
               fwd_data <= in_data;
               fwd_last <= in_last;
               fwd_err  <= in_last && in_err;
           end
       end

   endmodule
   ```

   SRAM model (rev C, RL=3, late write, hazard):
   ```
   reg [DW-1:0] mem [0:(1<<AW)-1];
   // write side
   reg               wr1;      // write cmd sampled last edge
   reg  [AW-1:0]     wr1_addr;
   reg               wr2;      // data sampled, commit this edge
   reg  [AW-1:0]     wr2_addr;
   reg  [DW-1:0]     wr2_data;
   // read side
   reg               rd1, rd2;
   reg  [DW-1:0]     rd1_d, rd2_d;
   reg  [DW-1:0]     sram_rdata;
   wire cmd_wr = (sram_ce_n == 1'b0) && (sram_we_n == 1'b0);
   wire cmd_rd = (sram_ce_n == 1'b0) && (sram_we_n == 1'b1);
   always @(posedge clk) begin
       // stage 1: command at edge n
       wr1 <= cmd_wr;
       if (cmd_wr) wr1_addr <= sram_addr;
       // stage 2: D sampled at edge n+1, commit at edge n+2 (read at n+2 sees old)
       wr2 <= wr1;
       if (wr1) begin wr2_addr <= wr1_addr; wr2_data <= sram_wdata; end
       if (wr2) mem[wr2_addr] <= wr2_data;
       // read: sample array at command edge, Q valid at edge n+3
       rd1 <= cmd_rd;
       if (cmd_rd) rd1_d <= mem[sram_addr];
       rd2 <= rd1; rd2_d <= rd1_d;
       if (rd2) sram_rdata <= rd2_d;
       else     sram_rdata <= {$random};   // undefined outside the data cycle
   end
   ```
   Check timing: cmd_rd at edge n → rd1 visible n+1, rd2 at n+2, rdata assigned at edge n+2 (if rd2 sampled at n+2... wait: rd2 <= rd1 at edge n+1 → rd2 visible n+2 → `if (rd2)` at edge n+2 TRUE → sram_rdata <= rd2_d at edge n+2 → visible cycle n+3 → DUT samples at edge n+3 ✓✓. The ECR says 6.4 unchanged ("fixed by the switch"), so the design MUST bypass: when the egress is at the head of a just-arriving packet (cut-through, block was empty), deliver words from the ingress stream directly.

How to implement bypass cleanly: in cut-through mode, when rd_ptr == wr_ptr-ish (the next word to read is the one being accepted NOW or not yet committed), push the incoming data directly into the output queue instead of waiting for the SRAM read.

```verilog
// pktbuf.v (rev C)
`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    ... same ports ...
);

    localparam ND  = 8;
    localparam NDW = 3;
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}};

    // ingress
    reg [AW:0] wr_ptr;
    reg [AW:0] pkt_start;
    reg [15:0] drop_cnt;

    // late-write pipeline: beat accepted -> write command 1 cycle later
    // on the pins, write data the cycle after that.
    reg          wr_d0;        // write command on the pins this cycle
    reg          wr_d1;        // write data on the pins this cycle
    reg          wr_buf_v;
    reg [AW-1:0] wr_addr_buf;
    reg [DW-1:0] wr_data_buf;

    // acceptance delay line: wpd3 is wr_ptr as it was 4 clocks ago.  A
    // read command for a word is issued only once the word's write
    // command is at least three SRAM cycles behind the read command
    // (NW61P1024 late write: a read sees a write whose command edge is
    // >= 3 cycles earlier).
    reg [AW:0] wpd0, wpd1, wpd2, wpd3;

    // descriptors ... same as rev B
    reg [AW-1:0] desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg [NDW:0] desc_wp, desc_rp, desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0] desc_cnt = desc_wp - desc_rp;
    wire [NDW:0] desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;

    reg [AW:0] free_ptr;

    wire [AW:0] rd_ptr;
    wire rd_want, rd_go, wr_go;
    reg rr_rd;
    wire pkt_release, pkt_retry;
    wire bypass;

    wire [AW:0] used = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    assign in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd);
    assign wr_go = in_valid && in_ready;
    assign rd_go = rd_want && !wr_go;

    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
    wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;
    wire pkt_pop;
    wire bypass_last = bypass && in_last;
```

Top file (pktbuf.v) full text:

```verilog
// pktbuf.v
//
// Packet buffer ... Board rev C: NW61P1024 pipelined SRAM, LAT strapped
// high (read latency 3), late write (D one cycle after the command).
// See docs/ECR-0412_pktbuf_rev_c.md, docs/NW61P1024_excerpt.md,
// docs/board_rev_c_notes.md.
//
// Rev C timing changes versus rev B:
//  - write data is registered and driven one cycle after the write
//    command (late write);
//  - read data is captured three cycles after the read command;
//  - a read command is only issued for a word whose write command is at
//    least three cycles older (wpd* delay line), because a read within
//    two cycles of the write command returns the old word;
//  - in cut-through mode a word that arrives while the egress side has
//    caught up (nothing queued or in flight) is forwarded straight to
//    the output queue (bypass), so the first-beat latency of section
//    6.4 is met despite the longer SRAM loop.

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    ...ports identical...
);

    localparam ND  = 8;
    localparam NDW = 3;
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}};

    reg  [AW:0]  wr_ptr;
    reg  [AW:0]  pkt_start;
    reg  [15:0]  drop_cnt;

    reg  [AW-1:0] desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg          desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg  [NDW:0] desc_wp;
    reg  [NDW:0] desc_rp;
    reg  [NDW:0] desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0] desc_cnt  = desc_wp - desc_rp;
    wire [NDW:0] desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;

    reg  [AW:0]  free_ptr;

    // wpd3: wr_ptr four clocks ago (flushed to pkt_start on a drop).
    reg  [AW:0]  wpd0, wpd1, wpd2, wpd3;

    // late-write data path
    reg  [DW-1:0] wdata_buf;
    reg           wdata_pend;

    wire [AW:0]  rd_ptr;
    wire        rd_want;
    wire        rd_go;
    wire        wr_go;
    reg         rr_rd;
    wire        pkt_release;
    wire        pkt_retry;
    wire        bypass;

    wire [AW:0] used = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire       can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    assign in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd);
    assign wr_go = in_valid && in_ready;
    assign rd_go = rd_want && !wr_go;

    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
    wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;
    wire pkt_pop;
    wire bypass_last = bypass && in_last;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            pkt_start <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            drop_cnt <= 16'd0;
            rr_rd <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (pkt_drop) begin
                wr_ptr <= pkt_start;
                drop_cnt <= drop_cnt + 16'd1;
            end else if (wr_go) begin
                wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
                if (in_last)
                    pkt_start <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
            end
            if (wr_go && rd_want)
                rr_rd <= 1'b1;
            else if (rd_go && in_valid && can_accept)
                rr_rd <= 1'b0;
        end
    end

    // acceptance age delay line
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wpd0 <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            wpd1 <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            wpd2 <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            wpd3 <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
        end else if (pkt_drop) begin
            wpd0 <= pkt_start;
            wpd1 <= pkt_start;
            wpd2 <= pkt_start;
            wpd3 <= pkt_start;
        end else begin
            wpd0 <= wr_ptr;
            wpd1 <= wpd0;
            wpd2 <= wpd1;
            wpd3 <= wpd2;
        end
    end

    // descriptors (same as rev B)
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (pkt_push) begin
            desc_end[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            desc_err[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= in_err;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            desc_wp <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_rp <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_keep <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            free_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (pkt_push)
                desc_wp <= desc_wp + 1'b1;
            if (pkt_retry)
                desc_rp <= desc_keep;
            else if (pkt_pop || bypass_last)
                desc_rp <= desc_rp + 1'b1;
            if (cfg_cut_through) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_rp;
                free_ptr <= rd_ptr;
            end else if (pkt_release) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_keep + 1'b1;
                free_ptr <= free_ptr + {1'b0, desc_end[desc_keep[NDW-1:0]] - free_ptr[AW-1:0]} + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    wire head_valid = (desc_cnt != 0);
    wire rd_last = head_valid && (rd_ptr[AW-1:0] == desc_end[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]]);
    wire rd_err  = desc_err[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]];
    wire rd_avail = (cfg_cut_through || head_valid) &&
                    (rd_ptr != wpd3) && (rd_ptr != wr_ptr);

    assign pkt_pop = rd_go && rd_last;

    // SRAM pins: command one cycle after the request, write data one
    // cycle after the write command (late write).
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            sram_ce_n <= 1'b1;
            sram_we_n <= 1'b1;
            wdata_pend <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            sram_ce_n <= !(wr_go || rd_go);
            sram_we_n <= !wr_go;
            wdata_pend <= wr_go;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go) begin
            sram_addr <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            wdata_buf <= in_data;
        end else if (rd_go) begin
            sram_addr <= rd_ptr[AW-1:0];
        end
        if (wdata_pend)
            sram_wdata <= wdata_buf;
    end

    assign drop_count = drop_cnt;

    pktbuf_egress #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) u_egress (
        .clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n),
        .retry_en(!cfg_cut_through),
        .rd_avail(rd_avail), .rd_last(rd_last), .rd_err(rd_err),
        .rd_go(rd_go), .rd_want(rd_want), .rd_ptr(rd_ptr),
        .rd_restart(free_ptr),
        .pkt_release(pkt_release), .pkt_retry(pkt_retry),
        .wr_go(wr_go), .wr_ptr(wr_ptr),
        .in_data(in_data), .in_last(in_last), .in_err(in_err),
        .bypass(bypass),
        .sram_rdata(sram_rdata),
        .out_valid(out_valid), .out_ready(out_ready),
        .out_data(out_data), .out_last(out_last), .out_err(out_err),
        .out_retry(out_retry)
    );

endmodule
```

WAIT — problem: `wdata_pend <= wr_go` and `sram_wdata <= wdata_buf if wdata_pend`: at end of t: wdata_pend(t+1)=wr_go(t); wdata_buf(t+1)=in_data(t). During cycle t+1: wdata_pend=1 → at end of t+1: sram_wdata(t+2) = wdata_buf(t+1) = in_data(t) ✓ D valid cycle t+2, cmd cycle t+1 ✓✓.

Hmm — but one bug: `sram_addr` on read when wr_go false ✓; and when neither, addr holds ✓ fine.

Another check: sram_we_n(t+1) = !wr_go(t) — if rd_go(t) also... wr_go/rd_go exclusive ✓. If NEITHER: ce_n high, we_n = 1 ✓ don't care.
