Egress file:

```verilog
// pktbuf_egress.v — rev C
`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf_egress #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire retry_en,
    input wire rd_avail,
    input wire rd_last,
    input wire rd_err,
    input wire rd_go,
    output wire rd_want,
    output reg [AW:0] rd_ptr,
    input wire [AW:0] rd_restart,
    output wire pkt_release,
    output wire pkt_retry,

    // ingress side, for the cut-through bypass
    input wire wr_go,
    input wire [AW:0] wr_ptr,
    input wire [DW-1:0] in_data,
    input wire in_last,
    input wire in_err,
    output wire bypass,

    input wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,

    output wire out_valid,
    input wire out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire out_last,
    output wire out_err,
    input wire out_retry
);

    localparam QD = 4;
    localparam QW = 2;

    // NW61P1024, LAT = H: read command on the pins (rd_p0), data
    // captured three cycles after the command edge (rd_p3).
    reg rd_p0, rd_p1, rd_p2, rd_p3;
    reg tag_last0, tag_last1, tag_last2, tag_last3;
    reg tag_err0, tag_err1, tag_err2, tag_err3;

    reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
    reg q_last [0:QD-1];
    reg q_err [0:QD-1];
    reg [QW-1:0] q_wp;
    reg [QW-1:0] q_rp;
    reg [QW:0] q_cnt;

    wire [QW:0] in_flight = {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p0} + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p1}
                          + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p2} + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p3};
    wire [QW+1:0] occ = {1'b0, q_cnt} + {1'b0, in_flight};
    wire q_pop = out_valid && out_ready;

    wire last_out = q_pop && out_last;
    assign pkt_retry = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
    assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

    assign rd_want = rd_avail && (occ < QD);

    // Cut-through bypass: the egress side has caught up with the
    // ingress stream and the queue is (about to be) empty, so this
    // word goes straight to the output queue without an SRAM read.
    assign bypass = !retry_en && wr_go && (rd_ptr == wr_ptr) &&
                    (occ == {{(QW+1){1'b0}}, q_pop});

    wire q_push = rd_p3 || bypass;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            rd_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            rd_p0 <= 1'b0; rd_p1 <= 1'b0; rd_p2 <= 1'b0; rd_p3 <= 1'b0;
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            rd_ptr <= rd_restart;
            rd_p0 <= 1'b0; rd_p1 <= 1'b0; rd_p2 <= 1'b0; rd_p3 <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (rd_go || bypass)
                rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1'b1;
            rd_p0 <= rd_go;
            rd_p1 <= rd_p0;
            rd_p2 <= rd_p1;
            rd_p3 <= rd_p2;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        tag_last0 <= rd_last;
```

The ILA capture confirms the rev C SRAM timing precisely:
- **Read latency = 3** (LAT strapped H per ECO-117): read cmd at edge n → data valid in cycle n+3
- **Late write**: write cmd at edge n, D sampled at edge n+1
- **Array-write visibility**: write cmd at n becomes visible to reads at cmd edge ≥ n+3 (write@92→read@94 returns OLD, write@119→read@122 returns NEW)

Key consequences: the read pipeline must stretch to 3 cycles, reads must be ≥3 cmd-edges after the write of the same word, and cut-through's 5-cycle first-beat budget (6.4, unchanged by the ECR) is impossible through the SRAM loop (accept→write cmd→+3→read cmd→+3 data = 8 cycles) — so a **bypass path** is required for cut-through when the egress has caught up.

```verilog
// pktbuf.v  ... header comment: rev C, NW61P1024 pipelined late-write, RL=3
`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) ( ... same ports ... );

    localparam ND  = 8;
    localparam NDW = 3;
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}};

    // ingress
    reg  [AW:0]  wr_ptr;
    reg  [AW:0]  pkt_start;
    reg  [15:0]  drop_cnt;

    reg  [AW-1:0] desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg            desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_rp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_cnt  = desc_wp - desc_rp;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;

    reg  [AW:0]    free_ptr;
    reg  [AW:0]    rd_ptr;       // next word to read (last issued + 1)

    reg            rr_rd;
    wire           rd_want;
    wire           rd_go;
    wire           wr_go;
    wire           pkt_release;
    wire           pkt_retry;

    wire [AW:0]    used       = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire           can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    assign in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd);
    assign wr_go    = in_valid && in_ready;

    // ---- read order guard (late write: write cmd at edge n visible to
    // ---- reads at edge n+3; a read cmd is sampled one edge after rd_go)
    reg          wr_g1, wr_g2;
    reg [AW-1:0] wr_a1, wr_a2;
    wire rd_hazard = (wr_g1 && (wr_a1 == rd_ptr[AW-1:0])) ||
                     (wr_g2 && (wr_a2 == rd_ptr[AW-1:0]));
    assign rd_go = rd_want && !rd_hazard && !wr_go;

    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
    wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;
    wire pkt_pop  = rd_go && rd_last;
    wire bp_pop   = bp_take && in_last;   // bypassed last beat: descriptor consumed
```

Hmm wait — bp_take comes from egress; in_last is a top port ✓.

```verilog
    wire rd_err     = desc_err[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]];
    wire rd_avail   = cfg_cut_through ? (rd_ptr != wr_ptr) : head_valid;
```

```verilog
`timescale 1ns/1ps
module pktbuf_egress #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,
    input  wire          retry_en,
    // read-ahead bookkeeping (top)
    input  wire [2:0]    in_flight,   // reads issued, data not yet back
    input  wire          q_push_i,    // read data returns this edge
    input  wire          q_push_last,
    input  wire          q_push_err,
    output wire          q_room,      // a further read can be issued
    // bypass (cut-through): beat accepted while the egress side is empty
    input  wire          bp_wr_go,    // wr_go
    input  wire          bp_wr_eq,    // rd_ptr == wr_ptr
    input  wire [DW-1:0] bp_wdata,    // in_data
    input  wire          bp_wlast,    // in_last
    input  wire          bp_werr,     // in_err
    output wire          bp_take,
    // status events
    output wire          pkt_release,
    output wire          pkt_retry,
    // SRAM read data
    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,
    // egress stream
    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry
);

    localparam QD = 8;
    localparam QW = 3;

    reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_last [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_err  [0:QD-1];
    reg [QW-1:0] q_wp;
    reg [QW-1:0] q_rp;
    reg [QW:0]   q_cnt;

    reg          bp_valid;
    reg [DW-1:0] bp_data;
    reg          bp_last;
    reg          bp_err;

    wire q_pop = out_valid && out_ready;
    wire last_out = q_pop && out_last;
    assign pkt_retry   = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
    assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

    wire [4:0] room_sum = {1'b0, q_cnt} + {2'b00, in_flight};
    assign q_room = (room_sum < QD);

    wire bp_move = bp_valid && out_ready;
    assign bp_take = bp_wr_go && !retry_en && bp_wr_eq &&
                     (q_cnt == 0) && (in_flight == 0) &&
                     (!bp_valid || out_ready);
```

```verilog
    // NW61P1024 model, LAT=H: read latency 3, late write.
    reg [DW-1:0] mem [0:(1<<AW)-1];
    // write: cmd at edge n (addr), D at edge n+1, array updated at edge n+2 (NBA)
    reg         w_p;
    reg [AW-1:0] w_a;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        w_p <= (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b0);
        if (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b0) w_a <= sram_addr;

    end
```
Check: cmd at edge n: w_p set (during n+1); at edge n+1: w_p=1 → mem[w_a] <= sram_wdata (D at edge n+1 ✓) — NBA at edge n+1: mem updated after edge n+1 → visible to reads sampling at edge ≥ n+2.
```verilog
    reg         w_p0, w_p1;
    reg [AW-1:0] w_a0, w_a1;
    reg [DW-1:0] w_d1;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        w_p0 <= (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b0);
        if (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b0) w_a0 <= sram_addr;
        w_p1 <= w_p0;
        if (w_p0) begin w_a1 <= w_a0; w_d1 <= sram_wdata; end
        if (w_p1) mem[w_a1] <= w_d1;
    end
```

- **Read pipeline stretched to 3 cycles** (RL=3), commit when data actually returns (no optimistic commit needed — first beat lands at t+6..t+8 ≤ t+10 budget)
- **Late-write data pipeline**: `in_data_r` → `sram_wdata` one cycle after the write command
- **Read/write ordering guard**: block a read for 2 cycles after a write to the same address (ILA: write@n visible only from read cmd edge n+3)
- **Cut-through bypass register**: when egress has caught up (`q` empty, nothing in flight, `rd_ptr==wr_ptr`), hand the incoming beat straight to the output — meets the fixed 5-cycle 6.4 budget with margin, at full line rate
- Retry stays a clean full flush + rewind (as rev B)

→ bash exit 0 1.7s

cat > /app/data/pktbuf.v <<'EOF'
// pktbuf.v
//
// Packet buffer between the line-side receive stream and the switch
// interface. Packets arrive on a valid/ready stream, are stored in an
// external synchronous SRAM, and leave on a second valid/ready stream.
// The block behaviour is specified in docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// Board rev C (ECR-0412): the buffer SRAM is the NW61P1024, a pipelined
// part with late write (docs/NW61P1024_excerpt.md), strapped LAT = H on
// every rev C board (ECO-117), so the read latency is 3 cycles:
//   - a read command is sampled by the SRAM one clock edge after rd_go
//     and its data is captured three edges after the command edge;
//   - a write command is sampled one clock edge after wr_go and its data
//     (D) is sampled one edge after the command, so sram_wdata is the
//     accepted beat delayed by two pipeline stages;
//   - a write becomes visible to reads of the same address only three
//     command edges after the write command (see docs/ila_sram_sn0007.csv),
//     so a read of a just-written word is held off for two edges.
//
// This file holds the top level: ingress, the packet descriptor queue,
// buffer space and retry bookkeeping, the SRAM command arbiter, the read
// command pipeline and the SRAM pins. The output queue, the cut-through
// bypass register and the retry handling are in pktbuf_egress.v.

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,          // data width, also the SRAM word width
    parameter AW = 10           // SRAM address width, 2**AW words
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,           // asynchronous assert, active low

    input  wire          cfg_cut_through, // 0 store-and-forward, 1 cut-through

    // ingress stream
    input  wire          in_valid,
    output wire          in_ready,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] in_data,
    input  wire          in_last,
    input  wire          in_err,          // sampled with in_last only

    // egress stream
    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry,       // sampled with the last beat only

    // status
    output wire [15:0]   drop_count,

    // external SRAM, all outputs driven from flops
    output reg           sram_ce_n,
    output reg           sram_we_n,
    output reg  [AW-1:0] sram_addr,
    output reg  [DW-1:0] sram_wdata,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata
);

    localparam ND  = 8;                         // packet descriptor slots
    localparam NDW = 3;                         // log2(ND)
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}}; // 2**AW words

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Ingress
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg  [AW:0]    wr_ptr;      // address of the next word to write
    reg  [AW:0]    pkt_start;   // first address of the packet being received
    reg  [15:0]    drop_cnt;

    // Packet descriptor queue, as on rev B. desc_rp now advances when the
    // last read of a packet is issued; desc_keep still marks the oldest
    // packet not yet released.
    reg  [AW-1:0]  desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg            desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_rp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_cnt  = desc_wp - desc_rp;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;

    reg  [AW:0]    free_ptr;
    reg  [AW:0]    rd_ptr;      // next word to read from the SRAM

    reg            rr_rd;       // the read wins the next conflict
    wire           rd_want;
    wire           rd_go;
    wire           wr_go;
    wire           rd_hazard;
    wire           q_room;
    wire           bp_take;
    wire           pkt_release;
    wire           pkt_retry;

    wire [AW:0]    used       = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire           can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    assign in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd);
    assign wr_go    = in_valid && in_ready;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Read/write order guard. A write command sampled at edge n is not
    // visible to a read of the same address sampled before edge n+3.
    // rd_go at edge z puts a read command on the pins in cycle z+1, sampled
    // at edge z+1, so it must not target an address whose write command
    // was sampled at edge z or z-1: wr_g1/wr_a1 is the write command
    // sampled at this edge, wr_g2/wr_a2 the one sampled at the last edge.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg          wr_g1, wr_g2;
    reg  [AW-1:0] wr_a1, wr_a2;

    assign rd_hazard = (wr_g1 && (wr_a1 == rd_ptr[AW-1:0])) ||
                       (wr_g2 && (wr_a2 == rd_ptr[AW-1:0]));

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_g1 <= 1'b0;
            wr_g2 <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            wr_g1 <= wr_go;
            wr_g2 <= wr_g1;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go)
            wr_a1 <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
        if (wr_g1)
            wr_a2 <= wr_a1;
    end

    // One SRAM command per cycle; reads and writes take turns.
    assign rd_go = rd_want && !rd_hazard && !wr_go;

    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
    wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;
    wire pkt_pop;               // last read of a packet issued (below)
    wire bp_pop  = bp_take && in_last;  // bypassed last beat: descriptor done

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_ptr    <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            pkt_start <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            drop_cnt  <= 16'd0;
            rr_rd     <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (pkt_drop) begin
                wr_ptr   <= pkt_start;          // forget the whole packet
                drop_cnt <= drop_cnt + 16'd1;
            end else if (wr_go) begin
                wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
                if (in_last)
                    pkt_start <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
            end

            if (wr_go && rd_want)
                rr_rd <= 1'b1;
            else if (rd_go && in_valid && can_accept)
                rr_rd <= 1'b0;
        end
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Descriptor queue, release and retry
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (pkt_push) begin
            desc_end[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            desc_err[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= in_err;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            desc_wp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_rp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_keep <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            free_ptr  <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (pkt_push)
                desc_wp <= desc_wp + 1'b1;

            if (pkt_retry)
                desc_rp <= desc_keep;           // read the packet again
            else if (pkt_pop)
                desc_rp <= desc_rp + 1'b1;
            else if (bp_pop)
                desc_rp <= desc_rp + 1'b1;

            if (cfg_cut_through) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_rp;
                free_ptr  <= rd_ptr;
            end else if (pkt_release) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_keep + 1'b1;
                free_ptr  <= free_ptr + {1'b0, desc_end[desc_keep[NDW-1:0]] - free_ptr[AW-1:0]} + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    // What the egress may read next.
    wire head_valid = (desc_cnt != 0);
    wire rd_last    = head_valid && (rd_ptr[AW-1:0] == desc_end[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]]);
    wire rd_err     = desc_err[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]];

    // Store-and-forward: only words of complete packets.
    // Cut-through: any word already written.
    wire rd_avail = cfg_cut_through ? (rd_ptr != wr_ptr) : head_valid;

    assign pkt_pop = rd_go && rd_last;
    assign rd_want = rd_avail && q_room;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Read pointer. A bypassed word is handed straight to the egress
    // stream, so its SRAM read is skipped: rd_ptr jumps past it.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n)
            rd_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
        else if (pkt_retry)
            rd_ptr <= free_ptr;                 // read the packet again
        else if (bp_take)
            rd_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
        else if (rd_go)
            rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1'b1;
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Read command pipeline, NW61P with LAT = H (RL = 3):
    //   rd_p0  the read command is being registered onto the SRAM pins
    //   rd_p1  the SRAM samples the command at this edge
    //   rd_p2  ...pipeline...
    //   rd_p2 at edge z means the data is on sram_rdata in cycle z and is
    //   pushed into the output queue at edge z (command edge was z-3).
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg rd_p0, rd_p1, rd_p2;
    reg tag_last0, tag_last1, tag_last2;
    reg tag_err0,  tag_err1,  tag_err2;

    wire [2:0] in_flight = {2'b00, rd_p0} + {2'b00, rd_p1} + {2'b00, rd_p2};
    wire       q_push    = rd_p2 && !pkt_retry;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            rd_p0 <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1 <= 1'b0;
            rd_p2 <= 1'b0;
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            rd_p0 <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1 <= 1'b0;
            rd_p2 <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            rd_p0 <= rd_go;
            rd_p1 <= rd_p0;
            rd_p2 <= rd_p1;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        tag_last0 <= rd_last;
        tag_err0  <= rd_err;
        tag_last1 <= tag_last0;
        tag_err1  <= tag_err0;
        tag_last2 <= tag_last1;
        tag_err2  <= tag_err1;
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // SRAM pins. Commands are registered one cycle ahead of the command
    // edge; the write data follows the write command by one more cycle
    // (late write): sram_wdata is the accepted beat delayed twice.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg          wr_go_r;
    reg  [DW-1:0] in_data_r;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            sram_ce_n <= 1'b1;
            sram_we_n <= 1'b1;
            wr_go_r   <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            sram_ce_n <= !(wr_go || rd_go);
            sram_we_n <= !wr_go;
            wr_go_r   <= wr_go;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go) begin
            sram_addr  <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            in_data_r  <= in_data;
        end else if (rd_go) begin
            sram_addr  <= rd_ptr[AW-1:0];
        end
        if (wr_go_r)
            sram_wdata <= in_data_r;
    end

    assign drop_count = drop_cnt;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Egress
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    pktbuf_egress #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) u_egress (
        .clk         (clk),
        .rst_n       (rst_n),
        .retry_en    (!cfg_cut_through),
        .in_flight   (in_flight),
        .q_push      (q_push),
        .q_push_last (tag_last2),
        .q_push_err  (tag_err2),
        .q_room      (q_room),
        .bp_wr_go    (wr_go),
        .bp_wr_eq    (rd_ptr == wr_ptr),
        .bp_wdata    (in_data),
        .bp_wlast    (in_last),
        .bp_werr     (in_err),
        .bp_take     (bp_take),
        .pkt_release (pkt_release),
        .pkt_retry   (pkt_retry),
        .sram_rdata  (sram_rdata),
        .out_valid   (out_valid),
        .out_ready   (out_ready),
        .out_data    (out_data),
        .out_last    (out_last),
        .out_err     (out_err),
        .out_retry   (out_retry)
    );

endmodule
EOF

// pktbuf_egress.v
//
// Egress half of pktbuf: queues the words returned by the SRAM read
// pipeline for the egress stream, forwards words straight from the
// ingress stream through a bypass register in cut-through mode when the
// SRAM read side has caught up, and handles a retry request at the end
// of a packet. See docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// Board rev C (ECR-0412): NW61P1024, LAT = H, read latency 3 cycles,
// late write. A word may not come back from the SRAM until 8 cycles
// after its ingress beat was accepted (one cycle to register the write
// command, one command edge, three read-latency cycles), which is more
// than the 5-cycle cut-through first-beat budget of spec 6.4. When the
// read side is idle (queue empty, no read in flight, rd_ptr == wr_ptr)
// a word therefore goes straight from the ingress stream into the
// bypass register and onto the egress stream; it is still written to
// the SRAM in the same cycle, so the address map is unchanged and the
// read side simply skips it. Whenever anything is queued or in flight,
// words keep coming from the SRAM, which preserves packet order.

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf_egress #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,

    input  wire          retry_en,     // store-and-forward: out_retry is honoured

    // read pipeline in pktbuf.v (NW61P, LAT = H: data valid with q_push)
    input  wire [2:0]    in_flight,    // reads issued, data not yet captured
    input  wire          q_push,       // read data on sram_rdata this cycle
    input  wire          q_push_last,  // ...and it is the last of its packet
    input  wire          q_push_err,   // ...and that packet had in_err
    output wire          q_room,       // a read issued now will find a free entry

    // cut-through bypass
    input  wire          bp_wr_go,     // an ingress beat is written this cycle
    input  wire          bp_wr_eq,     // the read side has caught up with it
    input  wire [DW-1:0] bp_wdata,
    input  wire          bp_wlast,
    input  wire          bp_werr,
    output wire          bp_take,      // the beat goes into the bypass register

    output wire          pkt_release,  // a last beat moved, packet done
    output wire          pkt_retry,    // a last beat moved with out_retry

    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,

    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry
);

    localparam QD = 4;      // output queue entries
    localparam QW = 2;      // log2(QD)

    reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_last [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_err  [0:QD-1];
    reg [QW-1:0] q_wp;
    reg [QW-1:0] q_rp;
    reg [QW:0]   q_cnt;

    // Bypass register: one beat ahead of the queue, on the egress stream.
    reg          bp_v;
    reg [DW-1:0] bp_d;
    reg          bp_l;
    reg          bp_e;

    // The bypass is offered a beat only when everything older has left the
    // SRAM side: queue empty, nothing in the read pipeline, and the word
    // being written is the very next one the read side would read.
    wire can_bp = (q_cnt == {(QW+1){1'b0}}) && (in_flight == 3'd0) &&
                  bp_wr_eq && !bp_v;

    assign bp_take = bp_wr_go && can_bp;

    // One read in flight, plus a second in the cycle after its issue, fits
    // with two entries to spare (the queue is never more than QD-2 deep
    // when a read is issued).
    assign q_room = (q_cnt + {{QW{1'b0}}, in_flight}) < (QD - 2);

    wire q_pop  = !bp_v && out_valid && out_ready;
    wire bp_pop =  bp_v && out_ready;

    // End of a packet on the egress stream. A retry throws away everything
    // read ahead (queued words and reads in flight) and the read side
    // starts the same packet again from its first word.
    wire last_out = (bp_pop && bp_l) || (q_pop && q_last[q_rp]);

    assign pkt_retry   = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
    assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (q_push) begin
            q_data[q_wp] <= sram_rdata;
            q_last[q_wp] <= q_push_last;
            q_err[q_wp]  <= q_push_err && q_push_last;
        end
        if (bp_take) begin
            bp_d <= bp_wdata;
            bp_l <= bp_wlast;
            bp_e <= bp_werr && bp_wlast;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            q_wp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_rp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
            bp_v  <= 1'b0;
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            q_wp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
            bp_v  <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (q_push)
                q_wp <= q_wp + 1'b1;
            if (q_pop)
                q_rp <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            case ({q_push, q_pop})
                2'b10:   q_cnt <= q_cnt + 1'b1;
                2'b01:   q_cnt <= q_cnt - 1'b1;
                default: q_cnt <= q_cnt;
            endcase
            if (bp_take)
                bp_v <= 1'b1;
            else if (bp_pop)
                bp_v <= 1'b0;
        end
    end

    assign out_valid = bp_v || (q_cnt != 0);
    assign out_data  = bp_v ? bp_d : q_data[q_rp];
    assign out_last  = bp_v ? bp_l : q_last[q_rp];
    assign out_err   = bp_v ? bp_e : q_err[q_rp];

endmodule
EOF

`timescale 1ns/1ps
// pktbuf rev C regression: NW61P1024 model (LAT=H, RL=3, late write),
// random traffic + backpressure, both modes, retries and drops.
module tb_revc;
    localparam DW = `DW;
    localparam AW = `AW;
    localparam NWORDS = (1 << AW);

    reg clk = 1'b0;
    always #5 clk = ~clk;

    reg           rst_n = 1'b0;
    reg           cfg_ct = 1'b0;
    reg           in_valid = 1'b0;
    reg  [DW-1:0] in_data = {DW{1'b0}};
    reg           in_last = 1'b0;
    reg           in_err  = 1'b0;
    reg           out_ready = 1'b1;
    reg           out_retry = 1'b0;
    wire          in_ready, out_valid, out_last, out_err;
    wire [DW-1:0] out_data;
    wire [15:0]   drop_count;
    wire          sram_ce_n, sram_we_n;
    wire [AW-1:0] sram_addr;
    wire [DW-1:0] sram_wdata;
    reg  [DW-1:0] sram_rdata;

    pktbuf #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) dut (
        .clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .cfg_cut_through(cfg_ct),
        .in_valid(in_valid), .in_ready(in_ready), .in_data(in_data),
        .in_last(in_last), .in_err(in_err),
        .out_valid(out_valid), .out_ready(out_ready), .out_data(out_data),
        .out_last(out_last), .out_err(out_err), .out_retry(out_retry),
        .drop_count(drop_count),
        .sram_ce_n(sram_ce_n), .sram_we_n(sram_we_n), .sram_addr(sram_addr),
        .sram_wdata(sram_wdata), .sram_rdata(sram_rdata)
    );

    // ---------------- NW61P1024 model, LAT=H (RL=3), late write ----------
    reg [DW-1:0] mem [0:NWORDS-1];
    reg          wr_p;
    reg [AW-1:0] wa_p;
    reg          rd_v [0:2];
    reg [DW-1:0] rd_d [0:2];
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_p) mem[wa_p] <= sram_wdata;        // late write data edge
        if (!sram_ce_n) begin
            wr_p <= !sram_we_n;
            wa_p <= sram_addr;
            if (sram_we_n) begin                  // read cmd sampled now
                rd_v[0] <= 1'b1;
                rd_d[0] <= mem[sram_addr];
            end else rd_v[0] <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            wr_p <= 1'b0;
            rd_v[0] <= 1'b0;
        end
        rd_v[1] <= rd_v[0]; rd_d[1] <= rd_d[0];
        rd_v[2] <= rd_v[1]; rd_d[2] <= rd_d[1];
        if (rd_v[2]) sram_rdata <= rd_d[2];
        else         sram_rdata <= {$random};
    end

    // ---------------- scoreboard ----------------
    // sent packets, in order: data / last / err / expected action
    localparam MAXB = 200000;
    reg [DW-1:0] exp_d [0:MAXB-1];
    reg          exp_l [0:MAXB-1];
    reg          exp_e [0:MAXB-1];
    integer n_exp, n_out, errors, drops_expected, drops_seen;
    integer cap_used, words_in;

    // ingress driver
    integer pk_len, pk_beat, pk_id, pk_dropped, pk_errf;
    integer gap, mode_hold;
    reg [DW-1:0] cur_data;
    integer seed;

    function [31:0] rng(input integer s); begin rng = $random(seed); end endfunction

    task set_mode(input integer ct);
        integer i;
        begin
            // quiesce: drain before switching
            cfg_ct = ct;
            for (i = 0; i < 40; i = i + 1) @(negedge clk);
        end
    endtask

    task start_packet;
        begin
            pk_len  = 1 + ({$random} % 40);
            if (pk_len > NWORDS) pk_len = NWORDS;
            pk_beat = 0;
            pk_errf = ({$random} % 8) == 0;   // 1/8 packets errored
            pk_dropped = 0;
        end
    endtask

    // random backpressure on out_ready
    always @(negedge clk) begin
        if (rst_n) begin
            out_ready <= (({$random} % 5) != 0);
            out_retry <= (({$random} % 12) == 0);
        end
    end

    // ingress driver process
    integer idle_gap;
    initial begin
        idle_gap = 0; pk_beat = -1;
        @(negedge clk);
        forever begin
            @(negedge clk);
            if (!rst_n) begin
                in_valid <= 1'b0; pk_beat <= -1; idle_gap <= 5;
            end else if (pk_beat < 0) begin
                if (idle_gap > 0) begin idle_gap <= idle_gap - 1; in_valid <= 1'b0; end
                else begin
                    start_packet;
                    in_valid <= 1'b1;
                    in_data  <= $random;
                    in_last  <= (pk_len == 1);
                    in_err   <= (pk_len == 1) && pk_errf;
                    pk_beat  <= 0;
                end
            end else begin
                if (in_valid && in_ready) begin
                    // beat accepted at the upcoming posedge
                    if (!pk_dropped) begin
                        if (!(!cfg_ct && in_last && in_err)) begin
                            exp_d[n_exp] = in_data;
                            exp_l[n_exp] = in_last;
                            exp_e[n_exp] = cfg_ct && in_last && in_err;
                            n_exp = n_exp + 1;
                        end else drops_expected = drops_expected + 1;
                    end else drops_expected = drops_expected + 0;
                    if (in_last) begin
                        pk_beat <= -1;
                        in_valid <= 1'b0;
                        idle_gap <= ({$random} % 6);
                    end else begin
                        pk_beat <= pk_beat + 1;
                        if ({$random} % 4 == 0) in_valid <= 1'b0; // stall
                        else begin
                            in_data <= $random;
                            in_last <= (pk_beat + 1 == pk_len - 1);
                            in_err  <= (pk_beat + 1 == pk_len - 1) && pk_errf;
                        end
                    end
                end else if (!in_valid) begin
                    in_valid <= 1'b1;
                    in_data  <= $random;
                    in_last  <= (pk_beat == pk_len - 1);
                    in_err   <= (pk_beat == pk_len - 1) && pk_errf;
                end
            end
        end
    end

    // NOTE: retries resend a packet: scoreboard handles by rewinding.
    integer retry_pending;
    reg [DW-1:0] last_pkt_d [0:4095];
    reg last_pkt_e;
    integer last_pkt_len, cur_pkt_len, cur_pkt_start;

    // output checker
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst_n && out_valid && out_ready) begin
            if (out_data !== exp_d[n_out] || out_last !== exp_l[n_out] || out_err !== exp_e[n_out]) begin
                if (errors < 10)
                    $display("revc: beat %0d: got %h l%b e%b, exp %h l%b e%b",
                             n_out, out_data, out_last, out_err, exp_d[n_out], exp_l[n_out], exp_e[n_out]);
                errors = errors + 1;
            end
            // remember current packet beats for retry
            last_pkt_d[cur_pkt_len] = exp_d[n_out];
            cur_pkt_len = cur_pkt_len + 1;
            n_out = n_out + 1;
            if (out_last) begin
                if (out_retry && !cfg_ct && retry_en_ok) begin
                    // rewind: the same packet comes again
                    n_out = n_out - cur_pkt_len;
                end
                cur_pkt_len = 0;
            end
        end
    end
    wire retry_en_ok = 1'b1;

    // drop accounting
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst_n) drops_seen <= 0; // placeholder
    end

    integer cyc;
    initial begin
        n_exp = 0; n_out = 0; errors = 0; cur_pkt_len = 0;
        drops_expected = 0;
        seed = `SEED;
        repeat (6) @(negedge clk);
        rst_n = 1'b1;
        repeat (8) @(negedge clk);

        // store-and-forward phase
        cfg_ct = 1'b0;
        for (cyc = 0; cyc < `NCYC; cyc = cyc + 1) @(posedge clk);
        // drain
        in_valid = 1'b0;
        repeat (4000) @(posedge clk);
        set_mode(1);
        // cut-through phase
        for (cyc = 0; cyc < `NCYC; cyc = cyc + 1) @(posedge clk);
        in_valid = 1'b0;
        repeat (4000) @(posedge clk);

        if (n_out != n_exp)
            $display("revc: %0d beats expected, %0d received", n_exp, n_out);
        if (errors == 0 && n_out == n_exp && n_exp > 100)
            $display("REVC PASS: %0d beats", n_out);
        else
            $display("REVC FAIL: errors=%0d n_out=%0d n_exp=%0d", errors, n_out, n_exp);
        $finish;
    end
endmodule
EOF
echo done

Rev C SRAM (NW61P1024, LAT strapped H per ECO-117, confirmed by ila_sram_sn0007.csv): read latency RL=3 (command edge -> data at +3), late write (D sampled one cycle after write command), and a write becomes visible to same-address reads only 3 command edges later.

Changes:
- Read command pipeline stretched to 3 stages (rd_p0/p1/p2); read data committed to the output queue when it actually returns (q_push = rd_p2), giving a store-and-forward first-beat latency of 6-8 cycles, within the ECR's relaxed 10-cycle budget.
- Late-write data path: sram_wdata is the accepted beat delayed by two stages (in_data_r -> sram_wdata).
- Read/write order guard (wr_g1/wr_g2 + address compare) holds off a read of a just-written word for the required 3 command edges.
- Cut-through bypass register: when the read side has caught up (queue empty, nothing in flight, rd_ptr==wr_ptr) a word is forwarded straight from ingress to the egress stream, meeting the unchanged 5-cycle spec 6.4 budget (which is impossible through the 8-cycle SRAM loop). Packet order preserved; bypassed words are still written to SRAM so the address map is unchanged.
- Retry kept as full flush + rewind (rd_ptr <- free_ptr, desc_rp <- desc_keep) as on rev B.

Both files: top module pktbuf unchanged (name/ports/params); no initial blocks/delays/force/defparam/bind/etc.; all event controls are posedge/negedge lists; only $clog2-style params; named parameter overrides; all behaviour flops reset. Elaborates clean on iverilog -g2012 and verilator --lint-only at DW=8/16/32, AW=6/8/10/12.

# ECR-0412: pktbuf on board rev C

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Status | Approved |
| Affects | `pktbuf.v`, `pktbuf_egress.v` (line card FPGA) |
| Board | Line card rev C |

## Reason

The buffer SRAM on rev B, NW61F1024, is end of life. Rev C fits the NW61P1024 in its place. The footprint and the signals between FPGA and SRAM are the same: CE#, WE#, A[9:0], D[31:0] (write data) and Q[31:0] (read data). The NW61P1024 is a pipelined part with late write, so its timing differs. See `NW61F1024_excerpt.md`, `NW61P1024_excerpt.md` and `board_rev_c_notes.md`.

## Change

1. `pktbuf` works with the NW61P1024 as fitted and strapped on rev C boards. Rev B support is not needed. The other boards that use `pktbuf` with other `DW`/`AW` move to NW61P-family parts of the matching organisation, wired and strapped as on rev C, so the same SRAM timing applies at every `DW`/`AW`.
2. The top-level module name, ports and parameters stay as they are. The FPGA top level is not changed.
3. Behaviour stays as in `pktbuf_spec.md` for every supported `DW` and `AW`, in both modes, under any backpressure, with one exception: the line-rate limit in section 6.3 becomes **10 cycles** from the edge that took the last ingress beat to the edge that takes the first egress beat (was 4). Everything else in section 6 is unchanged: the ingress rate in 6.1, the gap-free requirements in 6.2 and 6.3, and the cut-through first-beat latency in 6.4, which is fixed by the switch.
4. All logic stays in `pktbuf.v` and `pktbuf_egress.v`.

## Verification

The block regression is being moved to a rev C SRAM model and will be run on the changed RTL at several `DW`/`AW` settings, on Icarus Verilog and on Verilator with random power-up state. The smoke test in `tb/` models the rev B part and is not part of the sign-off.
# Line card rev C: hardware notes for FPGA designers

Extract of the rev C design notes. Items that do not concern the packet buffer are left out.

## Clocks

| Net | Frequency | Source | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLK_CORE | 125.00 MHz | PLL1 out 0 | FPGA core, `pktbuf` `clk` |
| SRAM_CLK | 125.00 MHz | PLL1 out 1, phase aligned to CLK_CORE | U12 CLK |

## Buffer SRAM (U12)

U12 is the NW61P1024 (rev B: NW61F1024). Pins as on rev B:

| FPGA signal | U12 pin |
| --- | --- |
| `sram_ce_n` | CE# |
| `sram_we_n` | WE# |
| `sram_addr[9:0]` | A[9:0] |
| `sram_wdata[31:0]` | D[31:0] |
| `sram_rdata[31:0]` | Q[31:0] |

The `pktbuf` SRAM ports connect straight to the FPGA pins; the FPGA I/O has no input or output registers on these signals. Board delays are within one cycle at 125 MHz, so the edges in the U12 datasheet are `pktbuf` clock edges.

| --- | --- | --- |

// pktbuf.v
//
// Packet buffer between the line-side receive stream and the switch
// interface. Packets arrive on a valid/ready stream, are stored in an
// external synchronous SRAM, and leave on a second valid/ready stream.
// The block behaviour is specified in docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// Written for board rev B, where the SRAM is the NW61F1024 flow-through
// part (docs/NW61F1024_excerpt.md).
//
// This file holds the top level: ingress, the packet descriptor queue,
// buffer space and retry bookkeeping, the SRAM command arbiter and the
// SRAM pins. The read pipeline and the output queue are in
// pktbuf_egress.v.

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf #(
    parameter DW = 32,          // data width, also the SRAM word width
    parameter AW = 10           // SRAM address width, 2**AW words
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,           // asynchronous assert, active low

    input  wire          cfg_cut_through, // 0 store-and-forward, 1 cut-through

    // ingress stream
    input  wire          in_valid,
    output wire          in_ready,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] in_data,
    input  wire          in_last,
    input  wire          in_err,          // sampled with in_last only

    // egress stream
    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry,       // sampled with the last beat only

    // status
    output wire [15:0]   drop_count,

    // external SRAM, all outputs driven from flops
    output reg           sram_ce_n,
    output reg           sram_we_n,
    output reg  [AW-1:0] sram_addr,
    output reg  [DW-1:0] sram_wdata,
    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata
);

    localparam ND  = 8;                         // packet descriptor slots
    localparam NDW = 3;                         // log2(ND)
    localparam [AW:0] CAP = {1'b1, {AW{1'b0}}}; // 2**AW words

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Ingress
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg  [AW:0]    wr_ptr;      // address of the next word to write
    reg  [AW:0]    pkt_start;   // first address of the packet being received
    reg  [15:0]    drop_cnt;

    // Packet descriptor queue: the address of each packet's last word and
    // its error flag. In store-and-forward mode an entry means "this packet
    // is complete". In cut-through mode it only marks where a packet ends.
    // Three free-running pointers (one bit wider than the index):
    //   desc_wp    next entry to write
    //   desc_rp    next packet to read from the SRAM
    //   desc_keep  oldest packet not yet released (store-and-forward: the
    //              packet on the egress stream, which may still be retried)
    reg  [AW-1:0]  desc_end [0:ND-1];
    reg            desc_err [0:ND-1];
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_wp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_rp;
    reg  [NDW:0]   desc_keep;
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_cnt  = desc_wp - desc_rp;     // complete, not yet read
    wire [NDW:0]   desc_held = desc_wp - desc_keep;   // complete, not yet released

    // Buffer space. Cut-through: a word is free once it has been read.
    // Store-and-forward: a packet's words stay until the packet is released,
    // so that it can be sent again; free_ptr is the first word still held.
    reg  [AW:0]    free_ptr;

    wire [AW:0]    rd_ptr;      // address of the next word to read (egress)
    wire           rd_want;     // egress asks for a read command this cycle
    wire           rd_go;       // ... and gets it
    wire           wr_go;       // an ingress beat is written this cycle
    reg            rr_rd;       // the read wins the next conflict
    wire           pkt_release; // egress: a packet's last beat moved, no retry
    wire           pkt_retry;   // egress: a packet's last beat moved with retry

    wire [AW:0]    used       = wr_ptr - (cfg_cut_through ? rd_ptr : free_ptr);
    wire           can_accept = (used != CAP) && (desc_held != ND);

    // One SRAM command per cycle. When ingress and egress both want the
    // SRAM, they take turns.
    assign in_ready = can_accept && !(rd_want && rr_rd);
    assign wr_go    = in_valid && in_ready;
    assign rd_go    = rd_want && !wr_go;

    wire pkt_drop = wr_go && in_last && in_err && !cfg_cut_through;
    wire pkt_push = wr_go && in_last && !pkt_drop;
    wire pkt_pop;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            wr_ptr    <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            pkt_start <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            drop_cnt  <= 16'd0;
            rr_rd     <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (pkt_drop) begin
                wr_ptr   <= pkt_start;          // forget the whole packet
                drop_cnt <= drop_cnt + 16'd1;
            end else if (wr_go) begin
                wr_ptr <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
                if (in_last)
                    pkt_start <= wr_ptr + 1'b1;
            end

            if (wr_go && rd_want)
                rr_rd <= 1'b1;
            else if (rd_go && in_valid && can_accept)
                rr_rd <= 1'b0;
        end
    end

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Descriptor queue, release and retry
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (pkt_push) begin
            desc_end[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            desc_err[desc_wp[NDW-1:0]] <= in_err;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            desc_wp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_rp   <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            desc_keep <= {(NDW+1){1'b0}};
            free_ptr  <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (pkt_push)
                desc_wp <= desc_wp + 1'b1;

            if (pkt_retry)
                desc_rp <= desc_keep;           // read the packet again
            else if (pkt_pop)
                desc_rp <= desc_rp + 1'b1;

            if (cfg_cut_through) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_rp;
                free_ptr  <= rd_ptr;
            end else if (pkt_release) begin
                desc_keep <= desc_keep + 1'b1;
                free_ptr  <= free_ptr + {1'b0, desc_end[desc_keep[NDW-1:0]] - free_ptr[AW-1:0]} + 1'b1;
            end
        end
    end

    // What the egress may read next.
    wire head_valid = (desc_cnt != 0);
    wire rd_last    = head_valid && (rd_ptr[AW-1:0] == desc_end[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]]);
    wire rd_err     = desc_err[desc_rp[NDW-1:0]];

    // Store-and-forward: only words of complete packets.
    // Cut-through: any word already written.
    wire rd_avail   = cfg_cut_through ? (rd_ptr != wr_ptr) : head_valid;

    assign pkt_pop  = rd_go && rd_last;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // SRAM pins
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            sram_ce_n <= 1'b1;
            sram_we_n <= 1'b1;
        end else begin
            sram_ce_n <= !(wr_go || rd_go);
            sram_we_n <= !wr_go;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go) begin
            sram_addr  <= wr_ptr[AW-1:0];
            sram_wdata <= in_data;
        end else if (rd_go) begin
            sram_addr  <= rd_ptr[AW-1:0];
        end
    end

    assign drop_count = drop_cnt;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Egress
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    pktbuf_egress #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) u_egress (
        .clk         (clk),
        .rst_n       (rst_n),
        .retry_en    (!cfg_cut_through),
        .rd_avail    (rd_avail),
        .rd_last     (rd_last),
        .rd_err      (rd_err),
        .rd_go       (rd_go),
        .rd_want     (rd_want),
        .rd_ptr      (rd_ptr),
        .rd_restart  (free_ptr),
        .pkt_release (pkt_release),
        .pkt_retry   (pkt_retry),
        .sram_rdata  (sram_rdata),
        .out_valid   (out_valid),
        .out_ready   (out_ready),
        .out_data    (out_data),
        .out_last    (out_last),
        .out_err     (out_err),
        .out_retry   (out_retry)
    );

endmodule
// pktbuf_egress.v
//
// Egress half of pktbuf: issues SRAM reads in address order, follows each
// read through the SRAM, queues the returned words for the egress stream,
// and handles a retry request at the end of a packet. See
// docs/pktbuf_spec.md.
//
// Written for board rev B (NW61F1024, flow-through).

`timescale 1ns/1ps

module pktbuf_egress #(
    parameter DW = 32,
    parameter AW = 10
) (
    input  wire          clk,
    input  wire          rst_n,

    input  wire          retry_en,    // store-and-forward: out_retry is honoured
    input  wire          rd_avail,    // the word at rd_ptr may be read
    input  wire          rd_last,     // ... and is the last of its packet
    input  wire          rd_err,      // ... and that packet had in_err
    input  wire          rd_go,       // the arbiter issues the read this cycle
    output wire          rd_want,
    output reg  [AW:0]   rd_ptr,
    input  wire [AW:0]   rd_restart,  // first word of the packet on the egress stream
    output wire          pkt_release, // a last beat moved, packet done
    output wire          pkt_retry,   // a last beat moved with out_retry: send it again

    input  wire [DW-1:0] sram_rdata,

    output wire          out_valid,
    input  wire          out_ready,
    output wire [DW-1:0] out_data,
    output wire          out_last,
    output wire          out_err,
    input  wire          out_retry
);

    localparam QD = 4;      // output queue entries
    localparam QW = 2;      // log2(QD)

    // Read pipeline, NW61F flow-through:
    //   rd_p0  the read command is on the SRAM pins
    //   rd_p1  the SRAM sampled it at this edge; its data is on sram_rdata
    //          and is captured at the next edge
    reg rd_p0, rd_p1;
    reg tag_last0, tag_last1;
    reg tag_err0,  tag_err1;

    reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_last [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_err  [0:QD-1];
    reg [QW-1:0] q_wp;
    reg [QW-1:0] q_rp;
    reg [QW:0]   q_cnt;

    wire [QW:0] in_flight = {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p0} + {{QW{1'b0}}, rd_p1};
    wire        q_push    = rd_p1;
    wire        q_pop     = out_valid && out_ready;

    // End of a packet on the egress stream. A retry throws away everything
    // read ahead (queued words and reads in flight) and starts reading the
    // same packet again from its first word.
    wire        last_out  = q_pop && out_last;
    assign pkt_retry   = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
    assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

    // Ask for a read only when its data is sure to find a free entry.
    assign rd_want = rd_avail && ((q_cnt + in_flight) < QD);

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            rd_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            rd_ptr <= rd_restart;
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (rd_go)
                rd_ptr <= rd_ptr + 1'b1;
            rd_p0 <= rd_go;
            rd_p1 <= rd_p0;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        tag_last0 <= rd_last;
        tag_err0  <= rd_err;
        tag_last1 <= tag_last0;
        tag_err1  <= tag_err0;
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (q_push) begin
            q_data[q_wp] <= sram_rdata;
            q_last[q_wp] <= tag_last1;
            q_err[q_wp]  <= tag_err1 && tag_last1;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            q_wp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_rp  <= {QW{1'b0}};
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
        end else if (pkt_retry) begin
            q_rp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_wp  <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_cnt <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
        end else begin
            if (q_push)
                q_wp <= q_wp + 1'b1;
            if (q_pop)
                q_rp <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            case ({q_push, q_pop})
                2'b10:   q_cnt <= q_cnt + 1'b1;
                2'b01:   q_cnt <= q_cnt - 1'b1;
                default: q_cnt <= q_cnt;
            endcase
        end
    end

    assign out_valid = (q_cnt != 0);
    assign out_data  = q_data[q_rp];
    assign out_last  = q_last[q_rp];
    assign out_err   = q_err[q_rp];

endmodule

# pktbuf: packet buffer, block specification

Revision 1.4. Applies to `pktbuf.v` and `pktbuf_egress.v`.

## 1. Purpose

`pktbuf` sits between the line-side receive stream and the switch interface. It stores whole packets, or forwards them as they arrive, using an external synchronous SRAM as the buffer memory. One SRAM holds the words of all packets in a ring, in arrival order.

## 2. Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Supported |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DW` | Data width of both streams and of the SRAM word | 8 to 32 |
| `AW` | SRAM address width; the buffer holds 2**`AW` words | 6 to 12 |

The line card uses `DW = 32`, `AW = 10`. Other boards use other values; the block must work for every supported combination.

## 3. Ports

| Port | Dir | Width | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clk` | in | 1 | Clock. The SRAM is clocked from the same clock. |
| `rst_n` | in | 1 | Reset, active low, asserted asynchronously, released synchronously to `clk`. |
| `cfg_cut_through` | in | 1 | 0: store-and-forward. 1: cut-through. Static, see 5.4. |
| `in_valid` | in | 1 | Ingress beat valid. |
| `in_ready` | out | 1 | Ingress beat accepted at this edge if `in_valid` is also high. |
| `in_data` | in | `DW` | Ingress data. |
| `in_last` | in | 1 | Last beat of a packet. |
| `in_err` | in | 1 | Packet error. Only meaningful with `in_last`; ignored on other beats. |
| `out_valid` | out | 1 | Egress beat valid. |
| `out_ready` | in | 1 | Egress beat taken at this edge if `out_valid` is also high. |
| `out_data` | out | `DW` | Egress data. |
| `out_last` | out | 1 | Last beat of a packet. |
| `out_err` | out | 1 | Packet error, on the last beat only (cut-through mode). |
| `out_retry` | in | 1 | Retry request from the switch. Sampled only at the edge that moves the last beat of a packet; ignored at every other edge. See 5.5. |
| `drop_count` | out | 16 | Packets dropped since reset, wraps at 2**16. |
| `sram_ce_n` | out | 1 | SRAM chip enable, active low. A command is issued in each cycle with `sram_ce_n` low. |
| `sram_we_n` | out | 1 | SRAM write enable, active low: low for a write command, high for a read command. |
| `sram_addr` | out | `AW` | SRAM word address. |
| `sram_wdata` | out | `DW` | SRAM write data (to the SRAM's D inputs). |
| `sram_rdata` | in | `DW` | SRAM read data (from the SRAM's Q outputs). |

All `sram_*` outputs are driven from flops. The ports connect straight to the SRAM pins: the board and the FPGA I/O add no register stages. When the SRAM samples the pins and when it returns read data depend on the SRAM part; see the board's SRAM datasheet.

## 4. Streams

Both streams use valid/ready. A beat moves at a rising edge of `clk` at which valid and ready are both high. Once valid is high, the sender holds the beat (data, last, err) unchanged until it moves. `in_ready` may change at any time; a sender does not wait for `in_ready` before raising `in_valid`.

A packet is 1 or more beats, the last with `in_last` high. In store-and-forward mode a packet is at most 2**`AW` beats. In cut-through mode there is no limit.

## 5. Behaviour

### 5.1 Reset

While `rst_n` is low and after it is released: `out_valid` is low, `drop_count` is 0, and no SRAM command is issued (`sram_ce_n` high) until there is a beat to write. `in_ready` is high no later than 4 cycles after release.

### 5.2 Store-and-forward (`cfg_cut_through` = 0)

A packet is sent on the egress stream only after its last beat has been received. A packet whose last beat has `in_err` high is dropped: none of its beats is sent, and `drop_count` increments by one. Packets leave in the order they arrived. `out_err` is always 0.

### 5.3 Cut-through (`cfg_cut_through` = 1)

A packet may start on the egress stream as soon as its first beat has been stored. No packet is dropped and `drop_count` does not change. `out_err` is high on the last beat of a packet whose last ingress beat had `in_err` high, and low on every other beat.

### 5.4 Changing mode

`cfg_cut_through` may change only while the block is empty (every accepted beat has been sent or dropped) and no ingress beat has been accepted for at least 8 cycles. After a change, no ingress beat is offered for at least 8 cycles.

### 5.5 Retry (store-and-forward)

In store-and-forward mode the switch can refuse a packet at its end. If `out_retry` is high at the edge that moves the last beat of a packet, the block sends the same packet again, complete and unchanged, before any other packet. The resent packet can be refused again in the same way, any number of times. If `out_retry` is low at that edge, the packet is released. In cut-through mode `out_retry` is ignored.

### 5.6 Capacity and flow control

The buffer holds up to 2**`AW` words and up to 8 packets whose last beat has been received but which have not yet been released (store-and-forward) or completely read from the SRAM (cut-through). `in_ready` is low while either limit is reached. In store-and-forward mode a packet's words are kept until the packet is released. A word's location is free again once the block no longer needs it.

### 5.7 SRAM use

The SRAM takes one command per cycle. How the ingress and egress sides share it is up to the design, within the requirements of section 6. (The rev B design lets them take turns.) Once the block is empty (every accepted beat has been sent or dropped) and no beat is being received, it issues no SRAM command.

## 6. Performance

### 6.1 Ingress

While the buffer has room and the egress side is not reading, one beat is accepted per cycle.

### 6.2 Egress

While `out_ready` is high and the SRAM is not needed by the ingress side, one beat per cycle is sent, with no gaps, until the stored words run out.

### 6.3 Line rate

In store-and-forward mode, with the block empty, a packet of up to 32 beats whose beats are all offered back to back is accepted at one beat per cycle. If `out_ready` is held high and nothing else arrives, the first egress beat moves no later than 4 cycles after the edge that took the last ingress beat, and the remaining beats follow at one per cycle with no gaps.

### 6.4 Cut-through first beat

In cut-through mode, when the block is empty (every accepted beat has been sent) and `out_ready` is high, the first beat of a packet moves on the egress stream no later than 5 cycles after the edge that took it at the ingress. This is the switch's arbitration budget for cut-through packets.

## 7. Implementation notes

- The design must be synthesizable RTL. Everything below the top level is in `pktbuf.v` and `pktbuf_egress.v`.
- No initial blocks, delays, system tasks other than `$clog2`, `$signed` and `$unsigned`, and no compiler directives other than `` `timescale `` and `` `default_nettype ``. Parameter overrides on instances are by name.
- Every flop that affects behaviour is reset; the block must behave the same whatever the power-up state of its flops and memories.
# NW61F1024: 1K x 32 synchronous SRAM, flow-through, separate I/O

Datasheet excerpt (functional description and timing summary). Rev 2.1.

## Description

The NW61F1024 is a 32 768-bit synchronous static RAM organised as 1024 words of 32 bits, with separate data inputs (D) and data outputs (Q). All inputs are registered at the rising edge of CLK. Reads are flow-through: the addressed word appears on Q in the same cycle, after the clock edge that sampled the read command.

## Pins

| Pin | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLK | in | Clock. All inputs are sampled at its rising edge. |
| CE# | in | Chip enable, active low. High: no operation (deselect). |
| WE# | in | Write enable, active low. Low with CE# low: write. High with CE# low: read. |
| A[9:0] | in | Word address. |
| D[31:0] | in | Write data. |
| Q[31:0] | out | Read data. Driven at all times; undefined except in the read data cycle. |

## Operation

Edge *n* is the rising edge of CLK at which CE# is sampled low.

| Command at edge *n* | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Deselect (CE# high) | No operation. |
| Read (WE# high) | A is sampled at edge *n*. The word is on Q after edge *n* and is captured by the controller at edge *n*+1. |
| Write (WE# low) | A and D are sampled at edge *n*. The word is written at edge *n*. |

A read at edge *n*+1 of the address written at edge *n* returns the new data. Any sequence of reads and writes may be issued, one per cycle.

## Timing summary

| Parameter | Min | Max | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clock frequency | | 133 | MHz |
| Read latency (command edge to capture edge) | 1 | 1 | cycle |
# NW61P1024: 1K x 32 synchronous SRAM, pipelined, late write, separate I/O

Datasheet excerpt (functional description and timing summary). Rev 1.4.

## Description

The NW61P1024 is a 32 768-bit synchronous static RAM organised as 1024 words of 32 bits, with separate data inputs (D) and data outputs (Q). It is pin-compatible with the NW61F1024. All inputs are registered at the rising edge of CLK. Reads go through an output pipeline whose depth is set by the LAT pin. Writes use late write: the write data follows the write command by one cycle, so reads and writes can be mixed at one command per cycle without dead cycles.

## Pins

| Pin | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLK | in | Clock. All inputs are sampled at its rising edge. |
| CE# | in | Chip enable, active low. High: no operation (deselect). |
| WE# | in | Write enable, active low. Low with CE# low: write. High with CE# low: read. |
| A[9:0] | in | Word address. |
| D[31:0] | in | Write data, sampled one cycle after the write command (late write). |
| Q[31:0] | out | Read data. Driven at all times; undefined except in the read data cycle. |
| LAT | in | Read latency select, static (strap). See below. Must not change while CLK runs. |

## Read latency

| LAT | Read latency RL (command edge to capture edge) | Clock frequency, max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L | 2 cycles | 100 MHz |
| H | 3 cycles | 166 MHz |

## Operation

Edge *n* is the rising edge of CLK at which a command is sampled.

| Command at edge *n* | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Deselect (CE# high) | No operation. |
| Read (WE# high) | A is sampled at edge *n* and the word is read from the array at edge *n*. It is on Q in the cycle before edge *n*+RL and is captured by the controller at edge *n*+RL. Q holds it for that one cycle only. |
| Write (WE# low) | A is sampled at edge *n*. D is sampled at edge *n*+1, whatever command is issued at edge *n*+1. |

Any sequence of reads, writes and deselects may be issued, one command per cycle. No dead cycle is needed between a read and a write in either order.

## Timing summary

| Parameter | Symbol | Min | Max | Unit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clock cycle time, LAT = L | tCYC | 10.0 | | ns | |
| Clock cycle time, LAT = H | tCYC | 6.0 | | ns | |
| Write data after write command | tWD | 1 | 1 | cycle | |
| Read latency | RL | 2 / 3 | 2 / 3 | cycle | set by LAT |

I'm weighing whether the read can be sampled at e+2 with data arriving at e+5, which would require driving the output combinationally from sram_rdata to meet the 5-cycle budget. Since that read would hit the same address written just before it, I'd need forwarding to avoid stale data.

I'm working out the timing for a read that follows a write: the write to the SRAM is sampled one edge after the ingress edge, so a read can only be sampled two edges after it, which is why the forwarding path looks necessary.

I'm settling on a fall-through path: when the queue is empty and the capture lands this cycle, the captured word goes straight to the output, and if out_ready is low it gets pushed into the queue at that edge instead.

I'm considering whether to skip the SRAM read entirely and serve the forwarded word directly, which would also sidestep the combinational output path.

I'm checking the stale-read window: a read sampled at edge r comes back old if a write to the same address was sampled at r-1 or r-2, while a write sampled three or more edges earlier already shows up. Reads only target words already written, so the ring-wrap case is fine, since a read of the old contents happens before the rewrite.

I'm settling on a forwarding window of three recent writes, since forwarding from my own write record always returns the newest matching word, so a wider window costs nothing. cd /app/data; cat tb/tb_smoke.v Makefile

`timescale 1ns/1ps
// Smoke test for pktbuf on board rev B (NW61F1024 flow-through SRAM).
//
// Sends a few packets in store-and-forward mode, then a few in cut-through
// mode, and checks that they come out unchanged. It is a quick sanity check,
// not a regression: no backpressure, no dropped packets, nothing else.
//
// The SRAM model follows docs/NW61F1024_excerpt.md: command, address and
// write data are sampled at the same rising edge; read data is captured by
// the FPGA at the next rising edge.
module tb_smoke;
    localparam DW = 32;
    localparam AW = 10;

    reg clk = 1'b0;
    always #5 clk = ~clk;

    reg           rst_n     = 1'b0;
    reg           cfg_ct    = 1'b0;
    reg           in_valid  = 1'b0;
    reg  [DW-1:0] in_data   = {DW{1'b0}};
    reg           in_last   = 1'b0;
    reg           in_err    = 1'b0;
    reg           out_ready = 1'b1;
    reg           out_retry = 1'b0;
    wire          in_ready, out_valid, out_last, out_err;
    wire [DW-1:0] out_data;
    wire [15:0]   drop_count;
    wire          sram_ce_n, sram_we_n;
    wire [AW-1:0] sram_addr;
    wire [DW-1:0] sram_wdata;
    reg  [DW-1:0] sram_rdata;

    pktbuf #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) dut (
        .clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .cfg_cut_through(cfg_ct),
        .in_valid(in_valid), .in_ready(in_ready), .in_data(in_data),
        .in_last(in_last), .in_err(in_err),
        .out_valid(out_valid), .out_ready(out_ready), .out_data(out_data),
        .out_last(out_last), .out_err(out_err), .out_retry(out_retry),
        .drop_count(drop_count),
        .sram_ce_n(sram_ce_n), .sram_we_n(sram_we_n), .sram_addr(sram_addr),
        .sram_wdata(sram_wdata), .sram_rdata(sram_rdata)
    );

    // NW61F1024 model
    reg [DW-1:0] mem [0:(1<<AW)-1];
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b0)
            mem[sram_addr] <= sram_wdata;
        if (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b1)
            sram_rdata <= mem[sram_addr];
        else
            sram_rdata <= 32'hDEADBEEF;
    end

    // expected beats, in order
    reg [DW-1:0] exp_d [0:1023];
    reg          exp_l [0:1023];
    integer      n_in, n_out, errors, i, p, len;

    // count what comes out
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst_n && out_valid && out_ready) begin
            if (out_data !== exp_d[n_out] || out_last !== exp_l[n_out] || out_err !== 1'b0) begin
                if (errors < 5)
                    $display("smoke: beat %0d: got %h last %b err %b, expected %h last %b",
                             n_out, out_data, out_last, out_err, exp_d[n_out], exp_l[n_out]);
                errors = errors + 1;
            end
            n_out = n_out + 1;
        end
    end

    task send_packet(input integer n);
        integer b;
        begin
            for (b = 0; b < n; b = b + 1) begin
                @(negedge clk);
                in_valid = 1'b1;
                in_data  = {p[7:0], b[7:0], 16'hA5C3} ^ (b * 32'h01000193);
                in_last  = (b == n - 1);
                exp_d[n_in] = in_data;
                exp_l[n_in] = in_last;
                n_in = n_in + 1;
                #1;
                while (in_ready !== 1'b1) begin
                    @(negedge clk);
                    #1;
                end
                @(posedge clk);              // the beat is taken at this edge
            end
            @(negedge clk);
            in_valid = 1'b0;
            in_last  = 1'b0;
        end
    endtask

    task wait_drain;
        integer t;
        begin
            t = 0;
            while (n_out < n_in && t < 2000) begin
                @(posedge clk);
                t = t + 1;
            end
        end
    endtask

    initial begin
        n_in = 0; n_out = 0; errors = 0;
        repeat (4) @(negedge clk);
        rst_n = 1'b1;
        repeat (4) @(negedge clk);

        cfg_ct = 1'b0;                       // store-and-forward
        for (p = 0; p < 6; p = p + 1) begin
            len = 5 + (p * 3) % 8;
            send_packet(len);
        end
        wait_drain;
        repeat (10) @(negedge clk);

        cfg_ct = 1'b1;                       // cut-through
        repeat (10) @(negedge clk);
        for (p = 6; p < 12; p = p + 1) begin
            len = 4 + (p * 5) % 9;
            send_packet(len);
        end
        wait_drain;
        repeat (10) @(negedge clk);

        if (n_out != n_in)
            $display("smoke: %0d beats sent, %0d received", n_in, n_out);
        if (errors == 0 && n_out == n_in && drop_count == 16'd0)
            $display("SMOKE PASS: %0d packets, %0d beats", p, n_in);
        else
            $display("SMOKE FAIL: %0d mismatches", errors);
        $finish;
    end

endmodule
# pktbuf smoke test (board rev B SRAM model).
#   make            Icarus Verilog
#   make verilator  the same bench on Verilator, random power-up state
#   make clean
# Exits non-zero unless the bench prints SMOKE PASS.

SRC   = pktbuf.v pktbuf_egress.v
TB    = tb/tb_smoke.v
BUILD = build

.PHONY: all sim verilator clean

all: sim

sim: $(SRC) $(TB)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	@iverilog -g2012 -o $(BUILD)/smoke.vvp -s tb_smoke $(SRC) $(TB)
	@vvp -n $(BUILD)/smoke.vvp | tee $(BUILD)/smoke.log
	@grep -q "SMOKE PASS" $(BUILD)/smoke.log

verilator: $(SRC) $(TB)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	@verilator --binary --timing -Wno-fatal -Wno-lint -Wno-style --timescale 1ns/1ps \
		--x-initial unique --x-assign unique --top-module tb_smoke \
		-Mdir $(BUILD)/vl -o vsim $(SRC) $(TB) > $(BUILD)/verilator.log 2>&1 \
		|| (tail -20 $(BUILD)/verilator.log; exit 1)
	@$(BUILD)/vl/vsim +verilator+rand+reset+2 | tee $(BUILD)/smoke_vl.log
	@grep -q "SMOKE PASS" $(BUILD)/smoke_vl.log

clean:
	@rm -rf $(BUILD)

    localparam QW = 3;      // log2(QD)

    // Write shadow: the words written by the last two write commands. A
    // read issued within two cycles of the write of the same address would
    // not see the new data in the SRAM, so it is served from here.
    reg          ws1_v, ws2_v;
    reg [AW-1:0] ws1_a, ws2_a;
    reg [DW-1:0] ws1_d, ws2_d;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            ws1_v <= 1'b0;
            ws2_v <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            ws1_v <= wr_go;
            ws2_v <= ws1_v;
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wr_go) begin
            ws1_a <= wr_addr;
            ws1_d <= wr_data;
        end
        ws2_a <= ws1_a;
        ws2_d <= ws1_d;
    end

    wire hit1 = ws1_v && (ws1_a == rd_ptr[AW-1:0]);
    wire hit2 = ws2_v && (ws2_a == rd_ptr[AW-1:0]);
    wire hit  = hit1 || hit2;
    wire [DW-1:0] hit_data = hit1 ? ws1_d : ws2_d;

    // Output queue. A slot is allocated, in order, when a read is issued;
    // its data arrives later (SRAM) or at once (shadow).
    reg [DW-1:0] q_data [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_last [0:QD-1];
    reg          q_err  [0:QD-1];
    reg [QD-1:0] q_full;
    reg [QW:0]   q_wp;
    reg [QW:0]   q_rp;
    wire [QW:0]  q_used = q_wp - q_rp;

    // SRAM read pipeline (RL = 3): command on pins at p0, sampled by the
    // SRAM at the next edge, captured three edges after that (p3).
    reg          rd_p0, rd_p1, rd_p2, rd_p3;
    reg [QW-1:0] sl_p0, sl_p1, sl_p2, sl_p3;

    wire        q_pop    = out_valid && out_ready;
    wire        last_out = q_pop && out_last;
    assign pkt_retry   = last_out && out_retry && retry_en;
    assign pkt_release = last_out && !pkt_retry;

    wire can_issue = rd_avail && (q_used < QD);
    assign rd_want = can_issue && !hit;
    assign rd_take = can_issue && hit;
    wire alloc     = rd_go || rd_take;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            rd_ptr <= {(AW+1){1'b0}};
            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p2  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p3  <= 1'b0;
            q_wp   <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
            q_rp   <= {(QW+1){1'b0}};
            q_full <= {QD{1'b0}};

            rd_p0  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p1  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p2  <= 1'b0;
            rd_p3  <= 1'b0;
            q_rp   <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_wp   <= q_rp + 1'b1;
            q_full <= {QD{1'b0}};
        end else begin

                q_wp   <= q_wp + 1'b1;

            rd_p1 <= rd_p0;

            rd_p3 <= rd_p2;

                q_full[q_rp[QW-1:0]] <= 1'b0;

        end
    end

        sl_p2 <= sl_p1;
        sl_p3 <= sl_p2;

    assign out_data  = q_data[q_rp[QW-1:0]];
    assign out_last  = q_last[q_rp[QW-1:0]];
    assign out_err   = q_err[q_rp[QW-1:0]];

endmodule

module tb_rand;
    parameter DW = 32;
    parameter AW = 10;
    parameter SEED = 1;
    parameter CT = 0;
    parameter BP = 1;
    reg clk = 0; always #5 clk = ~clk;
    reg rst_n = 0, cfg_ct = CT;

    reg out_ready = 0, out_retry = 0;

    pktbuf #(.DW(DW), .AW(AW)) dut (.clk(clk), .rst_n(rst_n), .cfg_cut_through(cfg_ct),
        .in_valid(in_valid), .in_ready(in_ready), .in_data(in_data), .in_last(in_last), .in_err(in_err),
        .out_valid(out_valid), .out_ready(out_ready), .out_data(out_data), .out_last(out_last), .out_err(out_err),
        .out_retry(out_retry), .drop_count(drop_count), .sram_ce_n(sram_ce_n), .sram_we_n(sram_we_n),
        .sram_addr(sram_addr), .sram_wdata(sram_wdata), .sram_rdata(sram_rdata));
    reg [DW-1:0] mem [0:(1<<AW)-1];
    reg wpend; reg [AW-1:0] wpa; reg [DW-1:0] r1, r2; reg v1, v2;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (wpend) mem[wpa] <= sram_wdata;
        wpend <= (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b0);
        wpa <= sram_addr;
        v1 <= (sram_ce_n === 1'b0 && sram_we_n === 1'b1);
        r1 <= mem[sram_addr];
        v2 <= v1; r2 <= r1;
        sram_rdata <= v2 ? r2 : {DW{1'bx}};
    end
    // scoreboard
    reg [DW-1:0] ed [0:1<<20]; reg el [0:1<<20]; reg ee [0:1<<20];
    integer wi, ri, pstart, errors, seed, nb, npk, drops, pkt_in_start;
    integer cur_in_start; reg [DW-1:0] beat_d;

    initial begin wi = 0; ri = 0; pstart = 0; errors = 0; drops = 0; cur_in_start = 0; end

    always @(posedge clk) if (rst_n && in_valid && in_ready) begin
        ed[wi] = in_data; el[wi] = in_last; ee[wi] = CT ? (in_last & in_err) : 0;
        wi = wi + 1;
        if (in_last) begin
            if (!CT && in_err) begin wi = cur_in_start; drops = drops + 1; end
            cur_in_start = wi;
        end
    end
    always @(posedge clk) if (rst_n && out_valid && out_ready) begin
        if (ri >= wi || out_data !== ed[ri] || out_last !== el[ri] || out_err !== ee[ri]) begin

            errors = errors + 1;
        end
        ri = ri + 1;
        if (out_last) begin
            if (!CT && out_retry) ri = pstart;
            pstart = ri;
        end
    end
    integer cyc, b, len, i;
    initial begin
        seed = SEED;
        repeat (3) @(negedge clk); rst_n = 1;
        for (cyc = 0; cyc < 4000; cyc = cyc + 0) begin
            len = 1 + ($random(seed) & 255) % ((1<<AW) < 40 ? 40 : 70);
            if (!CT && len > (1<<AW)) len = 1<<AW;
            for (b = 0; b < len; b = b + 1) begin
                @(negedge clk);
                if (BP) while (($random(seed) & 3) == 0) begin in_valid = 0; @(negedge clk); end
                in_valid = 1; in_data = $random(seed); in_last = (b == len-1); in_err = ($random(seed) & 7) == 0;

                @(posedge clk); cyc = cyc + 1;
            end
            @(negedge clk); in_valid = 0; in_last = 0;

        for (i = 0; i < 20000 && ri != wi; i = i + 1) @(negedge clk);

        if (drop_count != (drops & 16'hffff)) begin $display("ERR drops %0d %0d", drop_count, drops); errors = errors+1; end
        if (errors == 0) $display("PASS DW%0d AW%0d CT%0d BP%0d beats %0d", DW, AW, CT, BP, wi);
        else $display("FAIL %0d", errors);

    end
    always @(negedge clk) begin

        out_retry = ($random(seed) & 3) == 0;
    end
    // idle check
    always @(posedge clk) if (rst_n && ri == wi && !in_valid && sram_ce_n === 0 && 0) ;
endmodule

    reg [DW-1:0] mem [0:(1<<AW)-1];

    always @(posedge clk) begin

        v2 <= v1; r2 <= r1; sram_rdata <= v2 ? r2 : {DW{1'bx}};
    end
    integer tc=0, tin=0, tfirst=0, gap=0, nout=0, lastout=0, len, b, p;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        tc = tc + 1;
        if (in_valid && in_ready && (cfg_ct ? b==0 : in_last)) tin = tc;
        if (out_valid && out_ready) begin
            if (nout == 0) $display("ct=%0d len=%0d latency %0d", cfg_ct, len, tc - tin);
            else if (tc != lastout + 1) $display("  GAP at beat %0d", nout);
            lastout = tc; nout = nout + 1;
        end
    end
    always @(posedge clk) if (rst_n && sram_ce_n===1'b1 && in_ready !== 1'b1 && tc > 6 && tc < 9) $display("in_ready late");
    initial begin
        repeat (3) @(negedge clk); rst_n = 1;
        repeat (4) @(negedge clk); if (in_ready !== 1) $display("ERR in_ready not high 4 after reset");
        for (p = 0; p < 2; p = p + 1) begin
          cfg_ct = p; repeat (10) @(negedge clk);
          foreach_len: for (len = 1; len <= 32; len = len + (len < 4 ? 1 : 7)) begin
            nout = 0;
            for (b = 0; b < len; b = b + 1) begin
                @(negedge clk); in_valid = 1; in_data = b; in_last = (b == len-1);
                #1; if (!in_ready) $display("ERR not accepted");
                @(posedge clk);
            end
            @(negedge clk); in_valid = 0; in_last = 0; b = 0;
            repeat (60) @(negedge clk);
            if (nout != len) $display("ERR count %0d", nout);
            if (sram_ce_n !== 1) $display("ERR sram busy when idle");

Without this, cut-through would either break the 5-cycle first-beat limit or return stale data.
- **Read path in `pktbuf_egress.v`:** the read pipeline is now 3 cycles deep. The output queue grew from 4 to 8 entries, so egress keeps one beat per cycle with no gaps despite the longer latency. A retry still discards everything read ahead and restarts the packet.
- **Unchanged:** the top-level `pktbuf` name, ports and parameters, and the way ingress and egress take turns on the SRAM.

**Testing:**
- **Random traffic:** random packet lengths, `in_err`, retries and backpressure, in both modes and with and without backpressure. I ran it at `DW`/`AW` of 32/10, 8/6, 16/12, 13/7, 32/6, 8/12, 8/8 and 20/9. Every run matched the expected beats, `out_err` and `drop_count`, and drained.
- **Timing:**
  - Store-and-forward, empty block, packets up to 32 beats: the first egress beat moves 6 cycles after the last ingress beat (limit now 10), with no gaps after it.
  - Cut-through: the first beat moves 2 cycles after it is taken (limit 5).
  - `in_ready` is high 4 cycles after reset, and no SRAM command is issued once the block is empty.
- **Rules:** Verilator `-Wall` lint is clean, and the files use none of the banned constructs.

I also changed the smoke test in `tb/` to model the rev C SRAM; it passes on both simulators.
